25649.name: Symbol
25649.docs: Greek letters and mathematical symbols, in the font's own encoding.

15404.name: drive
15404.docs:
Applies `f` to scalar argument values. When any argument at a `drivers` position is an
array, `f` runs per element over the broadcast shape of all arguments; otherwise it receives
the arguments whole (so the chosen value may itself be an array).

1308.name: precision
1308.docs:
"Set precision as displayed" (File › Options › Advanced; `fullPrecision="0"` in `.xlsx`,
CalcPrecision in `.xls`): with it on, a number is stored as its cell's number format shows it,
and formulas read those rounded values. The rounding itself is the number format crate's
([`crate::numfmt::NumberFormat::round_as_displayed`]); this module looks up each cell's
format, parsing every style's code once.

16712.name: layout
16712.docs: Lays `latex` out. Errors carry the offending span when RaTeX reports one.

24414.name: check_sheet_name
24414.docs:
Validates a sheet name like Excel: 1–31 chars, none of `: \ / ? * [ ]`, not starting or
ending with `'`, unique (case-insensitive) unless it is `except`'s own name.

29573.name: write
29573.docs: Writing a workbook as an XLSX package.

16785.name: array
16785.docs:
Legacy array formula (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) covering this range; the formula lives in the
top-left cell.

292.name: quote_sheet
292.docs: A sheet name as it is written in a reference: quoted, with `'` doubled, when Excel quotes it.

4143.name: run_script
4143.docs:
Runs a stored script. Scripts in a workbook opened from a file run only once the workbook is
trusted for this session (`automate.trustScripts`, or `trusted: true` on this call); steps that
reach outside the workbook ([`denied_script_step`]) are refused before any step runs.

25941.name: circle
25941.docs: A circle approximated by four cubic Béziers.

10610.name: value
10610.docs: Value at (row, col) relative to the top-left.

27322.name: unwrap_google_sheets
27322.docs:
The model text of `text` (a formula as read, see [`from_file`]) with its Google Sheets export
wrappers replaced (see [`crate::xlsx::read_xlsx_with`]), or `None` when nothing changes.

31173.name: write_xlsx
31173.docs: Writes a workbook as an `.xlsx` package, or as an `.xlsm` one when it holds a VBA project.

22309.name: take_cells
22309.docs: Removes content in a range; returns scalar cells, with pictures removed from the side map.

4362.name: series_from_range
4362.docs: Builds series from a block: first row/column as names/categories when they're text.

30011.name: function_name
30011.docs: Strips the prefixes newer functions carry in files (`_xlfn.IFERROR`).

13372.name: parse_input
13372.docs:
Parses UI input using the selected function table and separators. Existing names and
LET/LAMBDA bindings take precedence over aliases. File and API syntax uses [`crate::formula::parse`].

4435.name: check_record_params
4435.docs:
Refuses parameters `macro.record` would ignore (`null` counts as not given): `relative` and
`shortcut` when stopping (they are chosen when recording starts), `stop: false` while
recording (the call stops it), anything beside `cancel: true`, and parameters of the wrong
kind. `name` and `description` count when starting and when stopping (stopping wins).

730.name: scalar
730.docs: Top-left element of an array, the value itself otherwise.

27687.name: package
27687.docs:
OPC package access: reading zip parts with decompression limits, relationships and part-name
resolution; writing a zip package deterministically.

14899.name: last
14899.docs: Position of the last time stamp.

9813.name: col_at
9813.docs: Column under `x`, clamped to the page's columns (margins and gaps hit the nearest one).

25217.name: GENERAL_WIDTH
25217.docs: Width (in characters) of General output in a cell.

12429.name: with_target
12429.docs:
Runs `f` with the target window active, then brings back the window that was active, so a
script acting on another window doesn't change what the user is looking at. When `f`
itself switched windows (`window.activate`, `file.new`, a close), its choice stands.

13737.name: parse_struct
13737.docs:
Parses the inside of `Table[...]`. Text between the bracketed items may only be the `,` and
`:` separators, except one unbracketed column after `[#This Row],` (`[[#This Row],Units]`,
how some writers spell `[@Units]`); anything else is an error rather than dropped.

7343.name: target_ranges
7343.docs:
A range parameter (`"A1:B2"`, `"Sheet2!A1"`, `"B:B"`), defaulting to the current selection's
areas.

12502.name: shift_relative_wrapping
12502.docs:
Defined names: relative parts move by `(dr, dc)`, wrapping around the sheet's edges. Files
store a name's relative references as seen from A1 (a name for "the cell to the left" defined
in B1 is `Sheet1!XFD1`), and a use in another cell moves them by that cell's offset from A1.

17661.name: has_header_footer
17661.docs: Any header or footer text at all (on any kind of page).

11267.name: bytes
11267.docs: The size of `steps` and `ran` serialized as JSON.

29287.name: note_anchor
29287.docs:
A note box's `<x:Anchor>` text and its width and height in points: the box read from the file
or [`DEFAULT_NOTE_BOX`], its corners moved with the note's `cell` and kept on the sheet.

11340.name: a1
11340.docs: The A1 text of all areas (`A1:B2,D4`).

4946.name: push_field
4946.docs: Appends `s` unless the section would pass [`MAX_SECTION_BYTES`]; what doesn't fit is left out.

26744.name: package_parts
26744.docs:
The plaintext size an `EncryptedPackage` states, and the ciphertext after it. A size larger
than the ciphertext is damage, so it never drives an allocation.

16499.name: width
16499.docs:
The glyph's box (TeX metrics), already scaled by `size`: advance, height above and depth
below the baseline. A painter without the glyph draws a `[?]` box this size.

1168.name: aggregate
1168.docs:
Performs aggregation operations without copying its ranges: blocks are folded over the stored
cells, so no array is built and there is no `MAX_CELLS` limit. Arguments are evaluated and read one
after another, as the array path does, so volatile formulas (like `RAND`) see the same order.
Only `SUM`, `COUNT` and `AVG` are supported currently.

3784.name: MAX_TEXT
3784.docs: The longest caption or name a control takes.

15337.name: OddLastArgs
15337.docs:
settlement, maturity, last_interest, rate, yld/pr, redemption, frequency, [basis].
`((dc, acc, dsc), rate, yield-or-price, redemption, frequency)` of an odd-last-period call.

5092.name: empty_for_overflow
5092.docs: Is a cell free for text to overflow into?

25655.name: family_for
25655.docs:
Picks a standard family for a font name: serif faces map to Times, monospaced ones to
Courier, everything else to Helvetica.

24420.name: next_object_id
24420.docs:
A free id for a new chart, picture, shape, table, slicer or form control: one more than the largest in
use, or, when that is `u32::MAX` (a file can carry any id), the lowest free one.

21877.name: preserved
21877.docs:
File content GridCraft does not model, carried through unchanged so that saving a workbook
never silently drops it (XLSX pass-through: custom XML, external links, connections, query
tables, form controls, OLE objects…).

The data is opaque to everything except the file-format crate: the model only holds it, so a
sheet's kept content disappears with the sheet. It is not part of the JSON format.

3930.name: draw
3930.docs: Draw tab: pen and eraser tools, ink strokes, Ink to Shape.

19334.name: smooth
19334.docs: Draw line segments as a smoothed (spline) curve.

16791.name: expr_arc
16791.docs: The parsed expression without copying it (re-parses after deserialization).

6546.name: report
6546.docs: `data.solverReport`: reports for a solution of the sheet's saved model.

29725.name: DEFAULT_BOOK_NAME
29725.docs: Workbook name written in a PivotChart's link when the file name isn't known.

298.name: outer
298.docs:
Outer levels beyond the innermost labels (the column or row nearest the values): 1 for a
two-level axis. At most 3 are kept.

4149.name: set_view
4149.docs:
Switches a sheet's view. Like zoom, the view is saved with the file but is not an edit: it
neither records an undo step nor marks a clean workbook as changed.

29871.name: Xti
29871.docs: XTI ([MS-XLS] 2.5.344): a supporting link and a range of its sheets.

31179.name: parse_values
31179.docs: Interpret fields like typed input (numbers, dates, booleans…); otherwise keep text.

13232.name: Name
13232.docs: Defined name, table name or LET/LAMBDA parameter.

2987.name: bar
2987.docs: Data bar: fraction 0..=1 of the cell width, colour, gradient.

6838.name: needs_escape
6838.docs: Whether `c` is stored escaped: XML can't carry it, or it is the marker.

11997.name: receive
11997.docs:
The trust of a document after it receives content from a document with trust `source`:
content from an untrusted file leaves the receiver untrusted.

4368.name: build_chart
4368.docs:
The chart `insert.chart` would insert for these params, without inserting it: the sheet it
goes on and the chart (previews in the Recommended Charts dialog).

30017.name: decode
30017.docs:
Decodes `rgce` (tokens) with `rgcb` (the extra data for array constants) evaluated at
`base`. Returns the expression or why it can't be represented.

13378.name: Bindings
13378.docs:
The LET/LAMBDA names in scope, with how many times each is bound, so a lookup is one probe
instead of a scan of every binding for each call.

4441.name: macros
4441.docs:
GridCraft macros: typed, declarative command lists, not VBA. The model is plain data in
`crate::model::Macro`; this module reads and writes it and keeps it within its limits.

Storage: the JSON format keeps `Workbook::macros` as a field. In xlsx each macro is one item of
GridCraft's hidden workbook data ([`crate::engine::cmd::stash`]), `_gc_macro_<n>_<k>`, written when the
file is saved and taken back out of the names when it is opened, so the names never linger in
the open document. Scripts made with Automate › New Script or Record Actions are a separate,
older feature with their own storage; macros neither read nor change it. A recording keeps the
steps a script run ran while it recorded, as the run reported them.

1898.name: fill
1898.docs: Fills a multi-contour path with the even-odd rule.

30163.name: MAX_STYLE_NAME
30163.docs: Characters kept from a style name (Excel allows 255).

10981.name: Look
10981.docs:
Colours for a PivotTable style name (our own palette, keyed by the familiar
`PivotStyleLight1…28 / Medium1…28 / Dark1…28` names).

736.name: rank
736.docs: Type rank for comparison and sorting: numbers < text < booleans < errors; empty sorts last.

27693.name: read
27693.docs: Reads a part's bytes; `Ok(None)` when it doesn't exist.

17448.name: source
17448.docs: Source: range formula text (`Sheet1!$A$1:$E$200`), a table name or a defined name.

9819.name: is_data_page
9819.docs: Page `(i, j)` holds printed data (others are "Click to add data" pages).

13670.name: MAX_FORMULA_LEN
13670.docs:
Longest formula accepted, in characters: Excel's limit for formula contents. It also bounds
the depth of the trees long operator chains build (`1+1+…`), which dropping and evaluating
walk recursively; without it a formula of a few hundred kilobytes in a file overflows the stack.

27839.name: keep
27839.docs: Keeps a set of relationships (all or nothing) and the parts behind them.

25296.name: FormatKind
25296.docs: Best guess at the ribbon's number-format category.

11200.name: known
11200.docs: Whether `name` (upper case, without `_xlfn.`) is a function of the catalog.

955.name: resized_sum_range
955.docs:
The range SUMIF/AVERAGEIF add up: from the sum range's top-left cell, as many rows and columns
as the criteria range (`height` × `width`), cut off at the sheet's edge.

7422.name: cell_text
7422.docs: The text a cell shows (full precision General; the grid narrows General to fit the column).

11273.name: cut_back
11273.docs:
Takes back the steps recorded in the document with uid `doc` since `mark` (an undo group
on it was rolled back, so playing them back would make edits it no longer has). Steps in
other documents stay: their edits do too. Steps the buffer dropped stay counted.
What a step ran ([`Recorder::ran`]) goes with its step, and stays with a kept one under its
new index. A mark from another recording (the recording started again inside the group)
means every step of this one came after it.

29293.name: solid_bar_id
29293.docs: The id linking a solid data bar's `cfRule` to its x14 extension; unique per sheet because priorities are.

4952.name: known_paper
4952.docs:
Paper sizes in points, portrait. `B4`/`B5`/`B6` are the **JIS** sizes Japanese Excel and its
e-mail attachments use (257×364, 182×257 and 128×182 mm); the ISO B series stays reachable as
`B4 (ISO)`/`B5 (ISO)`/`B6 (ISO)`. The Japanese postcards and envelopes are the JIS ones too.

26823.name: decrypt_cbc
26823.docs: CBC: each block XORed with the previous ciphertext block (the IV for the first).

7641.name: value
7641.docs: The value `k` steps beyond the source (forward) or before it (backward).

12.name: parse
12.docs: Parses `A1`, `$A$1`, `xfd1048576` (case-insensitive). `None` if malformed or out of range.

29512.name: BUILTIN_FORMATS
29512.docs:
Built-in number format codes (en-US) by id. Ids not listed (23–36 are East Asian
locale formats) read as General.

5171.name: output
5171.docs:
`python.output`: the cell's return type. The code stays; a cached result belongs to the old
return type, so it goes, as with `python.set` and a new return type: the cell shows
`#BLOCKED!` until it runs, and its old spill goes with its readers recalculated.

27042.name: is_ordinal_after_digit
27042.docs:
`º` and `ª` after a digit (`1º`, `2ª`) are Western ordinals, though Windows-1256 reads the bytes
as `؛` and `ھ`; either way they are no evidence.

1466.name: settle
1466.docs: Merges pending insertions and drops dead entries when there are enough of them.

27115.name: DateEvidence
27115.docs: The evidence a column's sample gives for its date order.

28423.name: kinds
28423.docs: Kinds for `containsMixedTypes`: strings (text, booleans, errors) and numbers.

4082.name: equation
4082.docs:
Equations (Insert › Symbols › Equation): floating shapes holding LaTeX source, laid out by
`gridcraft-math` and drawn from the cached layout.

An equation is drawn to fit its frame, so resizing the frame scales it. Inserting sizes the
frame for the requested font size; editing keeps the current scale and resizes the frame to
the new content.

11857.name: recorded
11857.docs:
Where the recording was when the group began (`None` when nothing was recording): a
rollback takes back the steps recorded since, as it takes back their edits.

4301.name: points_to_chars
4301.docs:
Column width (points) → characters of the default font's digit width (7 px), without the
cell padding: the value the Column Width dialog shows.

8152.name: HTML_EXPORT_MAX_CELLS
8152.docs: Rows × columns of one web-page table. Save as Web Page writes every kept row's full used column span into one growing String, so a sparse sheet with a lone far-right cell (or a tall, wide one) would otherwise be gigabytes of `` before finishing (#2387).

14619.name: INIT_POINTS
14619.docs: Seasonally adjusted values the initial level and trend are fitted to.

4374.name: series_block
4374.docs:
The block a chart's series come from, and whether each series is a row of it: the bounding
range of the series names, categories and values, when they're all references to one sheet.

30023.name: records
30023.docs:
BIFF8 record framing ([MS-XLS] 2.1.4) and the string structures ([MS-XLS] 2.5.240,
2.5.293, 2.5.294) that may continue across `Continue` records.

9533.name: WindowState
9533.docs: One window on an open workbook.

4447.name: Source
4447.docs: The source list: header names, per-column number formats and the records.

26245.name: open
26245.docs: Parses the header, FAT, mini FAT and directory. Errors on anything that can't be followed.

3285.name: clip_html
3285.docs:
Reading the HTML flavour of the system clipboard on paste.

Spreadsheets put an HTML table on the clipboard next to the tab-separated text. The text holds
what each cell *shows* ("Rp10,000.00"), which en-US input parsing can't always turn back into a
number. The HTML of the common sources also carries the underlying number as a cell attribute:
`x:num="10000"` (Excel, Excel for the web) and `sdval="10000"` (LibreOffice Calc). Paste uses
it to keep such cells numeric (#257). Only the table structure, the cell text and these two
attributes are read; everything else in the markup is ignored.

28934.name: cf_ext_ids
28934.docs: x14 conditional-format ids of the current sheet's data bars, with the index of the rule in `cond_formats`.

13603.name: starts_range_end
13603.docs: Whether `c` can start the second end of a range after `:.` (`A1:.E10`, `A:.$C`, `1:.5`).

25156.name: render_number
25156.docs: Renders a non-negative number through a number section.

30315.name: border_style
30315.docs: A border line style from its BIFF8 code (dgLeft and the like); unknown codes are no border.

3431.name: ENTITY_WINDOW
3431.docs:
Entities are at most `&` + 8 chars + `;` (a decimal code point at most 7 digits deep), so
the semicolon is only looked for in the first 12 bytes — and `unwrap_or(rest)` never falls
back to scanning the remainder of the text either (that turn re-scans per `&`, quadratic
when a paste holds many bare `&`).

25229.name: rgb
25229.docs: RGB value used to render this number-format color.

888.name: Acc
888.docs: What a folded aggregate carries from one value to the next.

3504.name: single
3504.docs: One variable from a single row or column (`range1`/`range2` of the two-sample tests).

7355.name: protection_checked
7355.docs:
The command applied sheet protection itself (row/column inserts and deletes the
protection allows), so cells it shifts aren't refused as edits of locked cells.

11206.name: execute
11206.docs:
Runs a command by id. Undoable commands record a history step when the workbook changed,
unless an undo group is open on the document (the group then makes the step).
Panics inside commands are caught and reported; the workbook is restored.

15057.name: forecast
15057.docs: Point forecast `h` steps after the last point (fractional steps interpolate).

2342.name: supports_trendline
2342.docs:
Whether series drawn as `k` show trendlines (Excel offers them on 2-D unstacked column,
bar, line, area, scatter and bubble charts).

27991.name: rebase_links
27991.docs:
`wb` as it is saved into the folder `to` (absolute): the relative paths of its linked
workbooks, relative to the folder it was read from, are rewritten relative to `to`, as Excel
does on Save As, or made absolute when no relative path exists (another drive). `None` when
nothing changes.

21597.name: id
21597.docs: The id in the source file (`rId7`). Ids of an owner GridCraft writes are reassigned on save.

25448.name: MAX_FORMAT_CODE_CHARS
25448.docs:
Longest number format code, in characters (not bytes), that is parsed: Excel's own limit.
A longer code is invalid: [`NumberFormat::parse`] returns a General format (the cell shows
its value unformatted; the stored code is kept as is) and `TEXT` returns `#VALUE!`. The cap
also bounds every allocation that scales with the number of placeholders in a code.

22905.name: charset
22905.docs: Windows character set the font was chosen for (178 = Arabic); kept so Excel substitutes a font for the same script.

4958.name: margins
4958.docs: Left, right, top, bottom, header, footer margins in points.

25521.name: pdf
25521.docs:
A tiny, self-contained PDF 1.7 writer for GridCraft's print and PDF export.

- The 14 standard fonts (no embedding) with WinAnsiEncoding, plus approximate width tables
  ([`text_width`]) so callers can measure, align and wrap text. Characters outside
  WinAnsiEncoding (CJK and other scripts) are set in a predefined, non-embedded Adobe-GB1 CID
  font with the `UniGB-UTF16-H` CMap instead of being replaced by `?`. Symbol uses its own
  built-in encoding ([`symbol_code`]), for Greek letters and mathematical operators.
- Vector drawing: rectangles, lines (solid or dashed), polygons, circles (Bézier), clipping.
- RGBA images as RGB image XObjects with a soft mask for alpha (run-length encoded).
- Coordinates are points with a **top-left origin** (y grows down); text `y` is the baseline.

Streams are written uncompressed (images use the trivial RunLengthDecode filter) so the crate
needs no dependencies.

8882.name: resolve_params
8882.docs: Step parameters with every token replaced by A1 text.

29445.name: bool_prop
29445.docs: `<b/>`-style boolean property elements: present means true unless `val` says otherwise.

15422.name: reject_multi_cell_refs
15422.docs:
A reference to more than one cell at a value parameter becomes a scalar `#VALUE!`, so it adds
no shape: `EOMONTH(A1:A3, {1;2})` is a 2x1 array of `#VALUE!`, as in Excel.

5177.name: convert_notes
5177.docs:
Review › Notes › Convert to Comments: every note in the workbook becomes a threaded comment
with the same author and text.

21889.name: result_value
21889.docs:
What the cell shows for its result: cell values (an array spills from the cell), or, for a
Python object, its type name. `None` before the code has run.

3942.name: parse_typed_formula
3942.docs:
Parses a formula as it is typed (without the `=`). Excel closes missing parentheses for you,
and refuses a formula that still doesn't parse.

27048.name: DATE_SAMPLE_ROWS
27048.docs: How many rows and bytes of a text file are read to decide each column's date order.

20654.name: Icon
20654.docs:
Rows whose cell shows icon `id` (0-based; `None` = no icon) of conditional-format icon set
`set` (`iconFilter`). Kept from files; re-applying the filter leaves those rows as they are.

18111.name: xml
18111.docs:
Binding to an element of an XML map. It moves with the column and goes when the column is
deleted; inserted columns are unmapped.

1472.name: walk_untaken
1472.docs: Returns whether everything under `node` has now been reported (or is dead).

4088.name: MathError
4088.docs: Why an equation could not be laid out.

29737.name: Unsupported
29737.docs: Why a formula could not be turned back into text.

5396.name: repair
5396.docs: Clamps into the box and rounds integer variables.

31118.name: is_macro_enabled
31118.docs: Whether this kind may carry a VBA project (`.xlsm`, `.xltm`).

9393.name: pair_sheets
9393.docs:
Each sheet of `before` with its index in `after` (`None` when deleted), and the sheets of
`after` that are new. Sheets are matched by name; what's left is matched in order (a renamed
sheet).

22254.name: spill
22254.docs: Values spilled by dynamic-array formulas (maintained by calc), keyed by cell.

4307.name: blank
4307.docs: Whether a cell on the active sheet is empty.

9466.name: bounds
9466.docs: The block that holds every written cell.

6923.name: split_op
6923.docs: Splits `">=10"` into (`">="`, `"10"`); text without an operator means "begins with".

4380.name: SHAPE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS
4380.docs: A text box holds at most as many characters as a cell.

26178.name: xlsx
26178.docs:
GridCraft file formats: XLSX (transitional and strict) and CSV import/export, plus XLSB and ODS data import
and legacy Excel 97-2003 `.xls` (BIFF8) import, and password-encrypted workbooks (Agile and Standard encryption).

Clean-room implementation from ECMA-376 / ISO/IEC 29500 and observed behaviour. All entry
points work on byte slices (no file system access), so the crate builds for WebAssembly.

Reading is lenient: unsupported or broken optional parts are skipped and reported in
[`ReadReport::warnings`]; only a missing/invalid package or workbook part is an error. Hostile
input is bounded: decompressed parts are capped at 512 MB (1 GB per package), cells outside
Excel's grid are dropped and XML nesting is limited.

9539.name: take
9539.docs: Takes the state and stops journaling until [`Saved::restore`].

28940.name: keep_phonetics
28940.docs:
Stores the phonetic data read from `xl/sharedStrings.xml`.

One entry per base text: the writer rebuilds the shared string table from the values the
sheets use and holds each text once (the format's `uniqueCount`), so only one reading can be
written per text. A later `<si>` with a text that is already there is dropped — with a
warning when its data differs, so nothing is lost silently.

30321.name: build
30321.docs:
Imports the formatting: sets the workbook's default (Normal) font and named cell styles, and
returns the model style of every XF in file order.

12374.name: windows
12374.docs: Windows on the open workbooks ([`windows`]); every workbook has at least one.

3437.name: MAX_INPUT_CELLS
3437.docs: Most input cells a tool reads.

4745.name: checkbox_state
4745.docs:
A checkbox cell prints TRUE/FALSE (and empty) as a box, as on screen (#2972); other values
print as text.

12447.name: push_journal
12447.docs:
Journals a command, then trims the oldest entries past either cap. A recording in progress
keeps pointing at the same entry (the steps the trim dropped are lost).

20149.name: locked
20149.docs: Locked when the sheet is protected.

11212.name: sheet
11212.docs: That document's active sheet (index and name) just before the command ran.

22765.name: default
22765.docs:
GridCraft's own default theme ("Craft"): original palette. The East Asian and
complex-script typefaces stay empty: the file did not set one.

26616.name: is_note_data
26616.docs:
Whether a VML shape's client data is a note's: its `ObjectType` is `Note` in any case and with
spaces around it. Only that attribute counts, not text elsewhere in the shape (a caption).

27924.name: with_decls
27924.docs: Adds the root's namespace declarations a fragment doesn't declare itself.

4891.name: codes_to_fields
4891.docs: A raw section as the user edits it: `&P` shows as `&[Page]`, `&N` as `&[Pages]`, and so on.

2348.name: clip_segment
2348.docs:
Liang–Barsky: the part of segment `a`–`b` inside the unit square, with whether the start and
end were cut.

13901.name: parse_arg
13901.docs:
Parses the criteria argument of COUNTIF, SUMIF, AVERAGEIF and the single-pair *IFS
functions: like `parse`, but text longer than 255 UTF-16 code units is `#VALUE!`, as in
Excel (checked on Excel 2016 and Microsoft 365: `"a"×254 & "😀"` is 255 characters but
256 units, and is `#VALUE!`).

2421.name: render
2421.docs: Lays out and draws a chart into a `w`×`h` box at the origin. Empty for a degenerate box.

3729.name: opt_num
3729.docs:
A number parameter: `None` when absent, null or blank; an error when present but not a
finite number (a typed "0,3" or "abc" must not quietly become the default).

8888.name: resolve_ref
8888.docs: Resolves a token, or a plain reference (`B2`, `Sheet2!A1:C3`, a defined name).

3802.name: check_objects_unlocked
3802.docs:
Drawing objects on a protected sheet can't be changed while they are locked.
For the object commands (`object.move`, `object.delete`, `object.setAnchorMode`, `arrange.*`,
`arrange.align`): refuses to change form controls `ids` on `sheet` when one is locked and the
sheet is protected, as `control.format` and `control.assign` do. Other kinds pass.

29451.name: read_fill
29451.docs:
A `<fill>`. In differential formats a solid fill's colour is the *background* colour and the
pattern type may be omitted.

15355.name: newton
15355.docs: Newton iteration with a numeric derivative, keeping the rate above -1.

21822.name: sheets
21822.docs: Chart sheets, in file order (workbook owner only).

29524.name: pt_to_px
29524.docs: Row height in typographic points → model px.

15428.name: needle
15428.docs: Lookup needle: the scalar to look for. Blank looks for 0; errors propagate.

5183.name: EditRange
5183.docs:
Review › Allow Edit Ranges: cells that stay editable on a protected sheet, with or without a
password (XLSX `<protectedRange>`).

15501.name: round_dir
15501.docs: Rounds |x| scaled by 10^digits with `op` (ceil / floor), keeping sign.

27054.name: Conflict
27054.docs: Values read only day first and values read only month first: the dates stay text.

30905.name: MAX_DEPTH
30905.docs: Maximum element nesting accepted in any part.

4021.name: numeric_from_html
4021.docs:
A pasted cell that came out as text ("Rp10,000.00" isn't en-US input) becomes the number the
source recorded for it in its HTML, with a format that shows the same text when one can be
inferred and the cell has none. The HTML cell must show the same text as the tab-separated
field, so HTML that belongs to another copy (or a table laid out differently) changes nothing.

30978.name: parse
30978.docs: Parses a whole part into a tree.

24584.name: DEFAULT_FONT
24584.docs:
Font used for new workbooks. Only a name: renderers substitute an available open font
(e.g. the metric-compatible Carlito) when it isn't installed.

4094.name: Face
4094.docs: The typeface a glyph asks for. Painters map it onto the fonts they have.

8018.name: PASSWORD_REQUIRED
8018.docs:
The error for an encrypted workbook opened without a password contains this. The interface
asks for the password when it sees it; programmatic callers pass `password` instead.

const.expr: "is password-protected. Enter its password to open it."

1624.name: MAX_ITERATION_WORK
1624.docs:
Formula evaluations iterative calculation may spend on one recalculation (passes × formulas
evaluated again), however high Maximum Iterations is.

6783.name: get
6783.docs: The item text stored under `key`, or `None` when there is none (or it is over the size limit).

26038.name: finish
26038.docs: Serializes the document. A document without pages gets one blank Letter page.

9399.name: rolls_back
9399.docs: The Stop step that ended the dry run asks for the run to be rolled back.

14558.name: resolve
14558.docs: Resolves a unit name to (unit, prefix multiplier). Exact names win over prefixed ones.

4313.name: guessed_range
4313.docs: The range a single cell's AutoSum guesses: the numbers above it, else the numbers to its left.

1770.name: now_serial
1770.docs:
Current date-time as a serial (1900 system), from the system clock (browser clock on wasm).
UTC; the local offset isn't available without platform calls. Falls back to a fixed date only
when no clock is available.

4386.name: size_cap
4386.docs:
The most a command may make a dimension that is `current` now: [`MAX_OBJECT_SIZE`], or the
current size when a file made the object larger (the XLSX reader accepts anchors far past the
limit). Such an object keeps its size when it is moved and shrinks by what a resize asks, but
it never grows further, so hostile input is still capped. Never NaN: `f64::max` drops one.

1843.name: axis
1843.docs: Value-axis scaling ("nice numbers") and label formatting.

4459.name: options
4459.docs:
PivotTable Options: Enable show details (Data). Changes only the option; the report is not
refreshed. Without params it returns the current setting.

14850.name: step
14850.docs: The timeline's step in timeline units (the average step for calendar months).

7221.name: shortcut_for_platform
7221.docs: Format the portable shortcut notation for the runtime operating system.

18774.name: Comment
18774.docs: A note (classic comment) or a threaded comment.

3443.name: MAX_RANDOM
3443.docs: Most numbers Random Number Generation or Sampling writes in one run.

12453.name: stop_recording
12453.docs: Stops recording and returns what was recorded (`None` when nothing was recording).

26622.name: crypto
26622.docs:
Password-encrypted workbooks. Excel wraps the ordinary OOXML package in a compound file with
two streams: `EncryptionInfo` (how the key comes from the password, and a verifier that tells
a wrong password) and `EncryptedPackage` (the package, encrypted with AES). Agile encryption
(Excel 2010 onward) and Standard encryption (Excel 2007) are read; RC4, Extensible and
certificate-only encryption are reported as unsupported.

Clean-room from Microsoft's public [MS-OFFCRYPTO] specification. Every read is
bounds-checked, and the costly inputs (spin count, stated sizes) are capped.

27930.name: passthrough
27930.docs:
Pass-through of package content GridCraft does not model, so that open → edit → save keeps it.

On read, the raw bytes of unmodelled parts are kept with their content type and their
relationship graph, per owner: the package root (custom document properties, ribbon
customisation, add-in task panes), the workbook (custom XML, links to external workbooks with
their `<externalReferences>`, data connections, XML maps) and each sheet (query tables, cells
mapped to XML elements, form controls other than the buttons, scroll bars and spin buttons
`controls.rs` models, ActiveX controls, OLE objects, the sheet background and printer settings, with the sheet's `<picture>`, `<oleObjects>` and `<controls>` XML, the `r:id`
of `<pageSetup>`, the legacy VML shapes those controls need and the pictures of the headers and
footers, `&G`, with their `<legacyDrawingHF>`). The workbook also keeps its
`<fileVersion>` and the calcFeatures extension, which Excel needs to trust the saved values.

On write, kept parts get fresh part names where needed and new relationship ids; the `r:id`s in
kept XML are rewritten to match. Kept content is conservative:
- Anything whose relationship graph reaches a part GridCraft reads and rewrites (worksheets,
  drawings, charts, tables, PivotTables, comments, slicers…) is not kept: it would point at
  content that no longer exists in the same form.
- External relationship targets (the path of a linked workbook) are kept as text and never
  opened, followed or refreshed. A relative path to a linked workbook is rewritten when the
  workbook is saved into another folder ([`rebase_links`]), so it still names the same file.
- Sheet content lives on the sheet: deleting the sheet drops it, Copy Sheet doesn't copy it.
  Cell references inside kept parts (a control's linked cell, a query table's range, a cell
  mapped to an XML element) are kept as they were, not adjusted to inserted or deleted rows.
- Strict Open XML files are not passed through (their namespaces differ from what we write).
- Sizes are bounded: per part and per workbook.

21536.name: new_sha512
21536.docs: A SHA-512 hash with Excel's default spin count, for a new password.

4897.name: HfSection
4897.docs: One header/footer section: its text and whether `&B` made it bold.

6205.name: split_constraint
6205.docs:
Splits `"B5 <= 10"` / `"B2 int"` into (lhs, relation, rhs). A relation's characters inside
a quoted sheet name (`'A<=B'!$C$1 <= 5`) are part of the name.

3662.name: forecast_grid
3662.docs:
Writes the forecasts (and with `standardErrors` the standard errors over `se_window`
points) down two columns.

25460.name: select
25460.docs:
Picks the number section for `v`. Returns the section and whether the minus sign is
dropped (the default negative section shows the absolute value). `None` = General.

15288.name: span
15288.docs: Days of `[from, to]` under a basis, or 0 when the span is empty.

8894.name: count_arg
8894.docs: The count `below(n)` and `right(n)` take: 1 when left out, and never less than 1.

3808.name: button_policy
3808.docs: The macro policy for a button's command, with the button's own refusals first.

11510.name: id
11510.docs: Identifies the window for the rest of the session; never reused.

28222.name: sheet_names_in
28222.docs:
The sheet names a formula such as `'My Sheet'!$A$1:$A$9,Data!$B$1` refers to. References to
other workbooks (`[1]Sheet!A1`) are not sheets of this one and are left out.

15434.name: binary_order
15434.docs:
Order of an entry relative to the needle for XLOOKUP / XMATCH binary search (search mode ±2):
Excel's sort order over all types (numbers < text < logicals < errors), reversed for
descending data, with blanks always last like a sort leaves them. Unlike the legacy
approximate match no entry is skipped (observed: `XLOOKUP(46523, {9700;"xyz";"xyz";160726;
204100;510300}, …, 0, 1, 2)` returns the row of the first "xyz").

5189.name: sheet
5189.docs: Worksheets and structure: insert/delete rows, columns and cells; sheet tabs.

12891.name: table
12891.docs: Empty for `[@Col]` inside the table itself.

29676.name: persons
29676.docs: Authors of threaded comments, in first-use order; written to `xl/persons/person.xml`.

5335.name: solver
5335.docs:
Solver (Data › Analysis › Solver): finds values for variable cells that maximise, minimise
or hit a value in an objective cell, subject to constraints.

The workbook is the model: every evaluation sets the variable cells on a copy of the
workbook and recalculates their dependents ([`Trial`]), so any formula works. Two methods:

- **Simplex LP**: the model is linearised from `n + 1` evaluations and checked for linearity
  at one more point; then a dense two-phase simplex (Dantzig's rule, Bland's rule when it
  stalls) solves it exactly. Integer and binary constraints use depth-first branch and bound.
- **GRG Nonlinear** (the name Excel's dialog uses): GridCraft's method is *not* a generalised
  reduced gradient. It is an augmented-Lagrangian method (Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar) whose
  inner problems are solved by projected gradient descent with Barzilai–Borwein steps and an
  Armijo line search, on central-difference gradients. Variable bounds are kept by
  projection. It finds a local optimum of a smooth model; integer constraints use a small
  branch and bound on top.

- **Evolutionary**: a genetic search for models that aren't smooth (IF, lookups, rounding),
  with tournament selection, blend crossover and Gaussian mutation inside the variable bounds,
  feasibility-first ranking and integer rounding, followed by a compass (pattern) search around
  the best member. It stops when the population has converged, when the best member stops
  improving, or at the evaluation budget.

Work is bounded by an evaluation budget (no clock: `Instant` traps on wasm). The model is
saved as hidden sheet-scoped names (`solver_opt`, `solver_adj`, `solver_lhs1`…), so it
travels with the workbook through XLSX.

24590.name: builtin_format
24590.docs:
Built-in format code for an id (0..=49, en-US), e.g. 14 => "m/d/yyyy". Locale-specific ids
(23–36) and unknown ids return `None`.

11802.name: group_end
11802.docs:
Ends an undo group. If the workbook changed, the group becomes one undo step, unless it is
nested in another open group on the same document, which then owns the step. Groups opened
inside it and still open end with it. Returns whether the workbook changed.

27206.name: date_warnings
27206.docs:
Warns when the sample could not choose a date order: an all-ambiguous column keeps the
month-first reading, and a column with both kinds keeps its dates as text.

20812.name: MAX_MACRO_STEPS
20812.docs: The most steps in one macro, counting the steps inside Repeat and If.

28514.name: item_labels
28514.docs: Item captions the PivotTable's `<item x>` indices refer to.

4173.name: CHECKBOX_FORMAT
4173.docs: Number format that marks checkbox cells (TRUE/FALSE values drawn as boxes).

8024.name: fit_imported_rows
8024.docs:
Excel auto-fits rows to their tallest font when opening a file: rows without a user-set
height grow to fit their content. Rows the file made taller keep their height — our
line-height estimate can differ from Excel's, and shrinking files that already look
right would be a visible regression. Custom-height rows are left alone entirely.

1630.name: spills
1630.docs: New spills found during the pass: anchor → array.

4246.name: Timeline
4246.docs: A timeline's step, for continuing it past its last point (the Forecast Sheet's future rows).

11948.name: doc_uid
11948.docs: Document uid of the source (a cut only moves within the same workbook).

1703.name: fit_to_range
1703.docs:
A legacy (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) array formula's result fitted to the range it was entered in, as
Excel does: a single row or column repeats across the range, a single value fills it, cells
past the result show `#N/A`, and a result larger than the range is cut off.

14564.name: format_base
14564.docs: Writes `v` in `radix`, using 10-digit two's complement for negatives and padding to `places`.

4319.name: is_r1c1
4319.docs:
Looks like an R1C1 reference (`R`, `C`, `RC`, `R2`, `C3`, `R1C1`), which Excel doesn't
accept as a name.

15872.name: bahttext
15872.docs:
BAHTTEXT(number): the amount in Thai words with บาท, rounded to satang (สตางค์); a whole
number of baht ends in ถ้วน and a negative amount starts with ลบ.

1776.name: keep
1776.docs: The kept span of `0..len` given the non-blank span and the trim flags.

28733.name: axis_fields_xml
28733.docs: `<rowFields>`/`<colFields>`: the axis's cache field indices, with Σ Values (`-2`) at `values_at`.

4392.name: Allow
4392.docs:
The host trusts every caller of this session (an embedding that vets requests itself):
`link.open` opens allowed addresses directly. Disallowed schemes stay refused.

26190.name: directory_names
26190.docs: Names of every directory entry, or `None` when the directory can't be read.

15945.name: A
15945.docs: No lifting (all positions take arrays / ranges).

27644.name: parse_duration
27644.docs: A bounded ISO day/time duration. Calendar years/months cannot be represented as days.

30333.name: WSBOOL
30333.docs: WsBool (MS-XLS 2.4.351): its first byte's `fDialog` bit marks a dialog sheet, whose BOF says worksheet.

12386.name: format_painter
12386.docs: Format painter source style (sticky when double-clicked).

13694.name: reference_from_word
13694.docs:
A word after an optional sheet: a cell, a column/row range (`A:C`, `3:5`) or a name. A
trim operator (`A1:.E10`, `A:.A`) in place of the colon wraps the range in
[`UnOp::Trim`].

22704.name: style
22704.docs:
Cell styles (font, fill, borders, alignment, number format, protection), interned per
workbook.

8608.name: inline_steps
8608.docs:
The steps a recording keeps for a run of `m`: its enabled command steps as written, when they
stand on their own (no inputs, no output and only plain commands; a Repeat, If or Stop means
nothing outside its macro). `None` when they don't, and the recording leaves the run out.

2214.name: squarify
2214.docs: Squarified treemap layout of (index, area) items, sorted descending, into `r`.

9916.name: need_for
9916.docs:
Sheet-wide helper: the bottom-right cell a page grid for this sheet must reach so that the
layout rectangle up to `(x, y)` is covered. Layout coordinates never run ahead of sheet
coordinates (pages only add margins and gaps), so the sheet position is a safe bound.

4830.name: draw_block_links
4830.docs:
PDF annotations are not affected by graphics clipping, so intersect each cell with its page
block before adding a clickable rectangle. A repeated print-title cell may appear on several
pages and receives one annotation on each of them.

27936.name: map_rel_ids
27936.docs:
Rewrites relationship-id attributes (`r:id`, `r:embed`…: any attribute in the relationships
namespace) of an XML fragment through `map`. `None` when the fragment is damaged or `map` has
no id for one of them.

29244.name: record_python_spill
29244.docs:
Records the spill range of the Python cell read at `pos`, its anchor, when the file declares
one that a result can fill: the spill then exists even when the file holds no records for its
blank cells. Charged like [`dynamic_range`]'s scans.

3668.name: t_rows
3668.docs: The t statistic rows shared by the three t-tests.

1125.name: STACK_BUDGET
1125.docs:
Native stack, in bytes, that one formula's evaluation may use below its first `eval`. Past it,
`eval` answers `#NUM!`. It guards the stack and leaves 128 KiB of a 1 MiB thread for the frames
above the formula. A cell that another cell's formula computes on demand shares the budget of the
outermost formula ([`Host::stack_top`]).

2433.name: Theme
2433.docs: Workbook theme: 12 colours and the heading/body fonts.

17837.name: password
17837.docs:
Hash of the password (Excel-compatible, written to XLSX `sheetProtection`; never the
password itself).

3814.name: ControlAction
3814.docs: What a button runs when it is pressed.

29463.name: font_xml
29463.docs:
`minor`: the font follows the theme's body font (`<scheme val="minor"/>`). `dxf`: a
differential format's font, which writes only what it states.

14132.name: check_output_size
14132.docs: `#NUM!` when an `h` x `w` output would exceed the function cell budget.

29536.name: compound_file
29536.docs:
A version 3 compound file (512-byte sectors) holding `streams` under the root, laid out as
Excel lays it out: streams under 4096 bytes in the mini stream, larger ones in regular
sectors. Up to 109 FAT sectors (about 7 MB of streams).

15440.name: cell_result
15440.docs: A looked-up cell value: blanks read as 0 like a reference to an empty cell.

26993.name: csv
26993.docs: CSV import and export (RFC 4180 with the usual real-world leniency).

9119.name: holds
9119.docs: What a cell holds, for "C7 holds text".

4033.name: folds_in_place
4033.docs:
Whether case-folding `s` maps every char to exactly one char of the same UTF-8 length, so
byte positions in the folded text still line up with the original's character boundaries.

29682.name: python_scripts
29682.docs: The code of the Python cells written so far, in order: script `i` of the Python part.

15586.name: gamma
15586.docs: Γ(x). NaN at non-positive integers, infinite on overflow.

24596.name: is_exact_tie
24596.docs: True when `a`'s exact decimal expansion has a 5 as its 16th significant digit and only zeros after.

27212.name: read_csv_with_report
27212.docs:
[`read_csv`], with the warnings an open shows: a column whose date order had to be guessed,
or whose dates stayed text because it holds both orders.

20818.name: MAX_MACRO_COLUMNS
20818.docs: The most column types an input lists: one per column of a sheet.

8030.name: MAX_ADOPTED_RESULT_CELLS
8030.docs:
The most result cells [`adopt_python`] rebuilds from a file's cached spills, over all its
Python cells (each one is also limited to [`crate::model::python::MAX_RESULT_CELLS`]).

4252.name: line_targets
4252.docs:
The sheet and the row (or column) spans a size or visibility command works on. The lines are
`rows`/`cols` (`"2:5"`, `"B:B,D:F"`, optionally `Sheet!`-prefixed), else the selection's; the
sheet is `sheet`, else the prefix, else the active one. The selection belongs to the active
sheet, so another sheet needs explicit lines.

1709.name: fixed_now
1709.docs: Fixed "now" for deterministic tests; `None` = system clock.

9411.name: Footprint
9411.docs: What a macro would change, from a dry run on the real workbook.

15878.name: find_matches
15878.docs:
Non-overlapping delimiter matches (start, end) in char positions, in ascending order. Scans left
to right preferring the longest delimiter starting at each position, or (`from_end`) right to
left preferring the longest delimiter ending at each position. Empty delimiters are ignored unless all
delimiters are empty, in which case every position matches with zero length. Repeated
delimiters are tried once, and only those whose first (or, from the end, last) character is the
one at hand; a search past [`MAX_MATCH_WORK`] is `#VALUE!`.

15951.name: has
15951.docs: Whether argument `i` was supplied (present and not an empty literal like `F(1,)`).

4471.name: move_values_field
4471.docs:
Moves Σ Values between Rows and Columns, or within Rows, to `position` (default: the end).
In Columns it always comes after the last column field: the column layout doesn't place it
anywhere else yet.

8322.name: LOOKS_AROUND
8322.docs:
Commands that run on the debugged workbook between steps, besides `macro.debug` and queries.
They only look around (the selection, the active sheet, Go To, Find, zoom, copying), switch to
another window, close the workbook (which ends the run) or stop the run (Stop Action). The
debugger puts the run's active sheet and selection back before its next step runs.

30120.name: chars
30120.docs:
`cch` characters, compressed (one byte each) or UTF-16. When the characters run into
a `Continue` record, that record starts with a fresh compression flag ([MS-XLS] 2.5.293).

16024.name: call_lambda
16024.docs:
Calls that LAMBDA with `arg` (one group's values) and returns its single result; `None` when
there is no lambda.

9630.name: with_output
9630.docs:
`m` with the run's `output` (a form button that sends the output elsewhere) in place of its own
output anchor, after the policy and the approval, which go by the macro as it is stored. The
anchor is resolved and checked by [`prepare`] like the macro's own, and the footprint, the
conflict rule and the per-step guard all work on the cells it names.

3236.name: layer_under
3236.docs:
Adds the parts `lower` sets that `style` leaves unset (differential styles: default parts
are unset).

14789.name: aggregate_arg
14789.docs: `[aggregation]`: 0 or 1 AVERAGE (default), 2 COUNT, 3 COUNTA, 4 MAX, 5 MEDIAN, 6 MIN, 7 SUM.

16097.name: scalar_args
16097.docs:
For automatic array lifting: true for each parameter position that expects a scalar. When
an argument at a scalar position is an array, the function is applied element-wise
(broadcast like Excel's dynamic arrays). The last entry repeats for variadic tails; an
empty slice means no lifting.

27650.name: find_math
27650.docs:
The first `m:oMath`/`m:oMathPara` under `e` (an `a14:m` element or a paragraph), searched to a
bounded depth.

25107.name: render_date
25107.docs: Renders a date/time. `None` when the serial is outside the supported range.

30266.name: short
30266.docs: Records that were shorter than their structure; the parts present were used.

9776.name: groups
9776.docs: Every group, with its summary line after the detail; see [`groups_with`].

12392.name: depth
12392.docs: How many `execute` calls are running (0 between top-level commands).

16243.name: is_xml_char
16243.docs:
Whether XML 1.0 can carry `c`: the same set the xlsx crate's escapes keep, so the OMML is
well formed wherever the drawing part embeds it.

3455.name: tool_id
3455.docs: A tool id from its id or its label (case and punctuation ignored).

29104.name: read_note_shapes
29104.docs:
Reads the notes' VML shapes: a shape carrying `<x:Visible/>` marks its note as shown, and its
`<x:Anchor>` and style size become the note's box. Shapes may sit in groups.

11157.name: value
11157.docs:
The value of calculated field `i` for one report cell; `sum` gives a source field's sum
over that cell's records.

22710.name: major_font_ea
22710.docs: The heading font's East Asian typeface (`<a:ea>`); empty when the file did not set one.

9922.name: MAX_CHART_ROWS
9922.docs: Most category rows a PivotChart plots.

2293.name: catmull
2293.docs: One Catmull-Rom point between `p1` and `p2` (uniform parameterisation), tangent-scaled by 0.5.

27942.name: SheetKept
27942.docs: A sheet's kept content being written.

29250.name: shared_cost
29250.docs: What one dependent of a shared formula costs: its printed text plus its expression tree.

2366.name: MAX_CATS
2366.docs: Most categories drawn by category-axis charts.

6217.name: saved_model
6217.docs:
The saved model of a sheet as `data.solver` params, if any.

A sheet's own (sheet-level) model wins over one saved as workbook-level names, and its names
are read alone, so the two never mix. A sheet-level `solver_opt` of `""` (written by Reset
All over a workbook-level model) means the sheet has no model.

1131.name: note_volatile
1131.docs: Called when a volatile or dynamic-reference function is used.

8833.name: Env
8833.docs: What tokens refer to while a step runs.

28088.name: NameMap
28088.docs: Original part name (normalized) → written part name.

29396.name: MAX_FONT_NAME_CHARS
29396.docs: Longest font name kept, in characters (Excel's own limit is 31).

21767.name: rels
21767.docs: Relationships of the owning workbook or sheet part to kept parts.

3820.name: ACTIONS_KEY
3820.docs: The hidden-data key of the button actions xlsx has no place for.

29469.name: intern
29469.docs: Interns `items` into a deduplicated list, returning the index.

42.name: into
42.docs: Calls `U::from(self)`. That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of [From]<T> for U chooses to do.

26999.name: Cp1256Evidence
26999.docs: Evidence that bytes which aren't UTF-8 are Windows-1256 Arabic rather than Windows-1252.

11668.name: model
11668.docs:
The GridCraft document model: workbooks, sheets, a copy-on-write cell store, interned
styles, defined names, tables, conditional formats, validation, comments, charts and print
settings. Pure data; calculation lives in `gridcraft-calc`.

15519.name: ceil_floor_math
15519.docs:
CEILING.MATH / FLOOR.MATH / *.PRECISE: `up` picks the direction for positive numbers;
negative numbers round away from zero when `away`, toward zero otherwise.

9125.name: elapsed_ms
9125.docs: Milliseconds since the start, or `None` where there is no clock.

7890.name: sylk
7890.docs:
SYLK (`.slk`) import: the symbolic link text format older spreadsheets and some legacy systems
export. One record per line, fields separated by `;` (`;;` is a literal semicolon):

- `ID` starts the file; `E` ends it.
- `C;Y<row>;X<col>;K<value>;E<formula>` is a cell. `Y` and `X` may be left out to stay on the
  current row or column. `K` is a number, `"text"`, `TRUE`/`FALSE` or an error; `E` is a
  formula in R1C1 notation; `S;R<row>;C<col>` shares the formula of another cell.
- `P;P<code>` adds a number format to the file's list; `F;P<n>;Y<row>;X<col>` gives a cell the
  n-th format (0-based), and `F;W<first> <last> <width>` sets column widths in characters.

Other records (fonts, options, window settings) are skipped. Formulas are converted to A1 with
the same relative and absolute references, as Excel does when it opens the file.

2877.name: number_format
2877.docs: Number format code of the source values ("General" by default).

4185.name: options
4185.docs:
File › Options: reports the workbook-level settings and asks the interface to show its Options
page. Nothing changes here; every setting has its own command.

8036.name: read_html_table
8036.docs:
A web page that holds a table, whatever its extension: a web app's "Export to Excel" is often
HTML saved as `.xls` (#3166). Excel opens its table as a sheet (after warning that the format
and extension don't match): the cells read like typed input (or as text with `csv_as_text`),
header cells (`<th>`) are bold and centred, and the sheet takes the name the page gives it
(`<x:Name>`) or the file's. `None` when the bytes aren't such a page.

1642.name: iterate
1642.docs:
Iterative calculation: a circular reference reads the cell's previous value instead of
giving `#CIRC!`.

9344.name: start
9344.docs:
The workbook when the run started, and for each sheet now, its index there (`None` for a
sheet the run added).

28599.name: finish
28599.docs: Writes the PivotTable parts. `fmt_id` maps a number format code to its styles id.

4258.name: approx_text_width
4258.docs:
Approximate text width in points for autofit (no font metrics in the engine: average glyph
widths for the default font; a front end with fonts measures instead, see `Session::text_width`).

480.name: serial_from_unix_ms
480.docs: Date serial (1900 system, with fraction) for a Unix time in milliseconds.

553.name: parse_fraction
553.docs: `1/2` (only with a whole part, else it's a date), `1 1/2`, `0 3/4`.

4404.name: cf_style_json
4404.docs:
A conditional format's `style` as the model's `Style` JSON (`font`, `fill`, `borders`, `align`,
`num_fmt`, `protection`, merged over the default by the caller), where a colour may also be
written as `format_range` takes it (`"#RRGGBB"`, `{theme, tint}`, `"auto"`) and `fill` may be a
colour alone (a solid fill) or `"none"` (no fill). An unknown key is an error rather than
dropped: dropped, it left a rule with an empty format that matches and shows nothing.

15957.name: text
15957.docs: Text coercion for a scalar parameter.

28818.name: python_part
28818.docs:
The Python part ([MS-XLSX] 2.1.23, 2.3.10): where a workbook keeps the code of its Python cells.

A Python cell's formula is `_xlfn._xlws.PY(index, return_type, …)` ([MS-XLSX] 2.3.10.2): the
first argument is the zero-based index of a `pythonScript` element in this part, whose `code`
is the cell's Python code, and the second is 0 (an Excel value) or 1 (a Python object). Further
arguments are references the code names as `%Px%`, `x` being the argument's zero-based index
([MS-XLSX] 2.3.10.4). The part's root is `python` ([MS-XLSX] 2.4.102, CT_Python 2.6.249), with
`pythonScripts` (2.6.253) holding the `pythonScript` elements (2.6.252).

GridCraft writes one script per Python cell, in the order the cells are written, with the code
as it is (its `xl()` references stay text in the code, so no further arguments). Reading
resolves the index and puts each `%Px%` back as the text of argument `x`. A formula that names
no script the part has keeps only its cached value. Hostile input is bounded: the part's size,
the number of scripts, each script's length, and the code all cells take from the part
together.

9636.name: MACRO_KEY
9636.docs: The hidden-data key prefix of a stored macro (`macro_<n>`).

4550.name: PivotLayout
4550.docs: How a PivotTable lays out its row fields.

16103.name: accepts
16103.docs: Whether a call with `n` arguments is valid (Excel allows at most 255).

9709.name: next_name

8474.name: path_of

30272.name: color_table

20027.name: Command

2080.name: Table

3388.name: start_row

11090.name: range_text

8547.name: READS_FILES
8547.docs: Commands that read a file when given a `path`.

29110.name: cfvos
29110.docs: `cfvo` elements: plain children, or x14 ones with the value in an `xm:f` child.

26567.name: controls_in

The `<control>` elements under a `<controls>` element, looking through `mc:AlternateContent`

16322.name: height
16322.docs: Height above the baseline, in em.

9928.name: NOT_A_VALUE_CELL
9928.docs:
Why Show Details turns a cell down when it isn't a value cell of a PivotTable (the front end
edits that cell instead).

const.expr: "select a value cell in a PivotTable"

27948.name: lone_vml
27948.docs: The kept VML drawing of a sheet without notes; its new relationship id.

13852.name: CutText
13852.docs:
A criterion cut to its first 255 UTF-16 units in the middle of a surrogate pair: the
complete characters before the cut, followed (in Excel) by a lone high surrogate.

No cell text holds a lone surrogate, so `=` matches nothing and `<>` everything, as
Excel gives 0 for SUMIFS with a criterion of 128 emoji. For `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` the
criterion sorts just above the kept text: a cell matches `>`/`>=` when it sorts above
that text, and `<`/`<=` otherwise. This is an approximation (Excel wasn't checked) and
only matters for comparison criteria over 255 units.

29256.name: read_sheet
29256.docs:
Reads the sheet part `part`, with the VML shape numbers of the form controls read into the
model (pass-through keeps the other controls).

15160.name: year_basis
15160.docs: Days in a year for discount securities.

6223.name: OPTIONS_FIELDS
6223.docs:
How many values the options row of Save Model holds at least: method, non-negative,
population size, mutation rate, random seed, require bounds, convergence and generations
without improvement.

3680.name: anova_two_factor_with
3680.docs:
Anova: Two-Factor With Replication. The input range holds column labels in its first row and
sample labels in its first column; each sample (a level of the row factor) spans
`rowsPerSample` consecutive rows, so every cell of the design holds that many observations.

1137.name: Host
1137.docs: What the evaluator needs from its surroundings.

2445.name: series_name
2445.docs:
A series name: a reference/formula or a defined name (`[0]!Title` in a file) is evaluated,
a quoted or other bare literal is used as is.

20465.name: text_outline

3826.name: install_filter

24389.name: remove_personal_info
24389.docs:
Trust Center › Privacy Options › "Remove personal information from file properties on save"
(`<workbookPr filterPrivacy="1"/>`): kept with the file, and while it is on the author and
company are left out of the XLSX files GridCraft writes, as Excel leaves them empty. Other
formats aren't filtered: the workbook's own serialization still holds them.

28240.name: MAX_META
28240.docs: Largest relationships, content-types or VML part read here.

5207.name: rewrite
