Rewrites every formula reference (chart series included), sparkline source and PivotTable
source for a structural edit on `target`.

9058.name: rolled_back
9058.docs: What a run that rolled back leaves: "Nothing was changed.", or the files it wrote before.

15598.name: norm_inv
15598.docs: Inverse of the standard normal CDF (NaN outside (0, 1)).

16906.name: input_text
16906.docs: What the formula bar shows: a formula, a Python cell's code, or the value.

20757.name: column
20757.docs: Header name of the filtered column within the table.

1575.name: precedents_of
1575.docs: Precedent areas of a formula cell (for Trace Precedents).

24681.name: Comma
24681.docs: Unresolved comma (resolved during analysis into thousands/scale markers or a literal).

6734.name: MAX_STORED_BYTES
6734.docs:
The most bytes the stored (escaped) form of an item can take: an escaped one-byte character
takes seven (the three-byte marker and four digits).

8042.name: save_file_bytes
8042.docs:
[`save_bytes`] for the file at `path`: relative paths to linked workbooks are rewritten for
its folder, so they still name the same files.

1648.name: precision
1648.docs:
"Set precision as displayed" is on: results are rounded to their cells' formats before
they are stored or read by other formulas.

27297.name: image_ext
27297.docs: File extension for an image MIME type.

29913.name: sheets
29913.docs: Every sheet's name in BoundSheet8 order (including skipped chart/macro sheets).

20976.name: non_empty
20976.docs: Every data cell must have something in it.

28678.name: resolve_source
28678.docs: Resolves a pivot source to (sheet, range including the header row, worksheetSource XML).

486.name: is_leap
486.docs: Whether `y` is a Gregorian leap year, for every `i32` year.

4410.name: rebase_cf_formulas
4410.docs: Moves the relative references of a rule's per-cell formulas written for `from` to `to`.

8261.name: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION
8261.docs: The error a programmatic `link.open` of a web or e-mail address returns.

const.expr: "Web and e-mail links open only when the user clicks them and confirms; a command can't open them."

15963.name: flatten
15963.docs: Every value of every argument, flattened row-major (scalars as themselves).

28824.name: MAX_CODE_BYTES
28824.docs:
Most bytes of code all the cells of a workbook take from the part together. Several formulas
may name one script, so without it a small part could fill memory.

8334.name: touched
8334.docs:
The workbooks the run has touched (by uid). Steps run on the macro's own workbook and the
policy refuses window and file commands, so this is the macro's workbook unless a command
reaches another one some other way; edits of these wait until the run ends.

1940.name: Prim
1940.docs: A drawing primitive in chart coordinates (origin top-left, y down, units = points/pixels).

9642.name: fit_size
9642.docs:
Leaves out the last top-level steps of `m` until it fits the size [`check_size`] allows, and
returns how many steps it left out (a recording cut to fit, as at the step limit). Each step's
JSON is measured once.

22503.name: contiguous_value_run
22503.docs:
Last row (inclusive, capped at `cap`) of the maximal run of contiguous rows at or after
`from.row` that store a cell in `from.col` with a non-empty *value* in `from.col`. `None`
when `from` itself doesn't qualify.

Deliberately narrower than `has`/`get` (which also count a formula with no cached value
yet, for Ctrl+arrow navigation): this matches `Sheet::value_ref`, whose callers test the
`Value` it returns with `!v.is_empty()` regardless of whether a formula produced it — a
formula cell with an empty cached value (`=""`, or not yet recalculated) is "empty" to
them. A stored cell with no value and no formula (for example a formatted spill child) does
fall through to `spill` in `value_ref`, so `last_contiguous_nonempty` asks `value_ref`
about the row where this run stops.

Walks each band's row map with `BTreeMap::range` (one in-order pass per band) instead of
one `get` per row, so a long, densely-populated run costs roughly one tree-traversal step
per row rather than one binary search per row.

27662.name: char_latex
27662.docs: LaTeX for one character of a math run.

9715.name: collapsed
9715.docs: Every detail line is hidden: the button shows +.

8480.name: add_notes
8480.docs:
What every answer about the run's end or its state adds: the data shift at the start and the
files the run wrote (they stay, whatever happens to the workbook).

27735.name: kind
27735.docs:
Last path segment of the relationship type (`worksheet`, `styles`, …): the same for the
transitional and strict namespaces.

9788.name: hf_text_k
9788.docs:
Layout units per sheet pixel of header and footer text: 1 with Scale with Document on,
otherwise `1 / scale`, so the text keeps its point size on paper.

11096.name: refresh
11096.docs:
Recomputes a pivot and writes its report. With `replace` false, refuses when the target area
holds other data. Returns the written area.

8553.name: recorder
8553.docs:
Turning a recording into a macro.

The recording buffer (`crate::engine::record`) holds the top-level commands run while recording, each
with the sheet and selection it ran in. When recording stops:

- commands a macro may not run (saving, opening files…) and other macros' commands are left
  out; a macro run while recording is replaced by its steps when it has no inputs, no output
  and only plain commands (otherwise it is left out), and an Automate script run while
  recording by the steps it ran, leaving out the steps a macro may not run; both are the steps
  as they ran, kept with the recording ([`crate::engine::record::Recorder::ran`]), and a run without
  them is left out;
- a `sheet.activate` or `selection.set` step is added where the sheet or selection changed
  between commands without one, and runs of `selection.set` collapse to the last;
- with relative references (the default), the selection when recording started is the example
  input: references on its sheet in, next to or near it become tokens (`Input.col(2)`,
  `Input.below`, `Input.cell(1,4)`), also inside formulas (`{{Input.col(2)}}`), and the input's
  shape, header and column types are inferred from it as it was when recording started;
- recorded text that playback would read as a token stays text: a reference parameter that
  reads as one (a defined name called `Output`) becomes `{"$text": …}`, and `{{` in a string
  becomes `{{{{`.

16255.name: SOURCE_TOO_LONG
16255.docs:
The error for a source over [`MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`]. It is one shared value so that a cache can
answer for such a source by its length alone, without reading it.

7318.name: is_secret_param
7318.docs: Params that hold a secret: `password`, or a name ending in `Password`.

26573.name: read
26573.docs:
Reads a sheet's buttons, scroll bars and spin buttons: each `<control>` with its properties
part, else its VML shape, and VML shapes the sheet doesn't list (files that only have VML).
The shapes come from the VML drawing with relationship id `vml_rid` (`<legacyDrawing r:id>`).
Returns the shape numbers of the controls it read, so pass-through keeps only the others.

27881.name: fragments
27881.docs: (slot, XML with the namespace declarations it needs).

18944.name: external
18944.docs:
The target is outside this workbook (Excel's "Existing File or Web Page"): a relationship in
the file, not a `location`. A bare file name can't be told from a defined name by its text.

6229.name: MAX_MODEL_ROWS
6229.docs:
Most cells a model written by Save Model takes: the objective, the variables, the options
and one per constraint.

3686.name: Rng
3686.docs:
A seeded generator: xoshiro256** (Blackman and Vigna, a public-domain algorithm) with its
state filled by SplitMix64. The same seed gives the same numbers in GridCraft; they are not
Excel's numbers, whose generator is not documented.

6302.name: target
6302.docs: The Limits report: the objective is this variable itself.

11461.name: windows
11461.docs:
Windows on open workbooks.

Every open workbook has one or more windows (View › New Window adds another on the same
workbook). A window has its own selection, active sheet and per-sheet selections. The active
window's view lives in its [`DocState`] (`selection`, `sheet_selections`) and in the workbook's
active sheet ([`crate::model::workbook::Workbook::active_sheet`]), where every command reads
it; each other window keeps its view in [`WindowState`] until it is activated. Swapping a view
in or out never copies the workbook or makes it dirty: the active sheet is set in place through
the shared `Arc`, and selections live outside the workbook.

5067.name: bands
5067.docs:
Splits `start..=end` into bands whose sizes fit `avail(band_start)`; `breaks` force a new
band before a line. Stops after `cap` bands.

3832.name: apply_filter
3832.docs: Hides rows of the autofilter range that fail any criterion.

14150.name: flat_filtered
14150.docs: Flattened values for TOROW/TOCOL with the ignore filter applied.

9064.name: approve
9064.docs:
Approves the macro for this session when `approve` is set, or asks (an
[`EngineError::Approve`]) when it needs approval it doesn't have.

4051.name: Ctx
4051.docs:
Applies an edit to a copy of the active workbook, then recalculates and commits it.
`changed` collects cells whose content changed; set `structural` for row/column/sheet edits
(full recalc).

25922.name: add_page
25922.docs: Adds a page of `width_pt` × `height_pt` points and returns it for drawing.

19528.name: intercept
19528.docs: Set Intercept: fixed y at x = 0 (linear, exponential, polynomial).

27230.name: write
27230.docs:
Invalid/native out-of-range data uses the existing rectangle fallback. A successful
result is complete before it is appended, so malformed points never yield half a stroke.

9283.name: bodies
9283.docs:
Repeat and If bodies by the path of their frame: a body is copied the first time its step
runs, not on every pass.

4197.name: range_on
4197.docs: A range parameter on any sheet (whole columns trimmed to the used range).

8048.name: iso
8048.docs: `date` and `time` say which parts the cell's format shows; a format with neither is not a date.

27303.name: XF_EXT_URI
27303.docs: `ext` URI of the `xfComplement` extension on an `xf`.

4270.name: apply_style
4270.docs: Applies `f` to the style of every targeted cell (whole rows/columns set the line format too).

492.name: time_fraction
492.docs: Fraction of a day for a time.

22290.name: preserved
22290.docs:
Unmodelled file content of this sheet kept for saving (form controls, OLE objects, query
tables). Goes away with the sheet; not in JSON.

4343.name: evaluate
4343.docs:
Evaluates what typing `formula` into a cell would show. A formula `cell.set` would refuse (it
doesn't parse, or calls a function with the wrong number of arguments) is an error that says
why, not `#NAME?`; an unknown function name still evaluates to `#NAME?`, as in Excel.

24906.name: FormatColor
24906.docs: Colour from a `[Red]` or `[ColorN]` section tag.

4416.name: inspect
4416.docs: Read-only commands for agents: inspect the workbook, read ranges, cell details.

8267.name: Refused
8267.docs: Refused, with the reason to show.

30065.name: Records
30065.docs: Iterates over the records of a stream starting at `pos`.

15969.name: util
15969.docs: Shared argument coercion and collection helpers.

17277.name: RunningTotal
17277.docs: Running total in the first row field.

8340.name: locks
8340.docs: Whether edits of the workbook with this uid wait for the run to end.

9648.name: normalize_steps
9648.docs:
Rewrites the short step form into the tagged one, in place, refusing nesting past the limit
before the steps are deserialized.

22509.name: shift_cols_in_rows
22509.docs:
Shifts cells within rows `r0..=r1` and columns `>= from` horizontally (Insert/Delete Cells
with shift right/left).

8486.name: changed
8486.docs:
What the run changed in its workbook since it started: cells as `Sheet!A1:B2` ranges and the
sheets it added, deleted or renamed (at most [`MAX_LISTED`] entries), and how many cells
changed on the sheets the workbook had at the start.

9794.name: data_rows
9794.docs: Bands holding printed data: `[first, last]` row bands and column bands.

29049.name: read
29049.docs: Resolves every value-metadata block without assuming the indices at each layer coincide.

14953.name: season
14953.docs: Seasonal state for positions 0..m (empty without seasonality).

16261.name: char_pos
16261.docs: The 1-based character position of the error in `source`, when known.

7324.name: not_grouping
7324.docs:
Undo and Redo wait while an undo group is open on the active document (an action that spans
several calls is still running).

8705.name: literal
8705.docs:
Plain recorded `params` written so playback reads them as they are: a string in a reference
parameter that playback would read as a token, or that holds `{{`, becomes `{"$text": …}`,
and `{{` in any other string becomes `{{{{`.

29268.name: extra_shared_cost
29268.docs:
What one dependent of a shared formula costing `cost` is charged: its cost beyond an ordinary
formula cell's.

12629.name: adjust
12629.docs: Adjusts a formula living on sheet `host` after `edit` on sheet `target`.

6235.name: check_options_spill
6235.docs:
The options row is an array constant that spills `width - 1` cells to the right of `anchor`.
Refused, before anything is written, when the spill would run off the sheet or be blocked
(the anchor would show `#SPILL!`): a cell there holds content or another formula's spilled
values, or a merged area or a table meets the row. `ours` are the cells Save Model
writes or clears (a model saved at the same place before, whose options spill may be
replaced); `used` are the model's own cells, which the spill must not cover.

2457.name: center
2457.docs: The same polynomial in `u = (X - center) / scale`, for stable evaluation.

14010.name: MAX_STEPS
14010.docs:
Steps one `match_from` call may take. An honest match against Excel's 32,767-character
cell ceiling costs a few hundred thousand; a hostile one (star churn) is capped instead
of quadratic — a call that spends more gives up and reports no match, quiet degradation
like the other work caps on far-past-realistic input.

5073.name: split_bands
5073.docs:
Splits a layout's area into row and column bands that fit its pages (at most `cap` of each),
honouring manual breaks (when `lay.manual_breaks`), print headings and repeated titles. The
one pagination rule shared by printing, PDF export, Page Break Preview and Page Layout view.

24328.name: PhoneticString
24328.docs:
The phonetic (furigana) data of one shared string: its `<rPh>` runs, in document order, and its
`<phoneticPr>` when the file had one.

`text` is the string's base text — the only handle a cell keeps on its shared string — and is
the key the writer uses to re-emit the runs next to the right `<si>`.

10232.name: formatted
10232.docs: The value is a number shown with the source format.

14083.name: serial_arg
14083.docs: A date serial argument (truncated to whole days when `whole`). Out of range → `#NUM!`.

3838.name: refuse_unless_outline_allowed
3838.docs: Outline commands change line visibility and grouping: a protected sheet must allow formatting that axis.

7689.name: ordinal_suffix
7689.docs: `1st Period` → `2nd Period`: an English ordinal ending is rewritten to suit the new number.

1295.name: computed_criterion
1295.docs:
Excel's "formula as criteria": the formula is written for the first record, so its relative
references move down to `record`'s row, and the database's labels name its fields.
Known gap: the shifted references are not dependencies of the calling cell. One that lands
outside both the database and the criteria cell's own precedents (say `=G2<H2` with column H
outside the database) is read here but not tracked, so editing that cell doesn't recalculate
the D-function until something else does.

8997.name: MAX_PARAM_BYTES
8997.docs:
The most bytes of parameters one run passes to its commands, all steps together: on the web
build, where there is no clock, this and the step limit bound the work a run does.

24401.name: vba_project
24401.docs:
VBA project (`xl/vbaProject.bin`) carried through unchanged. GridCraft does not run
macros; the blob is preserved so that saving a macro-enabled workbook never destroys the
macros it arrived with. base64 in JSON. `None` = the workbook has no macros. Shared, so a
copy of the workbook (every edit's undo step) doesn't copy it.

28252.name: CALC_FEATURES_URI
28252.docs: The workbook extension listing the calculation features the saved values were computed with.

14156.name: span
14156.docs: Range of kept indices for TAKE (`take = true`) or DROP along an axis of length `len`.

3911.name: is_literal_list
3911.docs:
Whether a list rule's source is a literal list (`"a,b"`, or `a,b` typed without quotes) rather
than a reference or a name to evaluate.

5219.name: Clipboard
5219.docs: The clipboard: a block of cells (with formulas and styles) or marching-ants reference.

25782.name: CID_BASE_FONT
25782.docs: Base font of the CID font used for characters WinAnsiEncoding lacks.

6600.name: Body
6600.docs: The variable rows, the constraint rows and their headers.

4057.name: area_shape
4057.docs:
The rows and columns a printed reference covers (`A1:B3`, `Sheet2!$A$1`, `C:E`), or `None`
for any other form (a name, an error).

attrs.other: #[error("the file is not a valid spreadsheet: {0}")]

19534.name: MAX_FORECAST
19534.docs:
Longest forward / backward forecast kept from a file or a command, in x units. Excel's own
limit is unconfirmed; the renderer additionally bounds the forecast by the plot's slot budget.

352.name: INDEXED
352.docs: The 64-entry legacy indexed colour palette, stored as `RRGGBB`.

11905.name: GroupStep
11905.docs:
Where the last [`Session::group_end`] or [`Session::group_rollback`] left its document: the
workbook and selection it ended at, the undo length then, and whether it made a step. A
command that ended the group tells its own later changes from the group's step by it, and
keeps the group's name only when the group's step is exactly its own (the entry holds the
workbook the step started from). Dropped when the outermost command finishes, so it keeps no
workbook alive between commands.

1660.name: iterate_loops
1660.docs:
Iterative calculation, after a first pass over `order` that met circular references. The
formulas that read a previous value (the loops and what depends on them) are evaluated
again in the same order, each pass starting from the last one's values and reading what it
has already produced (Gauss-Seidel), until no formula on a loop changes by `max_change` or
more, or after `max_iterations` passes in all. Returns the number of passes.

498.name: Parsed
498.docs: A parsed entry: its value and the number format Excel would apply automatically.

22296.name: has_object
22296.docs:
Whether the floating object `o` exists on this sheet. `Shape` accepts any shape (an
equation included); `Equation` only an equation.

8200.name: script_sandbox_check
8200.docs:
Refuses file access while a [`ScriptSandbox`] is alive (and, failing closed, while the
thread is being torn down).

571.name: Python
571.docs: A Python cell's code raised an error, or Python stopped.

12124.name: trust
12124.docs:
Where the workbook's content came from: whether its active content may run without
asking. Unlike `scripts_trusted`, this is provenance, not consent: it is set when the
workbook is opened from a file, carried by content pasted from such a workbook, and never
changed by a trust decision.

9581.name: objects
9581.docs: Objects added, changed and removed between two versions of a sheet.

10889.name: flatten_values
10889.docs:
The Σ Values level at row field depth `depth`: one item per value field, each followed by
the row fields below it (`nodes`) or, innermost, holding that value.

12197.name: formula_bar
12197.docs: View › Show › Formula Bar (an application option in Excel, not saved in the file).

9654.name: load
9654.docs:
After a file is opened: moves macros out of hidden names into `Workbook::macros`, keeps
macros in a newer format unread (`Workbook::macros_unread`), and drops macros that are damaged
or over the limits. Returns a warning for what was kept unread and one for what was dropped.

25058.name: parse_sections
25058.docs: Parses a whole format code into its sections.

30217.name: builtin
30217.docs: `Some(id)` for a built-in style (BuiltInStyle.istyBuiltIn), `None` for a user style.

27674.name: nary
27674.docs: `m:nary`: a large operator with its limits and operand.

28982.name: read
28982.docs: Reading the workbook part and everything hanging off it.

8492.name: NeedsPermission
8492.docs:
Reads or writes files: the macro must list the command in its permissions, and the person
approves the macro before it runs. The text says what it does ("reads a file").

12416.name: doc_window
12416.docs: The most recently active window of a workbook, preferring one that isn't hidden.

23969.name: MAX_TAB_RATIO
23969.docs: The entire bar, in thousandths: the upper bound used by XLSX I/O.

936.name: broadcast_len
936.docs:
Cell count of a `rows`×`cols` broadcast result, or `None` when it would exceed [`MAX_CELLS`].
Each operand passes its own size cap, but their broadcast product can be far larger
(`SEQUENCE(1048576)*SEQUENCE(1,16384)` is 17 billion cells), so it is checked before allocating.
The product is formed in `u64`: on wasm32 `usize` is 32 bits, where a `usize` product above
`u32::MAX` would wrap (2^32 cells → 0) and slip past the cap.

7403.name: displayed_updates
7403.docs:
The constants among `cells` on sheet `si` whose value the option changes, with their rounded
values. A locked constant on a protected sheet keeps its value: protection keeps its content,
and rounding it by its format would change the content that the sheet protects.

8711.name: infer_input
8711.docs:
The example input's shape: a header when the first row is all text over other kinds of
values, and each column's type when all its values agree.

29274.name: sheet_write
29274.docs: Writing worksheet parts and the parts they own (tables, comments, drawings, charts).

6241.name: load_model_cells
6241.docs: `data.solverLoadModel`: makes a model written by Save Model the active sheet's model.

28039.name: decode_name
28039.docs: A target segment with its percent-escapes decoded; as written when they don't decode to UTF-8.

2463.name: eval
2463.docs: The trendline's y at `x`; `None` outside its domain (x ≤ 0 for log/power) or when not finite.

14016.name: field_index
14016.docs: Resolves the field argument: a label or a 1-based column number. `None` when omitted.

5079.name: fallback_lines
5079.docs:
The lines of `text` printed in place of an equation that has no layout: those of its first
`MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` (a longer source never lays out, and a file can carry megabytes) that fit a
frame `h` points tall at `line_h` points per line (at least the first), and never more than
[`MAX_FALLBACK_LINES`]. A single `pg.text` call would print every newline as `?`.

3844.name: move_marks
3844.docs:
Data ▸ Outline ▸ Settings: whether summary rows sit below their detail and summary columns
right of it. A changed direction moves each collapsed group's mark (+) to its new summary line.
Moves the collapsed marks of a line axis to the summary line on its new side (`on` is the new
setting, `was_before` the old one). A line that nested groups share keeps its mark on the outermost
group whose detail is all hidden, or the outermost when none is.

24407.name: source_path
24407.docs:
The file this workbook reports as its own, which is what `CELL("filename")` returns.
`None` = no file yet, which Excel reports as an empty string until the workbook has been
saved once. Deliberately separate from `source_dir`: that one names the folder relative
links are relative to and must keep naming it after a Save As into another folder, since
the links in memory are still written for the old one. Not in JSON.

5225.name: check_table_shift
5225.docs:
Like Excel, Insert/Delete Cells never shifts part of a table: cells shifted up or down must
hold whole table columns, cells shifted left or right whole table rows, and deleting cells
never takes a table's header row without the whole table.

16778.name: b64
16778.docs: Minimal base64 for serde (image bytes in JSON).

25788.name: pdf_uri_string
25788.docs: URI actions use byte strings. Percent-encode non-ASCII UTF-8 before PDF string escaping.

6606.name: flip
6606.docs: -1 for a row the tableau negated, else 1.

15616.name: interp
15616.docs: Value at fractional rank `pos` of the sorted data, linearly interpolated, found by selection.

1520.name: dependents_untaken
1520.docs:
[`Graph::dependents`] leaving out the formulas whose range reads an earlier call with the
same `taken` already listed. A walk over many changed cells that a few broad ranges cover
then lists those formulas once, instead of once per cell (which squared the work). The
graph must not change while `taken` is in use.

27242.name: described_source
27242.docs:
The marker and source of a `gridcraft:latex:<marker>:<source>` description; `None` for any
other description, a malformed marker or a blank source.

15762.name: check_regression_size
15762.docs:
Rejects regressions too large to fit: more than [`MAX_REGRESSORS`] predictors is `#VALUE!`,
more than [`MAX_REGRESSION_WORK`] multiply-adds is `#NUM!`.

27315.name: prefix_params
27315.docs: Adds Excel's `_xlpm.` prefix to LET/LAMBDA parameter names, at the declaration and at every use in scope.

22302.name: value
22302.docs: Displayed value of a cell: its own value, or a spilled value.

4355.name: write_totals
4355.docs: Writes the totals row cells (labels and SUBTOTAL formulas).

8206.name: Confirm
8206.docs:
`link.open` refuses external addresses; the user opens them by clicking the link, which
asks first ([`Session::open_confirmed_link`]). References still navigate.

12130.name: from_saved
12130.docs:
A workbook as its file saved it: the dependency graph is built but nothing is
evaluated, so every value is the one the file holds until an edit reaches it. `trust`
is as for [`DocState::new`].

1885.name: format_number
1885.docs: Formats a number with a format code (General shows up to the precision implied by `step`).

13438.name: Struct
13438.docs: Structured reference body after a table name or bare: the raw text inside `[...]`.

19905.name: get

25064.name: render
25064.docs: Rendering a value with a parsed section.

7117.name: json_value
7117.docs: What a JSON value typed into a cell is, as a constant.

8425.name: BUSY
8425.docs: The message for edits refused while a macro is being debugged.

27680.name: limit
27680.docs: `m:limLow`, `m:limUpp`: a limit under or over its base.

3339.name: table_cells
3339.docs:
The cells of the first table in `html`, row by row, read no further than `max_rows` rows of
`max_cols` cells (the pasted text's shape, itself clamped to the sheet) and [`MAX_HTML_CELLS`]
in all. A cell spanning columns is followed by empty cells, and a column covered by a `rowspan`
from above holds an empty cell, so positions line up with the tab-separated text. Empty when
there is no table.

26445.name: colors_xml
26445.docs: The colour style part a chartex part comes with: the theme accents in turn.

12422.name: activate_recent
12422.docs: Activates the most recently active window that isn't hidden, else any window, else none.

27826.name: raw_rels
27826.docs:
A part's relationships with full type URIs. `Ok(vec![])` when it has none; an error when the
rels part is damaged or too large (its part then can't be kept faithfully).

7409.name: locked_cell_error
7409.docs:
Whether a locked cell on a protected sheet stays locked: `None` when it's in an Allow Edit
Range without a password or one unlocked in this session, else the message to show.

30515.name: read_xls
30515.docs: Reads an Excel 97-2003 workbook. Inspect the report's warnings for what was skipped.

29280.name: thread_ids
29280.docs:
Ids of the threaded comments of sheet `si`: the thread's id, then one per reply. GUID-shaped
and deterministic; they only need to be unique within the file.

6247.name: Point
6247.docs: The values the solvers see at a point: the objective and `lhs − rhs` per row.

28045.name: KeptOut
28045.docs: Names given to kept parts while a package is written.

11406.name: accent_for
11406.docs: Accent theme slot (4..=9) for a style number; 1 and every 7th style are neutral (dk1).

30661.name: xlsb
30661.docs:
Data-only XLSB import, implemented from Microsoft's public MS-XLSB specification:
<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-xlsb/acc8aa92-1f02-4167-99f5-84f9f676b95a>.
Formula caches become constants. Styles, macros and other workbook features are not run or imported.

3777.name: random_numbers
3777.docs:
Random Number Generation: `count` numbers from a distribution in each of `variables`
columns, drawn row by row.

1307.name: NumberFormat
1307.docs: A parsed number format code. Cheap to clone.

5158.name: render_pdf
5158.docs: Renders laid-out sheets to a PDF.

24413.name: next_sheet_name
24413.docs: A fresh sheet name `SheetN` not in use.

19327.name: name
19327.docs: Formula text for the series name (`Sheet1!$B$1`) or a literal.

5231.name: slicer
5231.docs:
Slicers: on-sheet widgets that filter one column of a table by clicking value tiles.

A slicer is a thin front-end over the existing filter machinery: its selection is written as a
[`FilterCriterion::Values`] into the sheet's [`AutoFilter`] (over the table's range) and
[`super::data::apply_filter`] hides the rows. Creating a slicer (`insert.slicer` /
`table.insertSlicer`) selects everything, i.e. applies no filter.

15622.name: pairs
15622.docs:
Pairs of numbers at matching positions of two arrays (pairs with a non-number skipped).
Different sizes give `#N/A`; errors propagate.

291.name: sheet_needs_quotes
291.docs:
Whether Excel quotes a sheet name in a reference (`'My Sheet'!A1`): it starts with a digit or
`.`, holds anything but letters (any script), digits, `_` and `.`, reads as an A1 cell within
the sheet or as an R1C1 reference, or is a boolean.

4142.name: ScriptSandbox
4142.docs:
While one is alive, [`read_file`] and [`write_file`] on this thread refuse every path: a
stored script's steps run inside one (#2178), so no command reaches the file system from a
script whatever its parameters are called. Dropping it (also on unwind) lifts the refusal.

25940.name: polygon
25940.docs: A closed polygon, filled and/or stroked.

27248.name: anchor_open
27248.docs:
The opening `<xdr:twoCellAnchor>` for a model anchor, carrying Excel's `editAs` when the mode
is not the default: omitted for "Move and size with cells", `editAs="oneCell"` for "Move but
don't size", `editAs="absolute"` for "Don't move or size". (Excel writes pictures this way;
the standalone `oneCellAnchor`/`absoluteAnchor` elements are read on import but not written.)
Returns the opening tag and the matching closing tag.

27321.name: read_xlsx_with
27321.docs:
[`read_xlsx`], and opens formulas from Google Sheets' XLSX export as the formulas written in
Google Sheets (#2871).

Google writes a formula that uses a function it thinks Excel lacks as
`IFERROR(__xludf.DUMMYFUNCTION("<formula, quotes doubled>"),<cached value>)`; Excel shows the
cached value. A cell formula holding that wrapper, whole or inside a larger formula, is read
as the formula inside when it parses and `known` says GridCraft calculates every function it
calls. Otherwise (a Google-only function such as `GOOGLETRANSLATE`, inner text that doesn't
parse, or nesting past the parser's limit) the wrapper stays, so the cell keeps showing the
cached value as in Excel. `known` is passed in because this crate doesn't depend on the
function library.

30010.name: area
30010.docs: An area; a range spanning every BIFF8 row (or column) becomes a whole-column (row) ref.

5669.name: FinalTableau
5669.docs: The final tableau of an optimal LP, for the Sensitivity report.

13371.name: parse
13371.docs:
Parses formula text. A leading `=` (or `+`/`-` as Lotus users type) is accepted and skipped
for `=`.

802.name: compare_numbers
802.docs:
Compares numbers the way Excel does: both are rounded to 15 significant digits first, so binary
noise such as `0.1+0.2` versus `0.3` counts as equal.

26451.name: REL_CTRL_PROP
26451.docs: The worksheet relationship to a control properties part (MS-XLSX), as Excel writes it.

13736.name: combine
13736.docs: Folds `A1:B2`-like range operations of two plain refs into a single reference.

15044.name: filter
15044.docs: Runs the filter over the data; `errors` collects the one-step errors when given.

12501.name: shift_relative
12501.docs: Copy/fill: relative parts move by `(dr, dc)`. References pushed off the sheet become `#REF!`.

7415.name: display
7415.docs: How cells look as text: number formats applied, for the grid, clipboard, CSV and agents.

7488.name: Extend
7488.docs: Fill Series from the right-drag menu: extends like a plain drag, and a lone number counts up.

29286.name: DEFAULT_NOTE_BOX
29286.docs:
The box a note made here gets: two columns right of its cell, four rows tall, 108 x 59.25 pt.
A box read from a file that equals it is kept as `None`, so a note's model survives a save.

11339.name: extend_to
11339.docs: Extends the current area from the anchor to `to` (Shift+click / Shift+arrows).

5018.name: PrintOptions
5018.docs: Options shared by the print commands.

15336.name: odd_last
15336.docs: Σ DCi/NLi, Σ Ai/NLi and Σ DSCi/NLi over an odd last period.

16717.name: check_caps
16717.docs: The size and nesting caps, checked before RaTeX sees the source.

24419.name: table
24419.docs: Table by name across sheets: (sheet index, table index).

5237.name: Values
5237.docs: Show rows whose display text is one of these (case-insensitive); `blanks` includes empty.

16790.name: expr
16790.docs: The parsed expression, re-parsing after deserialization.

20641.name: Custom
20641.docs: Custom: one or two comparisons (`op` like `>=`, `=*abc*`), joined by and/or.

1459.name: PENDING
1459.docs: Insertions an [`Intervals`] keeps aside (scanned by every query) before merging them in.

4075.name: clear
4075.docs:
The Clear commands (Delete is Clear Contents). As in Excel, the rows an applied filter hides
are left as they are; rows hidden by hand are cleared.

29724.name: check_sheet_names
29724.docs:
Refuses sheet names XLSX cannot hold. The reader repairs such names (cuts, strips, renames
duplicates) but formulas keep the old spelling, so the saved file would turn into `#REF!`.

297.name: by_columns
297.docs:
The levels are columns and the points run down the rows (else the levels are rows and the
points run along the columns).

6837.name: assemble
6837.docs: The text of the item held by `parts`, as [`get`] reads it.

11996.name: allows_code
11996.docs: Whether active content may run without asking.

22314.name: filter_button_space
22314.docs:
Horizontal header space in unzoomed grid units (96 units per inch).
Observed in Windows Excel 16.0 build 20326: AutoFit reserves 12.5 pt at
100-200% zoom, 25 pt at 50%, regardless of header row height. Below 100%
the dropdown keeps its screen width. This is geometry, not font padding.

4367.name: recommend_charts
4367.docs:
Chart types that suit the shape of the data, best first, as `(type, subtype, label)` for
`insert.chart`. Our own heuristic from the shape of the block (series count, points per
series, text categories, negative values), not a copy of Excel's ranking: two numeric columns
without labels → scatter; one short series → column, pie, bar; long series → line; several
series → clustered and stacked columns and bars, line.

30016.name: push
30016.docs: Pushes the result of a token one level above the operands it consumed.

9526.name: journal
9526.docs:
The journal's length: the dry run journals nothing (`Session::journal_paused`), so nothing
of the person's is evicted, and the length puts back exactly what was there.

4440.name: RecordingStart
4440.docs:
Where recording started, kept beside the buffer, with the name, shortcut and description the
macro is to be saved with (from the Record Macro dialog), applied when recording stops.

5748.name: normalize_rows
5748.docs:
The rows over the tableau's columns, each with a non-negative right side, and per row
whether it was negated to get there.

3278.name: wedge_path
3278.docs: A pie or doughnut sector. Angles run clockwise from 12 o'clock, like the chart crate's.

735.name: display
735.docs: Display text with General formatting (for logs, CSV and tests).

9818.name: HfZone
9818.docs: A header or footer zone of one page.

27838.name: closure
27838.docs:
The parts reachable from `root` that aren't in `seen` yet. Fails (and keeps nothing) when the
graph reaches rewritten content, a missing or damaged part, or a size limit.

7348.name: cell_param_on
7348.docs: Like [`cell_param`], for a command that operates on `sheet` (a `Sheet!` prefix must name it).

11199.name: defaults
11199.docs: What the list holds before any function has been used.

954.name: ev_shape
954.docs: Height and width of a single-area reference or an array argument.

7421.name: formula_hidden
7421.docs:
Whether `c` has a formula or Python code that must not be shown: its cell is formatted
Hidden on a protected sheet. A spilled cell follows its anchor.

11272.name: attach_ran
11272.docs:
Attaches what the last kept step ran ([`Recorder::ran`]), within the byte budget: past it,
the step stays without it, and the recording leaves the run out and lists it as skipped.

7494.name: fill
7494.docs:
Fill: copy, AutoFill series (numbers, dates, weekdays, months, text with numbers, custom
lists), Series dialog and Flash Fill.

11345.name: next_corner_by
11345.docs:
[`Selection::next_corner`] where `stop` says where each corner takes the active cell: the
top-left cell of a merged cell the corner is in, or `None` for a corner that can't be
selected (it is skipped). Corners that end up on the active cell are one stop with it.

4951.name: paper_size
4951.docs: Paper size in points (portrait) for a paper name; unknown names fall back to Letter.

25514.name: text_function
25514.docs:
The `TEXT()` worksheet function: formats a value with a format code. Numeric text is
converted to a number first; other text and booleans (as `TRUE`/`FALSE`) go through the text
section, or are returned as is.

26822.name: decrypt_ecb
26822.docs: ECB: each block on its own. `data` must be whole blocks.

3789.name: whole
3789.docs:
A whole number from 0 to 30000 named `key`, if given. Numbers in text (`"12"`) count; anything
else is refused with a message that names the parameter.

7640.name: alternate
7640.docs:
The pattern of a Ctrl+drag, which swaps copying and extending: a single
number (which a plain drag copies) counts up by 1, and every series a
plain drag would extend (numbers, dates, lists, `Item 1`) is copied.

11.name: offset_clamped
11.docs: Moved by `(dr, dc)` and clamped to the sheet.

29511.name: dxf_id
29511.docs: Index of a differential format, adding it when new.

5170.name: store
5170.docs:
Writes `py` into the cell, which held `old`: what `python.set` and `python.output` share. The
code must fit in one cell and a table header takes none; a locked cell on a protected sheet is
refused by the edit itself.

21882.name: python
21882.docs:
Python cells: the code a cell holds, its last result, and the text forms around it (the
`PY("…",0|1)` formula of the function's syntax, and the `xl("…")` references inside it). An
xlsx file keeps the code in its Python part instead (see the xlsx crate).

27041.name: is_invisible_mark
27041.docs:
ZWNJ, ZWJ, LRM and RLM: common inside Persian words and around Arabic cells, but no evidence
either way.

6551.name: sens_num
6551.docs:
A sensitivity figure: values within `noise` of zero (rounding) print as 0, unlimited ones
as 1E+30. The noise level is local to the figure: it comes from the terms the figure is a
sum of (the rounding error of a sum scales with the sum of its terms' sizes), never from
the model's largest coefficient or gradient component, so a small price or gradient keeps
its value beside a large unrelated one, and never from the objective's value, so adding a
constant to the objective changes nothing the report shows.

13018.name: Spill
13018.docs:
Spill range operator `A1#`: the whole spill range of the dynamic array anchored at the
cell (`ANCHORARRAY` in files).

28422.name: strings
28422.docs: Excel counts booleans and errors as strings in the cache field flags.

11856.name: redo
11856.docs: The redo stack when the group began (a rollback puts it back).

31111.name: oversized_part
31111.docs:
The part of a zip package that declares more than [`MAX_PART`] unpacked bytes, with that size:
what an [`IoError::TooLarge`] from reading the package is about when one part is too large.

6843.name: get_json
6843.docs: The item under `key` as JSON (`None` when missing or not JSON).

22247.name: NEXT_SHEET_UID
22247.docs: The next [`SheetUid`]; 0 is never given out.

8151.name: HTML_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS
8151.docs: Most rows Save as Web Page writes. A sheet whose used range is taller fails instead of losing cells.

14618.name: MAX_MISSING
14618.docs: Share of the timeline's points that may be missing.

22320.name: row_top
22320.docs: Y offset (points) of the top of `row`.

30022.name: MAX_CHARS
30022.docs: Characters in one string at most (Excel's cell limit is 32,767; the SST may hold longer).

26244.name: Compound
26244.docs:
A parsed compound file: the FAT, the mini FAT and the directory, all bounds-checked.
Implemented from Microsoft's public [MS-CFB] specification.

19850.name: EquationCache
19850.docs:
The laid-out form of an equation's LaTeX source. It is derived data: rebuilt by
[`EquationCache::refresh`] whenever the source changes, never saved, and ignored when shapes
are compared. Painters read it and never lay equations out themselves, so nothing in a paint
path can reach the layout engine.

An entry answers only for the source it was built from, compared in full: a hash match alone
is not enough, so two sources whose hashes collide never share a layout. A source over
[`crate::math::MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`] never lays out, so [`EquationCache::get`] answers for it
by its length alone, with [`crate::math::SOURCE_TOO_LONG`], and an entry built from one holds
neither the source nor its hash: a painter asking every frame about a source of megabytes read
from a file does no work on it.

21231.name: children
21231.docs: The step lists inside this step (Repeat's body, If's branches).

3284.name: MAX_HTML
3284.docs: Largest clipboard HTML we look at; past this the paste uses the plain text alone.

28933.name: cell_pictures
28933.docs: Value metadata blocks, indexed by the worksheet's one-based `vm` attribute.

16145.name: lookup
16145.docs:
Looks a function up by name (case-insensitive; `_xlfn.`- and `_xlws.`-free names). A
`_xludf.` name is user-defined and never found.

13602.name: is_range_end
13602.docs:
`A1`, `$A$1`, `A`, `$A`, `1`, `$1`: a word that can end a range, so `A1.:` is a trim
reference and not a name ending in a dot.

25155.name: shown_value
25155.docs:
The number a number section shows for a non-negative `v`, as a value: what "Set precision as
displayed" stores. `None` when the section shows no digits (`"x"`) or the result isn't finite.
It uses the display's own rounding, so 1.005 with `0.00` gives 1.01, and 0.123456 with
`0.00%` gives 0.1235 (the nearest double to the decimal shown).

30314.name: color
30314.docs:
A colour index in an XF (IcvXF) or Font (IcvFont): 0-63 from the colour table, the system
and automatic colours as automatic.

3430.name: attr
3430.docs:
The value of attribute `name` in a tag's attribute text (quoted or bare). A bare attribute
without `=` has no value.

27844.name: vml
27844.docs:
The sheet's VML drawing without its notes and the form controls read into the model

11205.name: lenient

Reads a saved list leniently: known function names only, at most [`MAX`]. A value that is not
a list gives the default list, so a hand-edited or hostile `prefs.json` loses this list, never

The byte offset of the first close tag of `local` at or after `from` in `x`, with any
namespace prefix (`</controls>`, `</x:controls>`).

21596.name: password
21596.docs:
Excel-compatible password hashes for protection (ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.2.29 and §18.3.1.66
attribute sets): the legacy 16-bit hash (`password="CC1A"`) and the iterated, salted hash
(`algorithmName`, `hashValue`, `saltValue`, `spinCount`). Protection is a convenience, not
security, but verification really checks the password: an unsupported variant is refused,
never accepted.

30606.name: pending_string

The cell waiting for its String record, with its style: a blank cell isn't stored, so a

24212.name: PhoneticRun
24212.docs:
One phonetic (furigana) run of a string item (`<rPh>`): the reading `text` and the range of the
base text it annotates.

`start` and `end` are zero-based offsets into the base text (`sb` and `eb` in the file) with
`start < end`; reading keeps them within the text's length in UTF-16 code units. Behaviour
reference: ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.4.6 `rPh` and the Microsoft Learn `PhoneticRun` class.

25520.name: metrics
25520.docs:
Advance widths of the standard 14 PDF fonts, in 1/1000 em, for the printable ASCII range.

Source: the glyph advance widths ("WX" values) of Adobe's Core 14 AFM font metrics files
(Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, Times-Roman, Times-Bold, Courier). Adobe distributes those metrics
files with permission to use, copy and distribute them for any purpose ("This file and the 14
PostScript(R) AFM files it accompanies may be used, copied, and distributed for any purpose and
without charge, with or without modification, provided that all copyright notices are retained;
that the AFM files are not distributed without this file; that all modifications to this file
or any of the AFM files are prominently noted in the modified file(s); and that this paragraph
is not modified."). Only the numeric widths are reproduced here, typed in from the public
metrics; no AFM file is included. Oblique/italic faces reuse the upright widths (an
approximation that is exact for Helvetica and close for Times), and characters outside ASCII
are approximated by their base letter.

15433.name: bsearch_last
15433.docs:
Approximate match of VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, LOOKUP and MATCH: the position of the largest entry
`<= x` in data sorted ascending (`desc = false`), or of the smallest entry `>= x` in data
sorted descending. Like Excel this is a bisection over the whole vector, so on unsorted data
it answers what Excel answers rather than a linear "best" entry:
- the probe is the middle entry of the remaining window; a probe whose type differs from the
  needle (text vs number vs logical, blanks, errors) is replaced by the nearest entry of the
  needle's type below it in the window; when there is none the window moves up past it, so
  entries of other types are skipped (`LOOKUP(9.9E+307, range)` finds the last number);
- a probe equal to the needle ends the search at once (the run of equal entries that follows
  it is taken, so sorted duplicates give the last one).

Observed in Excel: `VLOOKUP(534, {"INTEGRAL";0;1;2;534;9999999999;-9999999999}, …)` finds 534,
`HLOOKUP("STRING", {"INTEGRAL","DOUBLE","BLANK","STRING","REF","AREA (rows)",<blank>}, …)`
finds "STRING" and `LOOKUP("DOUBLE", {"DOUBLE","BLANK","STRING","REF","AREA (rows)"}, …)`
finds "DOUBLE". Work is linear in the vector length at worst.

24595.name: decimal
24595.docs:
Decimal-string rounding and the General format.

Excel works with 15 significant digits, so numbers are first written with 15 significant
digits and then rounded half away from zero on that decimal string. That makes 2.675 with
"0.00" show 2.68 and 1.005 show 1.01, as in Excel, even though neither is exact in binary.

Parses bytes that aren't encrypted, then takes the workbook's macros, and the button actions

8321.name: debug
8321.docs:
The macro debugger: a run that stops between steps.

`macro.debug` starts a run that pauses before its first step, then steps, continues to the next
breakpoint, runs to a chosen step, or stops. The run lives on the session between calls (one
action per call) inside an undo group that spans them; Stop keeps the changes as one undo step
or rolls them back. While a macro is being debugged its workbook is locked: only the
debugger, queries and the commands in [`LOOKS_AROUND`] run there, and everything else, saving
included, is refused ("Finish or stop the macro first"). Other workbooks stay editable. The
debugger runs on its own, never as a step of a script or macro, and is never recorded.

30119.name: rest

16023.name: has_lambda

After an edit: each slider and spin button whose linked cell holds a number takes that number

are left untouched.

The sheet and range a sort works on: the sheet `sheet` or a `Sheet!` prefix on `range` names,

Accented Latin bytes the two code pages share, next to another high byte: Hebrew

14283.name: bessel_y01
14283.docs: Y_0 and Y_1 by Neumann series over J_k (x ≤ 25) or the asymptotic expansion.

7889.docs: The largest SYLK file read, as for other text imports: past it the file is refused.

16899.name: py

24601.name: parse
24601.docs: Format code parsing: sections, bracket tags and tokens.

22058.name: xl_calls
22058.docs:
The `xl(…)` calls in `code`, skipping comments and other string literals. A call whose first
argument isn't a plain string literal has no reference: the cells it reads are only known when
it runs.

27217.name: ink
27217.docs:
The open, solid polylines the model can represent as editable ink. This is DrawingML
geometry, not Office InkML. Unsupported geometry keeps the existing shape-import fallback.

20823.name: inputs
20823.docs: The ranges the macro works on, checked before it runs.

2876.name: TrendlineData

22131.name: PageLayout
22131.docs: Pages on paper with rulers, margins and in-place headers and footers.

8035.name: HTML_SNIFF_BYTES
8035.docs: How much of a text file is read to tell whether it is a web page.

19588.name: default_hole_size
19588.docs:
Charts saved before `hole_size` existed were drawn with a 50% hole. New charts and charts read
from XLSX set 75 explicitly (Excel's default), so only a missing JSON field keeps the old look.

28598.name: number_formats
28598.docs: Number formats used by value fields (to be registered in the styles part).

4257.name: chars_to_points
4257.docs: Excel column width in characters (of the default font's digit width, 7 px) → pixels.

15810.name: sym_inverse
15810.docs:
Inverts a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix by Gauss–Jordan on the diagonal, dropping
(zeroing) collinear variables. Returns the inverse and the dropped flags.

20969.name: name
20969.docs: The token that stands for it in step parameters (`Input`, `Rates`).

479.name: unix_now_ms
479.docs:
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC) from the system clock; `None` when the clock is unavailable.
Chrono uses the browser clock on wasm32, where the standard library clock methods trap.

31287.name: ravenrs_sheet
31287.docs:
Headless spreadsheet engine for RavenRS.

The layers, from the bottom up:

- [`base`]: cell addresses, values, errors, date serials and input parsing.
- [`numfmt`]: number format codes, General display and `TEXT()`.
- [`formula`]: the formula language: lexer, parser, printer and reference adjustment.
- [`functions`]: the worksheet function library.
- [`math`]: equations laid out from LaTeX, and their OMML form for XLSX.
- [`model`]: workbooks, sheets, copy-on-write cells, styles, tables and charts.
- [`calc`]: dependency graph, recalculation and dynamic arrays.
- [`xlsx`]: XLSX and CSV import and export.
- [`chart`]: chart data and layout into toolkit-free primitives, and sparklines.
- [`pdf`]: a small PDF writer for printing sheets.
- [`engine`]: sessions: every action is a command with an id and JSON parameters, with undo,
  clipboard, fill, sort and filter.

Nothing here draws or depends on a window, so it also runs on servers and in WebAssembly.
The engine comes from GridCraft (MIT OR Apache-2.0); see `NOTICE`.

28744.name: EXT_X14_DATA_FIELD
28744.docs: The `x14:dataField` extension (Excel 2010 show-values-as additions such as rank).

552.name: plain_number
552.docs:
A plain ASCII number: digits, with an optional `.digits` fraction when `frac` is set. Rejects
`nan`, `inf`, signs and exponents that `f64::from_str` would accept, and digits too many for a
finite number (#2163).

28817.name: REL_KIND

and the cached count are derived state, and the ones a file carries are not trusted. Cells

16102.name: is_value_arg

27655.name: mark_text

9708.name: check_new_name

8473.name: bool_param

29036.name: richdata

`vm` and metadata type IDs are one-based; every subsequent table index is zero-based.

4695.name: xs

8546.name: ALLOWED

12397.name: draw_tool
12397.docs: Draw tab tool: "" (select), "pen" or "eraser"; pen colour and width.

22715.name: minor_font_scripts
22715.docs: The body font's per-script typefaces, as (script, typeface) in file order.

26566.name: controls_of_child

The `<control>` elements one child of a `<controls>` element holds: the child itself, or those

2225.name: Swatch

9927.name: clear_output

27947.name: shape_base
27947.docs:
The number GridCraft's own VML shapes start after when they join the kept drawing

3679.name: rows_per_sample
3679.docs: The number of rows in each sample of a two-factor Anova with replication.

1136.name: stack_exhausted

2444.name: is_defined_name

6295.name: Trial
6295.docs: Evaluates a workbook with some input cells replaced, without touching the document.

7603.name: starts_with_date
7603.docs:
Whether the first cell of `src` holds a date, so a fill from it can step by days, weekdays,
months or years: a number (not a formula) shown in a date format.

11454.name: sync_headers
11454.docs:
Editing a table's header row renames the column, as in Excel: an empty or repeated header
gets a unique name written back into the cell, and structured references follow the rename.

20464.name: text_color
20464.docs: Text fill colour; `None` is the default (black in text boxes).

2517.name: expand

3825.docs: Data tab: sort, filter, remove duplicates, text to columns, data validation, outline.

6441.name: cell_name
6441.docs: A cell's name in the reports: the nearest text to its left and the nearest text above it.

28239.name: MAX_RELS
28239.docs: Most relationships read from one rels part.

1355.name: FxHasher
1355.docs: A fast, non-cryptographic hasher for cell keys (FxHash-style multiply-rotate).

5206.name: shift_sheet_features
5206.docs: Shifts everything that has a position on the sheet for an insert/delete.

24534.name: spell_calls
24534.docs: Calls of the names in `lambdas` spelled as the names are.

4044.name: go_to_names
4044.docs:
The names the Go To dialog lists, seen from sheet `sheet`: the named ranges of the workbook and
of every sheet, in alphabetical order. A name scoped to another sheet is written `Sheet2!Name`,
and the active sheet's own name hides the workbook name it shares. Hidden names and names that

7895.name: parse_value

A `K` value: `"text"` (everything between the first and the last quote, as written), a
boolean, an error or a number.

16905.name: clear_content

20756.name: table
20756.docs: Name of the table this slicer filters.

22064.name: BLOCKED

24680.name: Point

1647.name: taint

27296.name: run_props

A text run's `a:rPr` attributes (size, bold, italic) and children in schema order (outline,
fill, typeface).

9349.name: check
9349.docs:
What one step wrote over that held data when the run started: cells outside the inputs,

1720.name: run

20975.name: col_types
20975.docs: What each column must hold, first column first; columns past the list may hold anything.

6879.name: Computed

22283.name: pivots
22283.docs: PivotTables whose output lives on this sheet.

558.name: current_year
558.docs:
The year used for dates typed without one, from the system clock (browser clock on wasm).

15962.name: check_size
15962.docs: Checks that a requested result size is acceptable.

28823.docs:
Most characters kept of one script: one more than a cell's code may have, so a longer script
still fails [`PyCode::fits`] and its cell keeps only its value, with the usual warning.

8333.name: paths

Rasterises primitives to straight RGBA8 (`w*h*4` bytes) over `background`. Empty for a zero
or oversized image. Text primitives are skipped.

9641.docs:
Refuses a macro too large to keep in an xlsx file ([`stash::MAX_ITEM_CHARS`] characters of
JSON). Every command that adds or changes a macro calls [`check`], so the size of a macro kept
in the workbook doesn't make a save fail. (A clashing visible name doesn't either:

19959.name: label

27661.name: read_properties

26426.name: write_chart

8479.name: advance
8479.docs: Runs one step (`Step`), or steps until a breakpoint, the target step or the end.

9787.name: hf_sides

Left and right margins of headers and footers in layout units (the side margins, or a

11095.name: compute
11095.docs: Computes a PivotTable report from the workbook.

The VML drawing also holds a control that the sheet doesn't list and the model doesn't
hold (a check box only the drawing has): the drawing is kept for it even when no

13784.name: criteria
13784.docs: Excel criteria (COUNTIF, SUMIFS, DCOUNT…) and wildcard matching.

17635.name: margins
17635.docs: Margins in inches: left, right, top, bottom, header, footer.

6228.name: number
6228.docs:
A number read from a hidden name as JSON: a whole number as an integer, so the Solver dialog
shows 20000 and not 20000.0.

2450.name: render_sparkline
2450.docs:
Draws a sparkline into a `w`×`h` box at the origin. Gaps (`None`) break lines; column and
win/loss sparklines draw negatives in our "down" red.

28099.name: KeptSheet
28099.docs: A kept chart sheet being written: its `<sheet>` entry's fields and its new relationship id.

26864.name: StandardHeader
26864.docs: What a Standard `EncryptionInfo` holds: the key size and the password verifier.

2523.name: auto_name
2523.docs: Excel's automatic trendline name for the legend, e.g. `Linear (Sales)`.

3831.name: grow_autofilter
3831.docs:
Excel grows an AutoFilter range when a value is entered in the row right below it, in one of its columns (#2342).
A table's own filter is left to the table, and a row typed after a blank row does not count.
A formula counts before it is calculated: this runs inside the edit, ahead of the recalc.

8990.name: a1
8990.docs: `place` as A1 text, with the sheet name when it isn't the active sheet.

29553.name: typeface
29553.docs:
The typeface of `<fontScheme>/<font>/<kind>` (`latin`, `ea` or `cs`), `None` when absent or
empty (an empty typeface means "not set" and must not overwrite the default).

5212.name: delete_areas
5212.docs:
The areas a line delete/insert targets as `(first line, count)`, merged and sorted from the
last line to the first so deleting one never shifts the next. A comma-separated list
(`"3:3,7:8"`) or a multi-area selection yields several; `count` forces the single-area form.

9063.name: Approve
9063.docs: Active content (a macro) asks to run; run it again with `approve: true` to allow it.

4050.name: paste_validations
4050.docs:
Pasting validation works on ranges, as Excel stores it: the pasted rectangle is cut out of the
destination's rules (cells whose source had no rule end up with none), then each source rule
that covers part of the copied block `src` comes along as one rule over the translated parts.
`size` is one tile's (height, width) at the destination; `pasted` is all the tiles together.

7901.name: resolve
7901.docs: The 0-based index and whether it is absolute, or `None` when it falls off the sheet.

2815.name: palette
2815.docs: Workbook-theme colours for the points of pie-like charts, repeating (point `j` uses entry `j % len`); empty uses the default theme.

28464.name: par
28464.docs: The next (coarser) grouping field of the same base.

19527.name: backward
19527.docs: Forecast before the first point, in x units.

27229.name: drawing
27229.docs:
DrawingML spreadsheet drawings (`xl/drawings/drawingN.xml`): anchors, pictures, shapes,
equations and chart frames.

An equation is written as `mc:AlternateContent`: the `a14` choice is a text box holding the
equation as Office Math (`a14:m`), the fallback the same text box holding the LaTeX as plain
text. Both carry the source in `descr="gridcraft:latex:…"`, which wins on reading; without it,
Office Math in the subset `omml` reads is converted back to LaTeX.

9282.name: wrote_files
9282.docs: Files the run wrote ("step 1 (file.exportCsv)"): rolling the run back doesn't take them back.

24686.name: Slash
24686.docs: The fraction bar (only after analysis decides the section is a fraction).

4196.name: line_cells

The active sheet as CSV of raw cell values, for automation: numbers at full precision, dates and
times as ISO 8601, booleans `TRUE`/`FALSE`, errors as their text, text as stored. Save As CSV
writes displayed text instead ([`save_bytes`]) and stays the default.

1653.name: with_python
1653.docs:
Adds the dirty Python cells of the pass and their kept results: like the formulas, they
are pending until laid out, so every read path calculates them before reading them.

491.name: datetime_from_serial
491.docs: Date/time from a serial. `None` for negative or too-large serials.

22289.name: view
22289.docs: Normal, Page Layout or Page Break Preview.

28756.name: mdy
28756.docs: `3/5/2024` for a date serial (group boundary captions).

15968.name: to_sig_digits
15968.docs: `x` rounded to `sig` significant decimal digits (via decimal formatting).

28829.name: warning
28829.docs: The warning for the Python cells that kept only their value, if any.

10882.name: vpos
10882.docs: Depth of Σ Values among the row fields when it sits in Rows (two or more value fields).

9647.name: kept_name
9647.docs:
The name of the macro kept in a newer format called `name` (compared as [`find`] compares),
as the file held it. Its name is taken: a new or renamed macro with it would clash when the
newer version reads the file.

25051.name: bracket
25051.docs: Handles the content of a `[...]` tag.

4561.name: find_pivot
4561.docs: (sheet, index) of the pivot a call targets.

27667.name: delim
27667.docs: A delimiter character as a `\left`/`\right` argument.

8485.name: state
8485.docs:
Where the run is: the next step with its parameters as they would run, the step that just
ran, and what the run has changed in its workbook so far.

12409.name: text_width
12409.docs:
Measures cell text for AutoFit Column Width. Without it (CLI, MCP) AutoFit uses
[`cmd::format::approx_text_width`].

24035.name: MAX_ITERATIONS
24035.docs: The largest Maximum Iterations Excel accepts.

6234.name: options_width
6234.docs: How many cells the options row of Save Model (`={…}`, one row) spans.

3691.name: normal
3691.docs: Standard normal by the Box–Muller transform.

2456.name: coef
2456.docs: Coefficients `c0..=cd` of `Y = Σ cₖ·Xᵏ` in the transformed variables, for the equation.

14009.name: wildcard_match
14009.docs: Case-insensitive whole-text match with `*`, `?` and `~` escapes.

5072.name: Bands
5072.docs: Inclusive-start/end index spans of the pages along one axis.

28178.name: elements
28178.docs: Workbook XML elements that go right after `<sheets>` (`<externalReferences>`).

8996.name: MAX_INPUT_CELLS
8996.docs: The most cells an input may have for its content to be checked.

24400.name: phonetics
24400.docs:
Phonetic (furigana) data of shared strings (`xl/sharedStrings.xml`), one entry per string
text, so that an open + save keeps a Japanese workbook's readings. Written back next to the
`<si>` holding the same text.

Keyed by text because that is all a cell keeps of its shared string: the saved table holds
each text once (the format's `uniqueCount`), so two `<si>` items that share a base text can
only keep one reading — the reader keeps the first and warns. Empty for workbooks without
phonetic data; not present in older JSON. Modelled data (unlike [`Workbook::preserved`],
which holds unmodelled parts), so it is saved to JSON as well as to XLSX.

15463.name: masked_numbers
15463.docs: Numbers in `target` where `mask` is set (errors at matched positions propagate).

10377.name: func_caption
10377.docs:
Excel's caption verb for a function ("Sum of Sales"). Count Numbers is captioned "Count of
Sales", as Excel names it and as the XLSX reader names a value field saved without a name.

14228.name: field_headers
14228.docs: Header text for each row field (or generated) when headers are shown.

25781.name: FONT_SLOTS
25781.docs: Number of font resources a page can use.

4056.name: rewrite_python_refs
4056.docs:
Rewrites the `xl("…")` literals in every Python cell with `f`, which maps a reference held on
sheet `host` to its new form. Every reference-moving edit (insert and delete of lines or cells,
cut-move, sheet rename and delete) runs it, as it adjusts formulas. A literal is only replaced
when the reference it names changed, and text that doesn't parse is kept. A cell's cached
result is kept while its references still name the same data (a rename, a move); a reference
the edit deleted (`#REF!`), or one that grew or shrank (rows or columns inserted or deleted
inside it), leaves the result stale, so the cell is new code (`#BLOCKED!`) and the
recalculation removes its spill. A rewrite that would
make a cell's code longer than one cell holds (a longer sheet name, `Z1` becoming `AA1`) refuses
the whole edit, which then changes nothing: see [`check_python_fits`].

15609.name: modes
15609.docs: Values occurring at least twice, ordered by first occurrence, with their (equal, maximal) count.

4129.name: shape_is
4129.docs:
Whether `kind` names the shape `sh`: an equation is a shape too, and a plain shape is not an
equation, as `Sheet::object_anchor` has it for the `object.*` commands.

27235.name: dml_color
27235.docs: Colour of a DrawingML colour choice inside `e` (e.g. a `solidFill`).

9288.name: settle
9288.docs: Moves to the next enabled step: past disabled steps, finished frames and loop passes.

351.name: category_levels
351.docs:
How `categories` lays its labels out beside `values` (`None` when the values aren't a
reference: the categories' own shape decides). `None` for a plain list of labels.

1659.name: circular_read
1659.docs:
Reading `k` while it is being evaluated, with iterative calculation on: its previous value.
The formulas around the loop are the ones whose changes decide when iteration stops.

23457.name: rotation
23457.docs: Degrees -90..=90, or 255 for vertical stacked text.

27308.name: feature_bags
27308.docs:
Feature property bags ([MS-XLSX] 2.1.22, 2.3.9): how Excel stores cell checkboxes.

A checkbox is a cell format (`xf`) whose `extLst` carries an `xfComplement i="n"` element
([MS-XLSX] 2.4.99, styles extension `{C7286773-470A-42A8-94C5-96B5CB345126}`). `n` indexes the
`MappedFeaturePropertyBags` array of the `XFComplements` bag; that entry is an `XFComplement`
bag whose `XFControls` key names an `XFControls` bag, whose `CellControl` key names a
`Checkbox` bag. Bag references are zero-based indexes into the part's list of `bag` elements.

GridCraft keeps a checkbox as the `checkbox` number format in its model, so reading maps each
`xfComplement` that resolves to a `Checkbox` bag onto that format, and writing emits one chain
that every checkbox `xf` points at.

424.name: DateTime
424.docs: A calendar date and time of day.

31232.name: LegacyBinary
31232.docs: Another compound (CFB/OLE2) file: a legacy Office binary that isn't an Excel workbook.

22295.name: object_ref
22295.docs: The floating object with workbook-unique id `id` on this sheet.

4348.name: insert
4348.docs:
Insert tab: tables, charts, sparklines, pictures, shapes, hyperlinks, comments and notes,
conditional formatting (Home › Styles) and symbols.

570.name: Circ
570.docs: Circular reference that could not be resolved (shown as 0 by Excel; we keep it explicit).

12123.name: scripts_trusted
12123.docs:
Whether the scripts stored in this workbook may run (`automate.runScript`). A workbook
that arrives already carrying scripts (opened from a file) starts untrusted until the
user trusts it in this session (`automate.trustScripts`); one with no scripts starts
trusted, since any script it gains later was written here.

9580.name: content_differs
9580.docs:
Whether a write changed what the person entered: the formula, the Python code and its return
type, or the value. A Python cell replaced by its own cached value, or by other code that
shows the same `#BLOCKED!`, has changed.

13431.name: Word
13431.docs:
A reference-looking or name-looking word, possibly sheet-qualified: `A1`, `$B$2`, `A:A`
is lexed as Word(A) Colon Word(A); `Sheet1!A1` → `Sheet(Some("Sheet1"))` then `Word`.

10888.name: value_subtotals
10888.docs: Per-value subtotal lines of an item with Σ Values below it ("East Sum of Sales").

12196.name: user_dictionary
12196.docs: Words added with Add to Dictionary.

9653.name: keep_unread
9653.docs:
Keeps a macro in a newer format unread, if it is small enough to save back
([`stash::MAX_ITEM_CHARS`] characters of JSON, the size every xlsx save can write).

26365.name: ref_values
26365.docs: Values of a same-workbook reference (`Sheet1!$B$2:$B$9`), row-major.

9799.name: paper
9799.docs:
Page Layout view geometry: a sheet shown as printed pages side by side.

The view uses the print pagination ([`crate::engine::cmd::print::split_bands`]) over the sheet from
A1, so its page edges are the printed ones whenever the print area starts at A1. Pages keep
going right and down past the data ("Click to add data" pages), as far as the view needs.

Coordinates are *layout units*: sheet pixels (96 dpi) at the print scale, so a cell keeps its
sheet size and a page is `paper / scale` big. The UI multiplies by its zoom. Pages sit in a
grid with a gap around each: page `(row band, column band)` starts at
`(gap + j·(page_w + gap), gap + i·(page_h + gap))`, and its cells start at its top-left margin.

12415.name: window_title
12415.docs:
The window title: the workbook's name when it has one window, "Name:1", "Name:2"… in
opening order when it has several.

23968.name: WorkbookView
23968.docs:
The workbook window's display settings from `<workbookView>` (Excel: File › Options ›
Advanced, "Display options for this workbook"): whether the window shows the sheet tabs
and the two scroll bars, and how much of the horizontal bar the tabs take (`tabRatio`,
thousandths of the bar; the format's default is 600). XLSX I/O normalizes this
share to 0–1000, including values supplied directly through the model.

The values are modelled so an open + save keeps them — a workbook Excel saved with the
tabs hidden must not come back with them shown and the settings gone. The app does not
act on them yet and there is no Options control for them; that is the other half of
storytold/gridcraft#3057.

935.name: MAX_CELLS
935.docs: Largest array a reference may expand to.

3551.name: call
3551.docs: Calls a worksheet function on numeric arguments (and `cumulative` flags as booleans).

7402.name: round_all_constants_as_displayed
7402.docs:
Turning "Set precision as displayed" on rounds every number constant in the workbook to its
format, permanently (Excel warns "Data will permanently lose accuracy"). Formulas are rounded
by the recalculation that follows.

29200.name: dynamic_checks
29200.docs: Row-membership checks served so far, for the work cap above.

8710.name: formula_token
8710.docs:
The token for a reference inside a formula: exactly the example input, one of its columns or
rows, or a column without its first row. Other references stay as they are.

17720.name: index
17720.docs:
The 0-based place in the printed sequence of the page in page row `row` and page column
`col`, on a sheet `rows` pages tall and `cols` pages wide.

29273.name: table_name
29273.docs:
Valid table name: letters, digits, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter, `_` or `\`
(Microsoft "Names in formulas" rules).

12634.name: delete_sheet
12634.docs:
References to a deleted sheet become `#REF!`. `order` lists the sheet names (before the deletion) in tab order:
a 3-D span that loses an end sheet shrinks to the neighbouring surviving sheet, as in Excel.

6240.name: complete_from_cell
6240.docs:
A model read down from `start` must end with its options row, which Save Model always
writes last: a cell without a formula before it (a constraint cleared, say) would otherwise
end the read early and load the rows above it as the whole model, with default options.

28038.name: encode_name
28038.docs:
A folder name as a segment of a relationship target (a URI): ASCII characters a URI path
can't hold are percent-encoded, other characters are written as they are.

7548.name: Weekday
7548.docs: Monday to Friday: Saturday and Sunday are skipped.

30654.name: blank_array_followers
30654.docs:
The other cells of a legacy array formula hold only cached results: dropped, as when an
.xlsx is read, so that the formula fills its range on recalculation. If the formula itself
couldn't be imported, they keep their values.

2462.name: poly
2462.docs: The fitted polynomial at transformed `x` (Horner in u).

14015.name: database
14015.docs:
Database functions (DSUM, DCOUNT, DGET…): aggregate one field of the records of a table
that satisfy a criteria table.

The database and the criteria are arrays whose first row holds column labels. Each criteria
row is a set of conditions that must all hold (AND); a record matches when any criteria row
holds (OR). An empty criteria cell matches anything. Plain text conditions match values that
begin with the text, as in Excel's advanced filter, so an empty string matches any text. A
formula under a label that names no field is a computed criterion, which the host evaluates
for each record ([`Ctx::computed_criterion`]).

5078.name: MAX_FALLBACK_LINES
5078.docs:
Sheet pixel rectangle of an anchor.
Most source lines printed for an equation that has no layout.

3843.name: show_levels
3843.docs:
The outline's level buttons: show rows / columns down to outline level `n` (1 = only the
top-level summaries); deeper detail is hidden and its summary lines marked collapsed.

24406.name: source_dir
24406.docs:
The folder the workbook was read from, which relative paths to linked workbooks in
`preserved` are relative to. Saving into another folder rewrites them from there. Not in JSON.

28257.name: OWN_DIRS
28257.docs:
Part-name prefixes (lower case) GridCraft's writer never produces: kept parts there keep their
original names. Anything else is renamed so it can't collide with written parts.

3916.name: move_rule_formula
3916.docs:
Moves the relative references of a rule formula written for `first` so it reads the same cells from `to`
(pasting a rule); text without relative references (constants, literal lists) stays as typed.

25787.name: pdf_string_in
25787.docs:
A PDF literal string for `text` in WinAnsiEncoding, or in Symbol's encoding (where a
character Symbol lacks becomes `?`).

15615.name: kth
15615.docs: k-th largest (k is rounded up like Excel).

18231.name: connection_id
18231.docs: The connection (`xl/connections.xml`) an XML table is bound through.

4135.name: anchors_of
4135.docs: The anchors of every object of `kind` on the sheet; under `equation`, only the equations.

25933.name: clip_rect
25933.docs: Intersects the clip with a rectangle (until the next [`Page::restore`]).

27241.name: LATEX_DESCR
27241.docs:
The `descr` prefix that carries an equation's LaTeX source, as
`gridcraft:latex:<marker>:<source>`: the marker is [`crate::xlsx::omml::body_marker`] of the text
body written beside it, 16 hex digits.

15761.name: MAX_REGRESSION_WORK
15761.docs: Most multiply-adds (rows × k²) a regression may spend building its normal equations.

26079.name: pdf_text_string
26079.docs:
A PDF text string (document Info entries) for `text`: a literal `( … )` for printable ASCII,
otherwise UTF-16BE with a byte-order mark as a hex string (ISO 32000-1 7.9.2.2).

10748.name: leaf
10748.docs: A category of a PivotChart: an innermost (or collapsed) item.

22301.name: object_anchors
22301.docs:
Every floating object's anchor in a fixed order (charts, images, shapes, slicers, controls)
that [`Sheet::object_anchors_mut`] repeats, so a pass can compute new anchors from the old
ones and write them back in step.

8205.name: image_size
8205.docs: Pixel size of a PNG or JPEG from its header.

19904.name: refresh
19904.docs: Lays `src` out again unless the cache already holds its layout. True when it did.

7116.name: cell_list
7116.docs: Cells of `"B2:B4,D1"` (row-major per area, duplicates removed), at most `cap`.

26371.name: split_array_items
26371.docs:
Splits the inside of an array constant on `,` and `;` outside double quotes; inside quotes `""` is a literal quote.
Unquoted items are trimmed; quoted ones keep the text between the quotes and drop the spaces around them.

8424.name: put_back_view
8424.docs:
Puts back the active sheet and the selections where the run left them, so the next step runs
where `macro.run` would run it, however the person looked around meanwhile.

27679.name: group_char
27679.docs: `m:groupChr`: a brace over or under its content.

26444.name: style_xml
26444.docs: The chart style part a chartex part comes with: every element at its plain default.

9805.name: page_x
9805.docs: Left edge of page column `j` / top edge of page row `i`.

25209.name: MAX_CODE_LEN
25209.docs: Longer codes are parsed every time and never stored.

3557.name: Grid
3557.docs: A report: values by (row, col) relative to its top-left corner.

6246.name: shape
6246.docs: Constraint values in the `≤ 0` / `= 0` form, and the objective to minimise.

28044.name: root
28044.docs: Package-root relationships (type, target, external), added when `_rels/.rels` is written.

11405.name: parse_style_name
11405.docs: (family, number) from a style name, e.g. `TableStyleMedium2` → ("Medium", 2).

26809.name: standard_key
26809.docs:
The Standard encryption key ([MS-OFFCRYPTO] 2.3.4.7): SHA-1 iterated 50,000 times, the
block-0 hash, then the 0x36 / 0x5C expansion, truncated to `key_len`.

24266.name: font_id
24266.docs:
`fontId`: a required attribute, an index into the style sheet's fonts. A file without one
gets 0 — the Normal style's font, which an out-of-range index falls back to anyway.

3776.name: pattern
3776.docs:
The numbers of a patterned sequence: `from` to `to` in steps, each number repeated, the whole
sequence repeated.

14094.name: day_seconds
14094.docs: Seconds into the day, rounded to the nearest second.

29571.name: NS_THREADED
29571.docs: Namespace of the threaded comments and persons parts ([MS-XLSX]).

15475.name: matrix
15475.docs: A numeric matrix (every element must be a number, else `#VALUE!`).

5230.name: reapply_slicer
5230.docs: Writes the slicer's current selection into the sheet filter and re-applies it.

25793.name: dash_values
25793.docs:
The entries of a dash array (`[on, off, …]`, at most 8). A pattern the PDF specification
forbids (any non-finite entry, or no entry that survives rounding to a positive number) is
replaced by an empty array, i.e. a solid line.

attrs.other: #[error("internal error in `{0}` (the workbook was kept as it was): {1}")]

6611.name: nonlinear_body
6611.docs: GRG Nonlinear: reduced gradients and the binding rows' Lagrange multipliers.

28409.name: pivot
28409.docs:
PivotTables: pivot cache definitions and records (ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.10.1) and PivotTable
definitions (§18.10.1.73), written from the model's [`PivotTable`]s and read back into them.
