Writing: one cache per PivotTable, with a records snapshot of the source list (omitted, with
`saveData="0"`, for very large sources) and `refreshOnLoad="1"` so a reader recomputes the
report from the source on open. Fields used on an axis get shared items (or, for date
grouping, `fieldGroup` group items) so the table's `<items>` can refer to them. The report
cells the engine wrote stay on the sheet as plain cells.

Reading: the cache's source and field names plus the table's areas, functions, show-values-as,
layout flags, grand totals and style become a model [`PivotTable`]. Anything we don't model
(OLAP sources, calculated fields, numeric grouping…) becomes a warning.

290.name: addr
290.docs:
Cell and range addresses.

Internally rows and columns are 0-based (`A1` = row 0, col 0). The sheet is 1,048,576 rows by
16,384 columns (`XFD1048576`), like Excel.

4141.name: has_scripts
4141.docs: Whether `wb` carries GridCraft scripts (a workbook opened with them starts untrusted).

27247.name: holds_written_text
27247.docs:
Whether a body without Office Math still holds the text the writer wrote for `src`: the same
paragraphs, read back through the same parser. The marker joins run text across paragraphs,
so a paragraph split that changes no character passes it; the text does not.

28555.name: Cache
28555.docs: A cache built from a PivotTable's source.

10608.name: label_col
10608.docs: Grid column holding the innermost row labels (`None` without row fields).

27320.name: mentions_dummy_function
27320.docs: Whether `text` may hold Google Sheets' export wrapper: a cheap test before parsing.

4287.name: merge_json
4287.docs: Deep-merges `patch` into `base` (objects merge, everything else replaces).

22307.name: set_cell
22307.docs: Replaces content, removing any picture at this address. Style-only edits use set_style.

30009.name: anchor
30009.docs:
One end of a reference. In `relative` (RgceLocRel) form the relative parts are offsets
from `base`, wrapped into the BIFF8 grid (65,536 × 256).

13370.name: input
13370.docs: Localized aliases accepted at user-entry boundaries; file syntax stays English.

9665.name: unique
9665.docs: The first of `name`, `name (2)`, `name (3)`… not in use.

7122.name: run
7122.docs: Sets `sets` to constants, recalculates their dependents and reads `reads`.

28920.name: write
28920.docs:
The Python part holding `scripts`, in order. Only written when there is at least one: the
format requires one `pythonScript` in `pythonScripts`.

3344.name: OpenCell
3344.docs: A cell whose closing tag hasn't been seen yet.

14897.name: interpolate
14897.docs:
Missing points become the straight line between their known neighbours (the nearest known
value at either end).

801.name: compare
801.docs:
Excel's comparison for `=`, `<`… operators. Text compares case-insensitively; empty acts as
0, "" or FALSE depending on the other side. Errors are handled by the caller.

9811.name: page_col_at
9811.docs: Page column under `x` (the nearest one in gaps).

13735.name: normalize_function_name
13735.docs:
`_xlfn.XLOOKUP` → `XLOOKUP`. `_xludf.` is kept (`_xludf.SUM`): it marks a user-defined
function, never the built-in of the same name, and files need it back.

7341.name: anchor_mode_name
7341.docs: The wire name of an anchor mode (matches the `mode` param of [`anchor_mode_param`]).

17659.name: hf
17659.docs: The header (`footer` false) or footer of a page kind.

7414.name: parsed
7414.docs: Parsed number formats are cached by code.

11265.name: record
11265.docs:
The recording buffer: the commands a person (or an agent) ran while recording, each with the
document, sheet and selection it ran in.

Only top-level calls are kept. A command that runs other commands (Custom Views › Show, a
script) is one step, so playing the recording back does not run the inner commands twice. The
buffer is separate from the journal, so trimming the journal never loses recorded steps, and
secret parameters are left out as they are in the journal ([`crate::engine::cmd::journal_params`]).

12573.name: Move
12573.docs: Cut-paste of a block: references into `from` now point into the block at `to` (top-left).

7487.name: ValuesOnly
7487.docs: Fill Without Formatting: extends like a plain drag, the targets keep their formats.

11338.name: moving_end
11338.docs: The corner of the current area opposite the anchor: the end that Shift+arrows move.

4944.name: MAX_SECTION_BYTES
4944.docs:
Most bytes one section's expanded text may hold. A code like `&A` adds the whole sheet name
(or file path) each time it appears, and a JSON workbook's names have no length limit.

16497.name: alt
16497.docs: A plainer character to draw when no font has `ch` (`R` for `ℝ`), before giving up.

25653.name: styled
25653.docs: The face of `family` with the given weight and slant.

1312.name: round_value
1312.docs: Like [`DisplayedPrecision::round`] for a value: only numbers change.

24418.name: lambda_names
24418.docs: Names of the defined names holding a LAMBDA (callable like functions).

29577.name: add_raw
29577.docs: Adds a relationship with its complete type URI, internal or external (kept content).

19332.name: secondary
19332.docs: Combo charts: this series drawn as a line on the secondary axis.

6544.name: write_reports
6544.docs: Inserts prepared reports before the model's sheet, which stays active.

21948.name: convertible
21948.docs: Whether `value` is the result converted to cells.

1458.name: Intervals
1458.docs:
Row intervals `[r0, r1]`, each with a payload, answering "which intervals overlap rows
`a..=b`?" in O(log n + k).

The intervals are sorted by start with an implicit segment tree of their largest end, so a query
only descends into subtrees that hold a match. Removals mark entries dead (re-inserting one
revives it); insertions wait in a small sorted set. [`Intervals::settle`] merges them and drops
dead entries once either grows, so mutations cost O(log n) amortised.

223.name: a1
223.docs: `A1:B2`, `A1` for single cells, `1:3` for full rows, `A:C` for full columns.

4074.name: filtered_rows
4074.docs: The rows of `range` an applied filter hides (rows hidden by hand are not among them).

4147.name: stop_action
4147.docs: Redo work there again. A macro being debugged on that workbook is stopped with them.

27326.name: ods
27326.docs:
Data-only OpenDocument Spreadsheet import. Formula caches become constants; styles and
other ODF features are deliberately not translated. All fixtures are authored in Rust.
Format reference: ODF 1.3, part 3, sections 6.1 and 9.1:
<https://docs.oasis-open.org/office/OpenDocument/v1.3/os/part3-schema/OpenDocument-v1.3-os-part3-schema.html>.

11995.name: new
11995.docs:
A document for `wb`, which came from where `trust` says: [`Trust::FromFile`] for anything
read from bytes (a file, a download, a recovery copy), [`Trust::Local`] only for a workbook
made in this session.

22313.name: has_filter_button
22313.docs: Whether this cell has a table or ordinary AutoFilter dropdown.

4366.name: MAX_CHART_CELLS
4366.docs: Most cells a chart's source block may span (bounds the series it builds).

9525.name: Mode
9525.docs: In-cell edit mode as shown in the status bar.

14684.name: Aggregate
14684.docs: Duplicate time stamps are combined with this function.

4439.name: Recorder
4439.docs: The steps recorded since recording started.

30161.name: styles
30161.docs:
Cell formatting in a BIFF8 Workbook stream, from [MS-XLS]: Font (2.4.122), XF (2.4.353) with
CellXF (2.5.91), Palette (2.4.188) and Style (2.4.269). Every XF is
decoded on its own: a cell XF stores its complete formatting (the fAtr* bits only say whether
later changes to the parent style propagate), so nothing is inherited from `ixfParent`.

3277.name: paint
3277.docs: Fill and stroke attributes of an open shape element; the caller closes it.

734.name: to_bool
734.docs: Coercion to a boolean as `IF` does it.

807.name: sci_text
807.docs: Scientific text like `1.23456789012346E+15` with up to `sig` significant digits.

26456.name: MAX_CONTROLS
26456.docs: The most controls read from one sheet.

9817.name: hf_zone_at
9817.docs:
The header or footer section under the point: the top or bottom margin of a page, split
into thirds between the header and footer side margins.

18827.name: size_pt
18827.docs: The shape's width and height in points (the VML style's `width`/`height`), when given.

25294.name: Special
25294.docs: Zip codes, phone numbers, social security numbers.

7347.name: cell_param
7347.docs:
A single-cell parameter. Absent or null is `Ok(None)` (callers default it); a value that is not
a cell reference, or that names a sheet other than the active one, is an error rather than a
silent fallback to some other cell.

11198.name: SCAN_BUDGET
11198.docs: The most formulas read from one command: a large paste needs only its last few.

953.name: resizes_sum_range
953.docs: SUMIF and AVERAGEIF with a sum range: Excel sizes the sum range like the criteria range.

12506.name: adjust
12506.docs:
Reference adjustment: copying formulas, inserting/deleting rows and columns, moving cells,
renaming and deleting sheets.

7420.name: edit_text
7420.docs:
What the cell editor and the formula bar start from. Same as `Cell::input_text`, except that a
constant number in a date or time format is shown as a date (as the grid shows it), not as its
serial. When the formatted text would not read back as the same date (for example
`dddd, mmmm d`), an ISO `yyyy-mm-dd` (with `hh:mm:ss` for a time of day; just `hh:mm:ss`
for a time alone) is used instead, and if even that would not read back, the serial.

11271.name: push
11271.docs: Adds a step, or counts it as dropped once the buffer is full; `true` when it was kept.

12579.name: DeleteCells
12579.docs:
Delete Cells shifting up (`Rows`) or left (`Cols`): `range` goes and the cells below
(right of) it move back by its height (width), within its columns (rows) only.

7493.name: extends_series
7493.docs: The modes that continue the source's series rather than copy it.

11344.name: next_corner
11344.docs:
Ctrl+. (Next Corner of Selection): the active cell moves clockwise to the next corner of
the current area (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left) and becomes the anchor,
so Shift+arrows then move the opposite corner. The area stays selected. From a cell that
isn't a corner the next corner is the top-left one; a single cell stays where it is.

4950.name: DENSE_BLOCK
4950.docs: Cells in a page block above which only stored cells are visited (not every grid position).

25513.name: format_value
25513.docs: Formats a cell value for display.

15341.name: pmt_calc
15341.docs:
The payment per period. `(1 + rate)^nper` comes from `nper * ln_1p(rate)` and `p - 1` from
`exp_m1`: rounding `1 + rate` first throws away the low bits of a small rate, which left PMT up to
about 1000 ULPs from Excel (observed over 400 synthetic probes; this form is within 4). A loan
schedule's last `IF(p - SUM(principal) > 0, ...)` turns on those bits. Excel gives #NUM! for a
rate of -1 or less, and -pv*rate (no divide) once `(1 + rate)^nper` overflows.

17957.name: size
17957.docs: Size in pixels at 96 dpi; `None` = default (rows auto-fit to content).

29510.name: write_styles
29510.docs:
`styles.xml` for the workbook: one cell format per model style, in `StyleId` order (so a
cell's `s` attribute is its style id), plus the given differential formats.
`extra_fmts` are number formats used outside cell styles (PivotTable value fields); the
returned map gives the id of every custom format written.

11563.name: from_json
11563.docs:
Reads `window` or `doc` from a JSON object (control channel envelopes, MCP arguments).
Neither present is [`Target::Active`]; a value that isn't an id is an error.

21881.name: CHUNK_CHARS
21881.docs: Characters in one string literal of a `PY(…)` formula (Excel's limit for a literal).

3934.name: ink_width
3934.docs: Ink width is stored in the red channel of `fill` (shapes have no width field).

6550.name: sensitivity_refusal
6550.docs: Why a model has no Sensitivity report (`None` when it has one).

6623.name: LP_WORK
6623.docs: Most simplex pivots × tableau cells per solve.

4080.name: PADDING
4080.docs: Space between an equation's frame and its content, in sheet pixels.

29729.name: write_xlsx_named
29729.docs:
Writes the workbook for the file `book_name` (a bare file name). A PivotChart is bound to its
PivotTable in Excel only when its link starts with the workbook in brackets.

4153.name: keep_view_modes
4153.docs:
Normal, Page Layout and Page Break Preview belong to the window, not to the edits: Excel doesn't
undo a switch between them, and `set_view` is no undo step. So undo and redo keep each sheet's
current view when they swap in another snapshot of the workbook, and a view kept this way
doesn't make a saved workbook dirty.

31110.name: read_xlsx
31110.docs:
Reads an `.xlsx` / `.xlsm` / `.xltx` / `.xltm` package (the workbook part is found through the
package relationships, so every main-part content type is accepted).

13309.name: FormulaLocale
13309.docs:
Formula-entry syntax selected by the interface language. Other interface languages
currently use the canonical English function table until a translation table is supplied.

14617.name: MAX_SEASON
14617.docs: Longest seasonality Excel supports (hours in a year).

4372.name: update_data_table
4372.docs: Shared by Chart Properties and Add Chart Element; no separate UI state.

6988.name: Key
6988.docs: A row/column key: a position or a label (matched case-insensitively).

4445.name: pivot
4445.docs:
PivotTable commands (Insert › PivotTable, PivotTable Analyze, PivotTable Design, Data ›
Refresh All). Every change re-renders the report as one undo step.

`pivot?` parameters name a PivotTable (name or numeric id); by default it is the pivot whose
report contains the active cell, else the last pivot on the active sheet.

19849.name: math
19849.docs: An equation's layout, rebuilt from `text` and never saved.

21157.name: breakpoint
21157.docs: The debugger stops before this step.

21230.name: Stop
21230.docs: Ends the run with a message. The changes made so far are kept, or undone with `rollback`.

3283.name: engine
3283.docs:
The GridCraft engine façade.

Every user-visible action is a command with a stable id (`cell.set`, `home.bold`,
`data.sortAscending`…) and JSON parameters. The egui UI, the CLI, the control channel and MCP
all go through [`Session::execute`], so every action is scriptable and journaled.

28932.name: num_fmts
28932.docs: Custom number formats from the styles part, by id.

16144.name: functions
16144.docs:
GridCraft worksheet function library.

Every function is described by a [`FnSpec`] (name, arity, category, which parameters take
scalars, a signature and a one-line description) and implemented as a plain Rust function over
already-evaluated arguments. The calculation engine looks functions up by name with
[`lookup`] and invokes them through [`call`], which applies Excel's automatic array lifting:
passing an array where a scalar is expected evaluates the function once per element.

Special forms that need references, laziness or hidden-row information (ROW, OFFSET,
INDIRECT, LET, LAMBDA, SUBTOTAL, AGGREGATE, TEXT…) are evaluated by the host; this crate
exports [`aggregate_values`] for SUBTOTAL/AGGREGATE.

27697.name: rels
27697.docs:
Relationships of a part (`xl/workbook.xml` → `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels`). Missing or
broken rels parts give an empty list.

13601.name: lexer
13601.docs:
Tokenizer for Excel formulas (A1 style, canonical or selected UI separators).

Token spans are byte offsets into the source, which the editor uses to colour references.

25154.name: scientific_parts
25154.docs:
Scientific notation of a non-negative `x` with `int_count` integer and `frac_count` fraction
placeholders: the exponent (a multiple of the integer placeholder count, engineering style)
and the mantissa's integer and fraction digits.

26462.name: corners
26462.docs: The two corners of a control: ((from, dx, dy), (to, dx, dy)), offsets in sheet pixels.

30313.name: read_font
30313.docs: Font record fields up to the name; `None` if the record is too short for them.

9823.name: row_band
9823.docs: Rows `(first, last)` of a page row and columns of a page column.

12439.name: document_index
12439.docs: Where the open workbook with this [`DocState::uid`] is in [`Session::documents`].

20141.name: value
20141.docs: The current value of a slider or spin button (the linked cell holds it too).

3502.name: numbers
3502.docs:
The numbers of a variable; blanks are skipped when `skip_blank`, anything else that isn't a
number is an error.

11204.name: note
11204.docs:
Moves the functions that the formulas a command entered call to the front of `recent`. The
last formulas are read first (they are the most recent), within [`SCAN_BUDGET`].

7426.name: clipboard_range
7426.docs: The existing plain-text clipboard limit, shared with its HTML representation.

27989.name: open_tag
27989.docs: The byte offset of the first open tag of `local` in `x`, with any namespace prefix.

25519.name: fold
25519.docs:
Maps a non-ASCII character to an ASCII character of similar width, or `None` to use the
font's default width.

8880.name: is_general_key
8880.docs:
Reference keys that other commands use for plain words: `to` is a replacement word in
Review › Change Spelling, `area` is `row` or `column` in a pivot field move. Under these a
bare `Row` or `Column` stays text; `Row.col(2)`, `{{Row}}` or `{"$ref": "Row"}` is the token.

3794.name: Anchor
3794.docs: Position of a floating object: top-left cell plus offset, size in points.

26900.name: standard_header
26900.docs: `info` starts after the version: flags, header size, header, verifier.

15420.name: VALUE_ARGS
15420.docs:
Value-parameter masks (see [`FnSpec::value_args`]), observed in Excel 365: a reference to more
than one cell at these positions gives `#VALUE!` in dynamic-array and legacy formulas alike (no
implicit intersection), while array constants and computed arrays lift. Range parameters
(holidays, schedules, cash flows, coefficients) and the WORKDAY.INTL/NETWORKDAYS.INTL weekend
(which lifts a range) are `false`.

21887.name: stale
21887.docs:
The cell's inputs changed while calculation was manual: its value is out of date until
the workbook is calculated.

3940.name: input_to_cell
3940.docs:
What typing `input` into a cell produces (constant or formula, plus an automatic number
format). Inherits the destination's cell, row or column style, including its number
format, before parsing. Errors when the formula can't be parsed.

27046.name: sniff_delimiter
27046.docs:
Picks comma, semicolon or tab: the candidate with the most consistent count per line
(outside quotes) over the first non-blank lines. A candidate must appear on every such line, otherwise comma wins.

1470.name: query
1470.docs:
Calls `f` for every interval overlapping rows `a..=b` (`r0 <= b && r1 >= a`). Returns the
number of tree nodes visited.

30970.name: PHONETIC_KINDS
30970.docs:
`<phoneticPr>` attributes (ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.4.7 `CT_PhoneticPr`: `fontId` is required,
`type`, `alignment`). `type` and `alignment` are kept only when they are values §18.18.57
`ST_PhoneticType` / §18.18.56 `ST_PhoneticAlignment` define, so a damaged file cannot make the
saved file invalid; a missing or unusable `fontId` becomes 0, the Normal style's font, which an
out-of-range index falls back to anyway.
`ST_PhoneticType` (ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.18.57), as `phoneticPr/@type` may write them.

4086.name: lay_out
4086.docs: `latex` laid out, or a readable error with the position of the problem.

29735.name: MAX_ARRAY
29735.docs: Values in one array constant at most.

4159.name: window_list
4159.docs:
The windows as scripts and the Switch Windows lists see them:
`[{window, doc, index, title, dirty, active, hidden}]`, `index` being the workbook's
position in [`Session::documents`].

31116.name: from_path
31116.docs: The kind a file name's extension asks for; anything else is a plain workbook.

27338.name: read_ods
27338.docs:
Imports ODS sheets, typed values, displayed text and merges. Cached formula results are
imported as constants, so editing their inputs does not recalculate the original formula.
Always inspect the returned warnings. Saving to ODS is not supported.

9464.name: conflicts
9464.docs: Written cells that hold data now.

4378.name: validate_cell_picture
4378.docs: Validate before mutating the workbook; header dimensions alone do not prove the pixels decode.

30027.name: Record
30027.docs: One record and the payloads of the `Continue` records that follow it.

9537.name: Saved
9537.docs:
Session state a dry run may touch, put back afterwards. The workbook, its selection and its
history are put back by the dry run's undo group.

26249.name: has_root_stream
26249.docs: Whether the root storage holds a stream called `name`, without reading it.

28938.name: python
28938.docs: The code of the workbook's Python cells, from its Python part.

16150.name: to_omml
16150.docs:
`latex` as an `<m:oMath>` element (prefix `m` for the OMML namespace and `a` for DrawingML,
declared by the caller), with runs at `size_pt` points in the `ink` colour (none: the
paragraph's own).

30319.name: num_fmt
30319.docs: The number format an XF names: a custom format, else a built-in one, else General.

4743.name: Point
4743.docs: A point in page coordinates, measured from the top-left corner.

12445.name: close_document
12445.docs: Closes a workbook and its windows; the most recently active remaining window comes forward.

13753.name: sheet_split
13753.docs:
Splits a sheet-qualified name at its last `!` outside brackets. A `!` inside brackets
belongs to a structured reference's column (`Table1[Done!]`, `Table1[#REF!]`).

11210.name: NOT_RECORDED
11210.docs:
Commands never recorded: recovery actions and the debugger, not steps of the person's work. A
recording that replayed Stop Action would stop the run it is a step of, and the debugger runs
on its own, never as a step of a script or macro.

26614.name: unlisted_kept
26614.docs:
Whether a VML shape the sheet doesn't list is a control that only pass-through can keep: it
has client data that is neither a note (GridCraft writes notes) nor an embedded object's
picture (`Pict`, which means nothing without its sheet entry).

27922.name: rel_id_attr
27922.docs: The `r:id` of an element (an `id` attribute with a namespace prefix).

21528.name: MAX_SPIN_COUNT
21528.docs:
Largest spin count accepted when verifying (the documented maximum); a file asking for more
would only make verification hang.

4889.name: split_header_footer
4889.docs:
Splits a header/footer string into its raw left, centre and right sections (codes kept).
Text before the first `&L`/`&C`/`&R` belongs to the centre, as when printing.

2346.name: max_backward
2346.docs: Longest backward forecast among `s`'s regression trendlines.

21601.name: PreservedRel
21601.docs:
A relationship from an owning part (the package root, the workbook or a sheet, or a kept part)
to a kept part or to an external target.

30611.name: unsupported
30611.docs: Records why a formula was kept as its value (each reason once).

25525.name: symbol_width
25525.docs: The advance width of code `code` in 1/1000 em, or `None` for an empty slot.

1184.name: xlookup
1184.docs:
XLOOKUP whose result range is a reference returns a reference, as in Excel, so that it can
end a range (`SUM(XLOOKUP(a,…):XLOOKUP(b,…))`) or feed CELL. Everything else (arrays of
lookup values, array arguments, errors) goes to the library function.

3800.name: write_link
3800.docs:
Writes `value` to the linked cell through `cell.set` (nothing without a link, or when the cell
already shows `value`, formula or not: Format Control's OK sends the value back every time, and
a write that changes nothing must not turn a formula into a constant or fail on a locked cell
of a protected sheet; a real change replaces a formula with the constant, as in Excel).

21820.name: elements
21820.docs: Owner XML elements that refer to kept parts.

29522.name: col_width_to_px
29522.docs: Column width as stored in a file (characters including padding) → model width (px).

15426.name: scan_len
15426.docs:
The length of the longest vector a lifted call of `spec` searches per needle: 0 unless `spec`
is one of the [`SCANS`] lookups and a non-lifted argument is an array.

27052.name: DayFirst
27052.docs: A value reads only day first (`31/05/2026`), none reads only month first.

4019.name: range_move
4019.docs:
Drag and drop (dragging the selection's border): moves `range` so its top-left cell lands on
`to`, as Cut and Paste would. Like Excel, it asks before replacing cells that hold data or show a
spilled value (other than the moved cells themselves); run it again with `overwrite: true` to replace them. A
refused or failed move leaves the clipboard as it was.

29668.name: book_name
29668.docs: The workbook's file name, which a PivotChart's link to its PivotTable names in brackets.

4092.name: source_excerpt
4092.docs:
The first [`crate::math::MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`] bytes of an equation's source, cut at a char
boundary. A longer source never lays out (the editor refuses it, and a file can carry one of
megabytes), so what shows it as text, the sheet painter and the PDF fallback, shows this much
and does no work on the rest.

27198.name: numeric_date
27198.docs:
A numeric date written with `/` or `-`, with the serial it has read day first and month first.
`None` when the field isn't such a date (including ISO `yyyy-mm-dd`, month names and dots,
which read one way and keep the input parser).

15718.name: x
15718.docs: n rows of k predictor values.

1622.name: MAX_NESTED
1622.docs:
Formulas a formula may calculate on demand one inside the other (each needing one another's
value before it is done). Each level takes stack, so a chain deeper than this is suspended and
calculated from the top instead (see [`PassHost::calculate`]): long dependency chains calculate
whatever order they come in, with bounded stack.

9397.name: executed
9397.docs:
Steps executed and bytes of parameters passed by the end of the dry run that made this
footprint (the run's one budget).

13248.name: Invoke
13248.docs: Calling the result of an expression, e.g. `LAMBDA(x,x+1)(2)`.

22258.name: default_col_width
22258.docs: Default column width and row height in pixels at 96 dpi (a file stores row heights in points).

4311.name: single_row_totals
4311.docs: One row: its total goes in its last cell when that is empty, else just after it.

15864.name: format_fixed
15864.docs: Formats `x` (already rounded) with `decimals` places and optional thousands separators.

26182.name: MAX_REG_SECT
26182.docs: Sector ids at or above this are markers (free, end of chain, FAT/DIFAT sector), not sectors.

15937.name: expand_capped
15937.docs:
Append a match's replacement to `out`, piece by piece; `None` once `out` would pass `limit`
bytes, before anything that long is built (#2162).

1841.name: nice_scale
1841.docs:
Picks a "nice" scale (steps of 1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ, 4–9 gridlines) covering `lo..=hi`.

`force_zero` always includes 0 (columns, bars, areas). Otherwise 0 is still included when the
data sits reasonably close to it (min below 5/6 of max), like common spreadsheet behaviour.
A little headroom is added past the data so the extreme value doesn't touch the frame.

4457.name: show_details
4457.docs:
Show Details (double-click a value cell): the source records behind it, as values with their
column's number format, under the source headers on a new sheet.

28871.name: py_call
28871.docs:
`PY(index, 0|1, params…)`, as a file's formula holds it: the index, whether the return type is
a Python object, and the parameters. `None` for anything else (the code in a string literal
is [`PyCode::from_formula`]'s form).

17464.name: values_on_rows
17464.docs:
The Σ Values pseudo-field (it exists with two or more value fields) sits in Rows rather
than Columns (Excel's "values on rows").

7219.name: menu
7219.docs: Ribbon/menu placement, e.g. `["Home", "Font"]`. Empty = not in menus.

18772.name: note_box
18772.docs:
Where the note's box sits and how big it is, as read from the file; `None` (a note made
here, or a file without the shape) writes the default box next to the cell.

12451.name: abort_groups
12451.docs:
Stops the running action on the document with uid `doc`: every undo group open on it is
rolled back as [`Session::group_rollback`] does, putting back the workbook, selection, undo
and redo history as they were when the outermost one began. Their tokens are then spent
(ending or rolling one back reports that it has already ended). Returns whether a group
was open. `automate.stopAction` runs it on the active document.

21461.name: Ask
21461.docs: Ask first: overwrite, shift the data down or right, or cancel. Programmatic runs fail.

971.name: FULL_SIZE_CELLS
971.docs: References up to this many cells (one whole row) are always read at their full size.

26620.name: vml_anchor
26620.docs:
A VML `x:Anchor` (`LeftColumn, LeftOffset, TopRow, TopOffset, RightColumn, RightOffset,
BottomRow, BottomOffset`, offsets in pixels).

2279.name: point_color
2279.docs: Colour of point `j` for charts that colour by point (pie, doughnut, treemap, sunburst).

27928.name: shape_numbers
27928.docs: Shape numbers (`_x0000_s1025` → 1025) used in VML text.

9981.name: PivotValue
9981.docs: A field in the Values area.

25458.name: is_text
25458.docs: True for a pure text format such as `@`.

4968.name: manual_breaks
4968.docs: Manual page breaks apply (they don't when the sheet is fitted to pages).

2425.name: finalize
2425.docs: Drops non-finite primitives and clamps every coordinate into the `w`×`h` box.

3733.name: pmf_table
3733.docs:
The probabilities of a distribution on 0, 1, 2 … `last`, as (first outcome, probabilities of
first, first + 1, …), from its probability `at_mode` at `mode`, its most likely outcome, and
`ratio`(k) = pmf(k + 1) / pmf(k). Each term is one multiplication of its neighbour towards the
mode, so no worksheet function runs per outcome, and the terms only shrink away from the mode,
so nothing underflows before the terms that matter. The left tail ends where its terms vanish,
the right tail once the cumulative probability reaches 1 within f64 resolution (every later
draw would map to the last outcome). The table is as wide as the distribution's effective
support, not as `last`: Binomial(1,000,000, 0.5) takes about 23,000 entries, not 1,000,001.

15286.name: MAX_QUASI
15286.docs: Most quasi-coupon periods an odd period may span (the date range allows ~32,400 quarters).

8892.name: name_end
8892.docs:
Where the name ends in `run`, the text after `Name:` up to the first character a name can't
hold: at the end or at a period, the longest choice that is a defined name or table. When
none is, the name ends before the first method (`Nope.cell`), so the error names it.

15359.name: dated_flows
15359.docs: Values and dates for XNPV/XIRR: both must be numeric and of equal length.

30763.name: metadata
30763.docs:
The two package metadata parts are flat, namespace-qualified XML documents. Keep only
direct child entries, and reject truncated XML instead of guessing a partial relationship.

28220.name: reachable
28220.docs: The part names reachable from `root` through kept parts' relationships (normalized).

15432.name: find_exact
15432.docs: Exact search (first match, or last when `reverse`). Text needles match wildcards when `wild`.

14270.name: distinct_keys
14270.docs:
Distinct keys in first-seen order, then sorted (by `sort` = ±column index within the key; 0
keeps all keys ascending).

10492.name: Item
10492.docs: Item row; `true` for a parent item (bold).

27204.name: sample_records
27204.docs: The first records of the file, bounded by rows and bytes, for date-order inference.

28512.name: formula
28512.docs: A calculated field's formula (without `=`); such fields aren't database fields.

4171.name: stash_map
4171.docs: Like `stash_get`, for the name-keyed lists (views, scripts): a stored value that is not a JSON object is treated as empty.

8022.name: open_bytes
8022.docs:
Parses a file's bytes into a workbook. `name` picks the format by extension when the bytes
don't say. An encrypted workbook needs [`open_bytes_with_password`].

20883.name: Macros
20883.docs:
The macros of a workbook. Workbook snapshots share the list until one of them changes it, so
an undo entry or a copy made for a cell edit holds the same list rather than a copy of every
step. Reads go through `Deref` to the list; a write through `DerefMut` first copies the list
when another snapshot shares it.

11946.name: selected
11946.docs:
The range as copied, before whole rows/columns were trimmed to the used range
(Insert Copied Cells inserts whole lines for a row or column copy).

1701.name: array_area
1701.docs: The area an array anchored at `anchor` covers.

14562.name: base_source
14562.docs: Source text of a base-conversion argument (numbers are written out as integers).

18413.name: CellIs
18413.docs: Cell value compared with one or two formulas.

15870.name: thai_group
15870.docs:
Thai words for a group of up to six decimal digits (most significant first); empty for zero.
One in the tens is สิบ, two is ยี่สิบ, and a final one after higher digits is เอ็ด; `after`
says the number already has a non-zero digit in a higher group (so 1,000,001 ends in เอ็ด).

1774.name: mode
1774.docs: (leading, trailing) for a trim_rows / trim_cols code.

26188.name: is_encrypted

15943.name: MAX_TEXT
15943.docs: Longest text a cell can hold.

1847.name: format
1847.docs: Formats `v`; `step` (axis labels) fixes the decimals for General.

30112.name: settle
30112.docs: Skips to the next part when the current one is used up. Returns whether a new part began.

12384.name: journal_paused
12384.docs:
While a dry run runs (the footprint, `macro.check`), its commands are not journaled: the
dry run is put back, and journaling it would evict the person's own oldest entries.

3447.name: TOOLS
3447.docs: (id, label) of every tool, in the order of Excel's Analysis Tools list.

29096.name: read_hyperlinks
29096.docs:
`budget` counts the cells and bytes this sheet's hyperlinks have copied so far, across
`<hyperlinks>` blocks.

11149.name: eval
11149.docs: Evaluates a compiled formula with the given field values (in `refs` order).

22702.name: apply_tint
22702.docs: Tint as in ECMA-376: lighten towards white (positive) or darken (negative) in HSL luminance.

12457.name: in_group
12457.docs: Whether an undo group is open on the document with this uid.

2212.name: doughnut
2212.docs:
Excel's doughnut: every series is one concentric ring, the first series innermost (measured in
Excel: ring outer radii ≈0.83, 0.92 and 1.0 of the plot radius for series 1, 2 and 3). The hole
size and first slice angle come from the chart; each ring is scaled to its own total.

26626.name: BLOCK_VERIFIER_INPUT
26626.docs: Agile block keys ([MS-OFFCRYPTO] 2.3.4.13): one per value derived from the password.

27934.name: without_controls
27934.docs:
A kept `<controls>` fragment without the controls whose `shapeId` is in `drop` (they are
written from the model): a bare `<control>` child goes when it is one of them, and within an
`mc:AlternateContent` child only those controls go, in each of its branches, the wrapper
staying while a control remains. `None` when nothing is left. A fragment that doesn't parse
is returned unchanged.

29242.name: push_dynamic
29242.docs:
Records a dynamic-array range, so its cells outside the anchor import as empty and the
formula fills them again. Repeated identical anchors (a damaged or hostile sheet may repeat
the same record) are recorded once, and count and area are capped: every later cell inside
known range territory pays a scan proportional to what is recorded here.

18997.name: Absolute
18997.docs: Don't move or size with cells (`editAs="absolute"` / `<xdr:absoluteAnchor>`).

26699.name: streams
26699.docs:
The `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` streams. Rights management (IRM) keeps the
package but describes its encryption elsewhere, with no `EncryptionInfo`.

6209.name: sensitivity_applies
6209.docs:
Whether `data.solver` params (such as the `model` of its result) describe a model that can
have a Sensitivity report: Simplex LP or GRG Nonlinear, a Max or Min objective and no
integer or binary constraints.

1123.name: MAX_LAMBDA_CALLS
1123.docs:
LAMBDA calls that one formula may have in progress at once, counted the same way on every build.
The next call answers `#NUM!`. A countdown from 131, the deepest that `MAX_DEPTH` allows, has 132
calls in progress, so it still runs.

8825.name: resolve
8825.docs:
Macro tokens: references in step parameters that are worked out when the step runs, so a
macro made on one block of data works on another.

A token is a base followed by methods:

- bases: a declared input (`Input`, `Rates`), `Output` (the output rule's anchor), `Row` or
  `Column` (the current item of the Repeat step around it), and `Name:Total` (a defined name or
  a table's data; a name can hold periods, and the longest one that exists is used, so
  `Name:Sales.Q1.cell(1,1)` is a cell of `Sales.Q1`);
- methods, 1-based and chainable: `.col(n)` or `.col("Amount")` (by an input's header row,
  also after `.data`), `.row(n)`, `.cols(a..b)`, `.rows(a..)`, `.cell(r,c)` (relative to the
  top-left cell; any whole numbers, so `cell(0,1)` is the cell above), `.offset(r,c)`,
  `.resize(h,w)`, `.data` (without the header row), `.below(n)` and `.right(n)` (the n rows
  below or columns right of the range).

In parameters a token is written three ways: `{"$ref": "Input.col(2)"}` anywhere; the whole
string `"Input.col(2)"` in a reference parameter (`cell`, `range`, `target`, `to`, keys ending
in `Cell` or `Range`…); or `{{Input.col(2)}}` inside any string (`"=SUM({{Input.col(2)}})"`).
Each becomes A1 text before the command runs, so commands never see a token. Text that would
read as a token is written `{"$text": "Output"}`: it is passed as it is, never resolved or
interpolated (a defined name called `Output`, or `Dear {{name}}`). Plain A1
references in steps are absolute: they don't follow row inserts (as in VBA); a `Name:` anchor
does.

2431.name: PALETTE_CYCLE
2431.docs: `series_color` repeats after this many colours (six accents × the tints).

3739.name: draw
3739.docs: A draw: the first outcome whose cumulative probability exceeds a uniform number (inversion).

15292.name: dc
15292.docs: Σ DCi / NLi over the odd period.

1196.name: trim
1196.docs:
Trims the bottom/right of an area to the sheet's used range (keeps the top-left so
positions stay right).

3812.name: takes_no_inputs
3812.docs:
The stored name of the workbook's macro `name` when it exists and declares no inputs: a fixed
input range would make every press fail (`macro.run` refuses inputs it doesn't take), so such
an assignment is refused when it is made and dropped to the selection when a file brings one
in. A macro the workbook doesn't have (yet) is not checked: the assignment is kept as given.

29461.name: read_dxf
29461.docs: One differential format (`dxf`): the style it sets over a cell's own.

11514.name: view
11514.docs:
`None` while this window's view is the one in the document (the active window, or the
workbook's most recently active window); exactly one window per workbook has `None`.

28226.name: write_package_rels
28226.docs: Adds the kept package-root relationships (custom properties…) to `_rels/.rels`.

14130.name: dynamic
14130.docs:
Dynamic-array functions: FILTER, SORT, SORTBY, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, RANDARRAY, VSTACK, HSTACK,
TOROW, TOCOL, WRAPROWS, WRAPCOLS, TAKE, DROP, CHOOSEROWS, CHOOSECOLS, EXPAND, GROUPBY,
PIVOTBY.

GROUPBY / PIVOTBY take their aggregation as a function name ("SUM", "AVERAGE"…) or a
SUBTOTAL-style code (1–11): the host resolves eta-reduced lambdas such as `SUM` to the name
text before calling. Custom LAMBDA aggregations are not supported here.

29534.name: encrypt_workbook
29534.docs:
`package` (normally an `.xlsx` zip) as Excel stores it with a password: Agile encryption
(AES-256, SHA-512) inside a compound file.

26991.name: MAX_CSV_BYTES
26991.docs: The largest CSV or tab-separated file written (bytes).

11660.name: active_sheet
11660.docs: The index of the sheet the workbook's window shows (the file's active tab).

9117.name: trim
9117.docs: Whole rows or columns shrink to the part of the sheet in use.

24594.name: significant_digits
24594.docs:
`n` significant digits of `a` (rounded half to even on the exact binary value) and the power of
ten of the first.

1561.name: col_deps
1561.docs: (sheet, col) → row intervals of the ranges (up to `WIDE` columns) that cover the column

16965.name: Outline
16965.docs: One column per row field; each item on its own row.

20816.name: MAX_MACRO_SHORTCUT
20816.docs: The longest shortcut text (`Ctrl+Shift+M`), in characters.

4177.name: file
4177.docs: File menu: new, open, save, close, export, properties, options.

8028.name: enforce_python_limits
8028.docs:
A file is somebody else's work: a Python cell whose code doesn't fit in Excel's
8,192-character formula keeps only its cached value, and a kept result that is not a
well-formed array of at most [`crate::model::python::MAX_RESULT_CELLS`] cells is dropped
(the cell keeps its value). Either way the values the cell spilled stay as plain values
([`crate::model::Sheet::settle_spill`]). Returns the warnings.

20889.name: check_id
20889.docs:
Refuses a command id that isn't one: empty, longer than a name, or holding anything other than
letters, digits, `.` and `_` (every command id is of that form).

4250.name: format
4250.docs: Formatting: Home › Font, Alignment, Number, Styles, Cells › Format.

9409.name: error
9409.docs: The step the run would fail at.

4323.name: holds_gridcraft_data
4323.docs:
Refuses a name of the shape GridCraft keeps its own workbook data in ([`super::stash`]):
defining, renaming or deleting one would replace or remove part of an item (a stored macro,
script or view) and leave the rest behind. `force: true` lets the call go ahead.
Whether `name` is one the workbook holds GridCraft's own data in: a hidden workbook-scope
name of an item's shape. A visible name of that shape is the person's own (see `stash`), and
the name commands may change it.

15876.name: delimiters
15876.docs: Delimiter list from a scalar or array argument.

545.name: parse_number_text_in
545.docs: Like [`parse_number_text`], with date text read in the given workbook date system.

15949.name: scalar
15949.docs: Scalar value of an argument (top-left element for arrays).

4469.name: PivotField
4469.docs: A field placed in the Rows or Columns area.

8320.name: MAX_LISTED
8320.docs: The most entries `changed` lists (ranges and sheet notes), as the footprint lists ranges.

30118.name: remaining
30118.docs: Bytes left in the record (all parts), constant-time in the part count.

9628.name: make_way
9628.docs:
The footprint check and the output rule, inside the run's undo group: an error when the macro
would fail or write over data it may not, after shifting the data if the rule says so. Returns
the machine for the run and whether it shifted. The dry runs count towards the run's time
limit.

The footprint proves nothing about steps it didn't reach (it stopped early) or a path the run
takes and the dry run didn't (RAND, NOW), so the machine also checks each step as it runs and
stops the run at one that writes over data.

14787.name: season_arg
14787.docs: `[seasonality]`: 1 (default) detects, 0 means none, 2–8,760 is the season length.

27648.name: to_latex
27648.docs:
The LaTeX for an `m:oMath` (or `m:oMathPara`) element, if every part is in the subset and the
result lays out.

25105.name: render_text
25105.docs: Renders a text value through a text section (`@` is replaced by the text).

30264.name: palette
30264.docs: Palette entries for colour indexes 8 and up (RRGGBB), when a Palette record is present.

20019.name: CONTROL_MAX
20019.docs:
The largest value a slider or spin button takes (Excel's scroll bar limit). Values are whole
numbers from 0 to this.

9774.name: max_level
9774.docs: The deepest outline level used by these lines (0 = no outline).

30337.name: is_xls
30337.docs:
Whether the bytes are a compound file holding an Excel workbook stream (BIFF8 `Workbook`
or BIFF5 `Book`).

12390.name: start_recording
12390.docs:
Starts recording top-level commands into an empty buffer, replacing any recording in
progress. Queries, failed commands and commands run by other commands are not recorded.

11155.name: source_refs
11155.docs: Source fields a calculated field needs, directly or through other calculated fields.

8612.name: Macro
8612.docs: A step of a recorded macro run: macro parameters (tokens and all), kept as written.

2218.name: QuartileMethod
2218.docs: Quartile calculation for a box & whisker series.

9920.name: rows_ref
9920.docs: An absolute reference to `col` over grid `rows` (contiguous runs joined into a union).

2291.name: smooth_run
2291.docs:
Catmull-Rom spline through `pts`: every segment gets the same number of sub-segments (up to
100), chosen so the whole curve stays within `MAX_LINE_PTS * 2` points. Endpoints are
duplicated so the curve passes through the first and last points, and the curve is clamped
to the `plot` box (a spline overshoots its data near sharp turns).

29248.name: MAX_HYPERLINK_TARGET
29248.docs: Longest hyperlink target kept, in bytes (Excel's own limit is about 2,079 characters).

26705.name: Scheme
26705.docs: The two schemes read, with the part of `EncryptionInfo` each one parses.

6215.name: is_model_name
6215.docs:
Whether `name` is one of the names of a saved model: Excel's Solver names (`solver_opt`,
`solver_lhs1` and so on) and GridCraft's own. A user's name such as `solver_budget` is not.

8831.name: item
8831.docs: The innermost Repeat step's current row or column.

2437.name: eval_list
2437.docs:
Evaluates a series formula to a flat list of values (row-major), capped. A union of
references (`(A1:A3,A5)`, as PivotCharts use) is read part by part.

3818.name: approval_key
3818.docs:
The approval key of a button's command: its id and parameters, with a prefix that keeps it
apart from a macro's fingerprint (canonical JSON, which starts with `{`).

14136.name: key_of
14136.docs: Hashable key for case-insensitive equality of values.

26997.name: arabic_touching_latin
26997.docs: Arabic bytes next to an ASCII letter: Western accents sit inside Latin words, Arabic doesn't.

11666.name: math
11666.docs:
GridCraft equations. LaTeX source is laid out by RaTeX (`ratex-parser`, `ratex-layout`; MIT)
into a [`MathList`]: plain glyph, rule and path data that the UI and the PDF writer paint
without calling RaTeX again.

RaTeX is young (0.1.x), so it only ever runs inside this crate's entry points ([`layout`],
[`to_omml`], [`check`]). Each one caps its input (4 KB, nesting 32) and runs under
`catch_unwind`, so a stray panic becomes a [`MathError`]. See the RaTeX gate in
`docs/decisions.md` and `tests/gate.rs`.

Units are em: one em is the equation's font size. Coordinates run right and down from the
top-left of the list's box; the baseline is at `y = height`.

9123.name: Stopwatch
9123.docs: A stopwatch for the time limit. `Instant::now` traps on wasm, so there it measures nothing.

14282.name: bessel_j_all
14282.docs:
J_0..J_m(x) for 0 < x ≤ ~100 by Miller's backward recurrence, normalised with
J_0 + 2ΣJ_{2k} = 1.

4037.name: GO_TO_NAME_DEPTH
4037.docs: How deep a name that refers to other names is followed.

7888.name: synthesize
7888.docs:
Candidate programs for one example, by greedy segmentation of the output into token matches
and literals (tries several index conventions).

24600.name: MAX_SECTIONS
24600.docs: At most this many sections are honoured (`pos;neg;zero;text`); extra ones are ignored.

20822.name: shortcut
20822.docs: Keyboard shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+M`) for a user interface to offer; the engine only stores it.

2875.name: trendlines
2875.docs: Trendlines to fit and draw over this series.

25981.name: MAX_PAGE_CONTENT
25981.docs:
Most bytes of content per page before further drawing is dropped (keeps hostile inputs from
exhausting memory).

8034.name: part_too_large_message
8034.docs:
What to tell the user when one part of an XLSX package unpacks to more than the reader's
per-part limit: the sizes, why the limit is there, and what gets the data in. The limit is
per part, so smaller sheets fit; the shared strings are one part for every sheet, so only a
CSV, which has no parts, helps there.

1640.name: also
1640.docs:
Other formulas read at [`MAX_NESTED`] levels deep by the evaluations being abandoned. They
are calculated along with the suspended one, rather than one per restart (a wide range
read at the limit would restart the abandoned evaluations once per cell in it).

28597.name: workbook_xml
28597.docs:
Adds the workbook relationships to the caches; returns the `<pivotCaches>` element (empty
when there are none).

19660.name: first_slice_angle
19660.docs: Pie/doughnut first slice angle in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock (0–359).

20968.name: entries
20968.docs:
Reads the `macros` field of a JSON workbook as raw entries, whatever they hold, so they can be
checked one at a time.

478.name: days_from_civil
478.docs:
Days since 1970-01-01 for a proleptic Gregorian date, exact for every `i32` year.

`NaiveDate` only covers about ±262143 years, but the Gregorian calendar repeats every 400
years (146_097 days): chrono converts the year within its cycle and whole cycles are added
back as days (an i128 so the i32 extremes can't overflow). 1970-01-01 is `num_days_from_ce`
719_163; the result matches the proleptic Gregorian count the old hand-rolled code gave.

31286.name: sniff
31286.docs: Guesses the format from content: ODS mimetype, XLSB package content types, other ZIP packages as XLSX, text as CSV.

551.name: parse_plain
551.docs: Signs, currency, thousands separators, percent, exponent.

28816.name: REL
28816.docs: Relationship type from the workbook part.

4475.name: canonical_any
4475.docs: The canonical name of a source or calculated field.

8326.name: machine
8326.docs: Out of the session only while a step runs.

9634.name: shifted_conflicts
9634.docs:
For `macro.check`, as the run would: shifts the data, checks the footprint again, and puts
everything back. What still stands in the way, or `None`.

22495.name: set
22495.docs: Stores a cell; a default (empty, unstyled) cell is removed instead.

16101.name: is_scalar_arg
16101.docs: Whether parameter `i` expects a scalar (and is therefore lifted over arrays).

2005.name: is_100
2005.docs: Families stacked to 100%: each category's values are shares of its total.

9707.name: shortcut_conflict
9707.docs: Why macro `name` cannot use Ctrl+Shift+`letter`: GridCraft uses it, or another macro has it.

30270.name: palette
30270.docs: A Palette record: colours for indexes 8 onwards.

12323.name: UiRequest
12323.docs: Requests from commands to the UI (open a dialog, show a message…).

9780.name: outline
9780.docs:
Outline groups (Data ▸ Group) of a sheet's rows or columns: the runs of lines at or above
each outline level, as the grid draws them (brackets, − / + buttons, level buttons) and the
Show / Hide Detail commands act on them. Summary rows sit below their detail and summary
columns right of it, or above / left of it when the sheet's outline settings say so
([`Sheet::summary_below`], [`Sheet::summary_right`]).

3386.name: Grid
3386.docs: The table being read, with its size limits.

8545.name: DENIED
8545.docs: Single commands that never run in a macro.

12396.name: macro_recording
12396.docs: Where the macro recorder started (beside `recorder`, its buffer).

16247.name: delim
16247.docs: A delimiter's character; `.` is no delimiter.

22714.name: major_font_scripts
22714.docs:
The heading font's per-script typefaces (`<a:font script="Arab" typeface="…"/>`), as
(script, typeface) in file order.

26565.name: build
26565.docs:
A control from what the file says, its numbers clamped to whole numbers 0..30000 that pass
the model's rules (a hostile or odd file can't give a control it couldn't have).

9926.name: pivot
9926.docs:
PivotTables: reading the source list, grouping and aggregating, laying out the report and
writing it onto the sheet as static, styled cells.

Behaviour follows Excel's documented PivotTable model (rows/columns/values/filters areas,
Compact/Outline/Tabular layouts, subtotals, grand totals, show-values-as); the code and the
look (our own palette) are original.

27946.name: notes_vml
27946.docs:
GridCraft's notes and form controls VML for part `name`, merged with the kept control and
object shapes.

13850.name: Text
13850.docs: Text (lower-cased chars kept for wildcard matching).

3605.name: mode
3605.docs: The most frequent value (the first one to reach the top count), `#N/A` when no value repeats.

29254.name: MAX_DYNAMIC_CHECKS
29254.docs:
Most row-membership checks the sheet's ranges may serve. Beyond it the remaining cells are
imported with their cached values instead of being blanked for a spill that may still come,
so adversarial range counts can't make each cell scan a long list (a real workbook has a
handful of ranges).

15158.name: day_count
15158.docs: Days between two dates under a basis.

30562.name: Parsed
30562.docs: A parsed formula: tokens and extra data.

2370.name: MAX_WEDGES
2370.docs:
Most wedges a doughnut draws for the whole chart. The per-series and per-category limits do not
bound their product: 255 series of 20,000 categories would be millions of wedges. Every drawable
ring shares this budget, so the innermost ring keeps its largest slices and the outer rings are
capped instead of the chart dropping rings wholesale.

3678.name: anova_two_factor_without
3678.docs:
Anova: Two-Factor Without Replication: one observation for each pair of levels (rows ×
columns), the error term being the residual after both main effects.

1135.name: visit_range
1135.docs:
Calls `f` on each stored value of a block, row-major (formula cells evaluated first),
until `f` returns false. `false` when this host can't (callers use `range_values`).

2443.name: category_table
2443.docs:
Category labels, formatted with each source cell's number format (dates, currency…), and
the outer levels of a multi-level axis: a category range wider than a column of values (or
taller than a row of values) groups its innermost labels, year beside month. Each outer level
has one entry per category, non-empty where a group starts, as the cells are.

28092.name: attach
28092.docs: Adds the owner's relationships; returns old id → new id.

7602.name: is_date_format
7602.docs:
Whether a number format shows a calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD` and `m/d/yyyy h:mm` do; `0 "days"`
and `h:mm` don't).

20463.name: font
20463.docs: Typeface (`a:latin typeface`); `None` is the default font.

2516.name: solve
2516.docs: Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting; `None` when (nearly) singular.

28238.name: MAX_KEPT_PARTS
28238.docs: Most parts kept for one workbook.

3897.name: case_order
3897.docs:
Case-sensitive tie-break for text that is equal ignoring case: as in Excel, lowercase sorts
before uppercase at the first letter that differs in case.

29546.name: encrypt_agile_with_hmac_key
29546.docs: [`encrypt_agile`] with the dataIntegrity HMAC keyed by `hmac_key`.

5205.name: shift_anchor
5205.docs:
Repositions one floating object's anchor for a structural insert/delete, honouring its
[`AnchorMode`]: absolute objects ("Don't move or size with cells") stay put; "move but don't
size" follows its cell and keeps its size; "move and size" is re-fitted to the lines it lands
on. `corner` is the pre-edit bottom-right line/offset (from [`anchor_corner`]); a line deleted
out from under an edge collapses that edge onto `at`. `sh` is the post-edit grid, used to
measure the re-fitted size.

7894.name: position
7894.docs: A 1-based row or column number → 0-based, within `max`.

16904.name: has_content
16904.docs: Whether the cell holds content (a value, a formula or Python code), formats aside.

22063.name: rewrite_xl
22063.docs:
Rewrites the reference of every `xl("…")` literal in `code` with `f`; `None` from `f` leaves
it. Returns the new code when anything changed. A new reference holding the literal's quote
(a sheet name that needs quotes, `'Q4 2026'!B2`) gets the other quote as its delimiter, or an
escaped quote when it holds both, so it never ends the string early.

4116.name: trendline_param
4116.docs:
The trendline described by `chart.addElement`'s trendline parameters (Excel's Add Chart
Element ▸ Trendline choices, plus the Format Trendline options).

9275.name: executed
9275.docs: Steps executed so far (each pass through a Repeat counts).

20828.name: step_count
20828.docs: Steps in the macro, counting those inside Repeat and If.

6732.name: MAX_KEY
6732.docs: The longest key: `_gc_<key>_<k>` stays well inside Excel's 255-character names.

4189.name: forecast
4189.docs:
Data › Forecast › Forecast Sheet: a new sheet with the history, a FORECAST.ETS column, the
FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT confidence bounds, optional FORECAST.ETS.STAT statistics and a chart.

Like Excel, the sheet holds a copy of the timeline and values (sorted by time) and live
formulas over that copy, so the forecast follows edits to the copied history.

8040.name: save_bytes
8040.docs: Encodes a workbook in the format chosen by `path`'s extension.

19593.name: ChartDataTable
19593.docs: A chart's data table (`c:dTable`), independent of the chart legend.

1646.name: tainted
1646.docs: Results that read a previous value, directly or through other formulas.

27295.name: write_drawing
27295.docs: The drawing part for a sheet's objects (relationship ids already assigned).

19666.name: supports_data_table
19666.docs: Data tables belong to category-axis column, bar, line and area charts.

1719.name: dirty_closure
1719.docs:
The formulas to recalculate after `seeds` and every cell of `areas` changed: the seeds
that are formulas, and everything that reads them, directly or through other formulas.

20974.name: header
20974.docs: The first row holds column names.

484.name: date
484.docs:
Date serial numbers.

The 1900 system counts days from 1899-12-31 (serial 1 = 1900-01-01) and, like Lotus 1-2-3 and
Excel, treats 1900 as a leap year: serial 60 is the fictitious 1900-02-29. The 1904 system
counts from 1904-01-01 (serial 0). Times are fractions of a day.

22282.name: controls
22282.docs:
Form controls (buttons, sliders, spin buttons). They paint above every other object and
take clicks first.

4335.name: select_trace_cells
4335.docs:
Excel's Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+]: select the precedent (or dependent) cells. When they all live on
another sheet, jump there. `all` walks every level (Ctrl+Shift+[ / Ctrl+Shift+]).

23590.name: DxfStated
23590.docs:
The parts a differential format states at a value its `Style` can't tell from unset: a dxf's
default parts are unset, so a bold turned off, a face, a size or a protection that matches the
defaults would otherwise read as nothing. The values are the style's own; this records that
the format states them, and only where they match the defaults, so a format built in the app
and the same format read back from a file stay equal.

15961.name: array_val
15961.docs: Wraps an array result. Rejects empty and oversized arrays.

28822.name: MAX_SCRIPTS
28822.docs: Most scripts read from the part.

8332.name: start
8332.docs: The workbook when the run started, for "changed so far".

1938.name: stroke_paths
1938.docs: Thick polyline → one quad per segment (each a separate path so overlaps don't cancel).

9640.name: with_names
9640.docs:
A copy of `wb` for xlsx with each macro in hidden names (`_gc_macro_<n>_<k>`) instead of the
field, or `None` when there is nothing to change. The macros keep their order; the index `n`
is this build's choice, so it steps around any a person's own visible name already uses.

22501.name: used_range
22501.docs: Smallest range containing every stored cell, `None` when empty.

27660.name: on
27660.docs: Whether the switch `name` in the property element `props` is on, when the converter reads it.

26425.name: strip_book
26425.docs: A PivotChart link without the workbook in brackets: `[Book.xlsx]Sheet2!PT` → `Sheet2!PT`.

8478.name: Step
8478.docs: One macro step and its editor flags.

9786.name: scale
9786.docs: Print scale (1.0 = 100%): screen sizes of cells are `zoom × scale`.

8551.name: previewable
8551.docs:
Whether the footprint dry run can preview a command. Solver can take long, so a dry run stops
before it and reports the footprint as partial.

12402.name: link_policy
12402.docs:
Whether `link.open` may open web and e-mail addresses without the user's confirmation
(#2181). Host code sets it; no command does.

16253.name: MAX_EM
16253.docs:
Largest coordinate or size accepted in a layout, in em. `\rule{1e308em}{1em}` lays out; this
stops it from reaching a painter.

26571.name: modelled
26571.docs:
The VML shape numbers of the controls read into the model: GridCraft writes those, so they
are left out of the kept content.

13783.name: MAX_CRITERION_UTF16_UNITS
13783.docs:
Longest text criterion COUNTIF and its relatives accept, in UTF-16 code units as Excel
counts them (😀 is two units); a longer one is `#VALUE!`.

18942.name: target
18942.docs:
URL, `mailto:`, a file path (`Book.xlsx`, `Book.xlsx#Sheet1!A2`), or an in-workbook location
like `Sheet2!A1`.

3611.name: sxy
3611.docs: Sum of cross products of deviations.

29260.name: read_protected_ranges
29260.docs:
Allow Edit Ranges. A range whose password can't be read keeps a hash that never matches
(or an unsupported algorithm), so it stays locked rather than open.

8770.name: ResolveError
8770.docs: Why a reference couldn't be worked out.

6227.name: percent
6227.docs:
Integer Optimality as a percent from its stored fraction. The product is rounded to 1E-10 %,
so a fraction such as 0.07 reads back as 7 and not 7.000000000000001.

3684.name: fourier_analysis
3684.docs:
Fourier Analysis: the discrete Fourier transform (or with `inverse` its inverse) of one row or
column of 2^k values, read and written as complex numbers the way IMREAL, IMAGINARY and
COMPLEX read and write them.

2449.name: resolve
2449.docs:
Evaluates a chart's series formulas: names, values, categories (default "1", "2", …), X
values (scatter/bubble), bubble sizes, number formats and colours (explicit, else the
default palette derived from the workbook theme accents).

11459.name: WindowView
11459.docs: The view state one window keeps while another window on its workbook is showing.

1214.name: trimrange
1214.docs:
TRIMRANGE: a range or array without its blank outer rows and columns (Microsoft's
documented semantics: trim_rows / trim_cols 0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both).

5065.name: trim_full
5065.docs: Whole rows/columns are trimmed to the used range.

2522.name: moving_average
2522.docs:
Moving average of `period` consecutive points in plotted order: point `i` (from
`period - 1`) is `(xᵢ, mean(yᵢ₋ₚ₊₁..=yᵢ))`. Empty when there are fewer points than `period`.

3830.name: filter_blank
3830.docs: The filter's "(Blanks)" group: truly empty cells and zero-length text such as a `=""` result.

24393.name: view
24393.docs: The workbook window's display settings (`<workbookView>`), kept across an open + save.

198.name: parse_a1_prefix
198.docs: Parses an A1 reference at the start of `s`: `(col, row, col_abs, row_abs, rest)`.

4049.name: MAX_PASTE_VALIDATION_RANGES
4049.docs:
Most validation ranges one paste adds (a rule covering part of a small block tiled over a huge
selection makes one range per tile).

7900.name: Part
7900.docs:
One part of an R1C1 reference: `R`/`C` followed by an absolute number, a bracketed offset or
nothing (the cell's own row or column).

20761.name: columns
20761.docs: Number of button columns in the layout (Excel default 1).

28463.name: base
28463.docs: The database field the grouping applies to.

18218.name: range
18218.docs: Whole table including header and totals rows.

19526.name: forward
19526.docs: Forecast past the last point, in x units (categories on a category axis).

27228.name: read
27228.docs:
Do not partially import a path: losing a curve, subpath, transform or line effect changes
the drawing. Accept only the explicit subset emitted below, including its line styling.

9281.name: last_params
9281.docs: The last step's resolved parameters (for the debugger).

6738.name: MAX_ITEMS
6738.docs:
The most items [`items`] and [`keys`] return: the first this many keys in sorted order. A
file can carry any number of hidden names; the rest are not listed.

8046.name: csv
8046.docs:
Save As CSV/Text writes "the text and values as they are displayed in cells" with "all
characters in each cell" (Microsoft Support, *Excel formatting and features that are not
transferred to other file formats*): number formats applied, never column-width `#####`.

490.name: serial_from_ymd
490.docs:
Serial for a date. Month and day overflow roll over like `DATE()` (month 13 = January next
year, day 0 = last day of the previous month), in the date system's own calendar: in the 1900
system February 1900 has 29 days, so `(1900, 2, 29)` and `(1900, 3, 0)` are serial 60.
`None` before the epoch or after 9999-12-31.

8265.name: External
8265.docs: An address to hand to the system, trimmed: `http`, `https` or `mailto` only.

15967.name: round_half_away
15967.docs:
Rounds half away from zero at `digits` decimals using the 15-significant-digit decimal
representation of `x`, so ROUND(2.675, 2) = 2.68 like Excel.

28828.name: ScriptsIn
28828.docs: The scripts read from a workbook's Python part, and what the cells took from them.

8338.name: View
8338.docs: The active sheet and the selections of the debugged workbook where the run left them.

12189.name: enter_direction
12189.docs: After pressing Enter, move the selection: "down", "right", "up", "left", "none".

5795.name: linear_program
5795.docs:
The LP to minimise for `goal`, from the linearised model: the costs, and the rows
(coefficients, sense, right side) in the order of `model_rows`.

9646.name: find
9646.docs: The index of the macro called `name` (case-insensitive).

22507.name: shift_rows
22507.docs:
Rows strictly greater than or equal to `from` moved by `delta` (positive = down). Rows that
would land before `from`... callers delete the vacated block first.

9719.name: has_summary
9719.docs:
Whether the summary line exists: a group that starts at the first line (summary before)
or ends at the last one (summary after) has none.

8484.name: stop
8484.docs: Stops the run: keeps what it did as one undo step, or rolls it back.

9792.name: rows_complete
9792.docs: The bands reach the sheet's last row / column.

11100.name: pivot_calc
11100.docs:
Calculated PivotTable fields: a formula over other fields (`=Sales*0.1`,
`='Unit Price'*Units`, `=IF(Units>0,Sales/Units,0)`).

As Microsoft documents for Excel, the formula operates on the *sums* of the fields it names
for each report cell (items, subtotals and grand totals alike), not record by record: for
`=Sales*1.2` a cell shows 1.2 × the sum of Sales of that cell's records. Fields are written
bare (`Sales`) or in single quotes (`'Unit Price'`); cell references and defined names are not
allowed. A calculated field may use other calculated fields; a cycle evaluates to `#REF!`.

12408.name: marks
12408.docs:
For each running command, innermost last: its document and that document's undo length
when it began. Steps before that length are not touched while the command runs (see
[`Session::bound_tail`]).

29120.name: cost
29120.docs:
Approximate bytes one dependent cell costs (its printed text plus its expression tree);
what exceeds [`SHARED_FORMULA_FREE_COST`] is charged against [`MAX_SHARED_FORMULA_BYTES`].

24034.name: iterative
24034.docs:
Enable iterative calculation: circular references are calculated repeatedly instead of
reporting an error.

27885.name: SheetScan
27885.docs: What a sheet part holds for pass-through.

9938.name: Probe
9938.docs:
What [`detail_records`] and [`detail_cells`] ask of a report computation: the row and column
item paths of the value cell at `at`, the paths of every record the filters let through (when
`paths` is set), and every value cell (when `cells` is set).

8703.name: RecordedStep
8703.docs: One recorded command and where it ran.

11319.name: with_toggle_state
11319.docs:
`params` with the state a toggle set (Bold's `on`, from the command's result), as Excel
records `Bold = True`: playing the step back sets that state rather than flipping it again.
`python.output` without `mode` is a toggle too: it keeps the return type it set (the result's
`output`) as its `mode`.

6233.name: saved_model_cells
6233.docs:
The cells of a model written by Save Model that starts at `start` (none if the cells there
don't hold one).

3690.name: below
3690.docs: Uniform whole number in [0, n), without modulo bias.

2455.name: trend
2455.docs:
Trendline maths: least-squares fits behind chart trendlines and moving averages.

Exponential, logarithmic and power trendlines are linear fits of transformed data
(`ln y` against `x`, `y` against `ln x`, `ln y` against `ln x`), the way Excel documents them;
points where the transform is undefined (non-positive values) are skipped and R² is reported
for the transformed fit. Polynomials solve the normal equations on centred, scaled x.

14008.name: has_wildcards
14008.docs: Whether the pattern contains an unescaped wildcard.

5071.name: PageOrder
5071.docs: The sequence of a sheet's pages (XLSX `pageSetup pageOrder`, ECMA-376 `ST_PageOrder`).

30720.name: read_xlsb
30720.docs:
Imports worksheet scalar values and saved formula results. Number formats are omitted;
dates remain serial numbers with the workbook's original date system. Inspect warnings.

14081.name: ND
14081.docs: NETWORKDAYS / WORKDAY: start, end/days scalar; holidays take arrays.

7687.name: add_months_clamped
7687.docs:
`serial` shifted by `months` calendar months, keeping the day of month but clamping it to the
target month's last day (Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28/29). Always measured from the original date,
so a series does not drift: Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30. The time of day is kept.

8995.name: DEFAULT_TIME_LIMIT_MS
8995.docs:
How long a run may take, in milliseconds. The web build has no clock; there only the step
limit applies.

24399.name: preserved
24399.docs: Unmodelled file content kept for saving (package root and workbook level). Not in JSON.

28250.name: SHEET_ELEMENT_KINDS
28250.docs: Sheet relationship kinds that mean the sheet XML may hold elements worth keeping.

3909.name: cmd
3909.docs:
The command registry. Ids follow Excel's ribbon (`home.bold`, `insert.chart`,
`data.sortAscending`) plus primitive editing commands (`cell.set`, `selection.set`).

5217.name: insert_copied_cells
5217.docs:
Insert Copied Cells / Insert Cut Cells: makes room at the destination, then pastes (or, for a
cut, moves) the clipboard there, as one undo step.

16770.name: styled
16770.docs:
The Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols letter for `c` (Unicode 15, chapter 22.2), using the
Letterlike Symbols block where Unicode put a letter before the alphanumeric block existed.

25780.name: CID_FONT
25780.docs: Index of the CID font in a page's font flags (after the [`Font::ALL`] faces).

16843.name: data
16843.docs: Encoded PNG/JPEG bytes, base64 in JSON. Sheet entries share the payload through Arc.

4055.name: check_python_fits
4055.docs:
Refuses Python code an edit has made longer than one cell holds: the limit `python.set`
enforces and opening a file applies (code over it is dropped to its value on open). The edit
is refused rather than made, so no code is lost and none keeps a reference the edit moved.

27161.name: read
27161.docs: The field under the column's rule: a date when that reading is valid, else text.

5436.name: Outcome
5436.docs: What a relaxation (or the whole solve) ended with.

1658.name: previous
1658.docs:
A formula's previous value for iterative calculation: from the last iteration, else the
value it shows. Blank, and the `#CIRC!` of a loop calculated with iteration off, are 0.

27307.name: xf_is_checkbox
27307.docs: Whether an `xf` element carries an `xfComplement` that resolves to a checkbox.

31231.name: Xls
31231.docs: An Excel 97-2003 `.xls` workbook: a compound file with a `Workbook` (or BIFF5 `Book`) stream.

3039.name: cf
3039.docs:
Conditional formatting evaluation: what extra style, data bar, colour scale or icon a cell
gets.

496.name: Value
496.docs: A cell value or an intermediate formula result.

22294.name: clear_spill
22294.docs:
Removes the spilled values inside `r`. The work is bounded by the values stored, not by
the size of `r`, so a range from a file that claims the whole sheet costs no more than the
values it holds.

15900.name: Piece
15900.docs: A piece of a replacement: literal text or a capture group (by number or name).

24910.name: scale
24910.docs: Number of scaling commas (each divides by 1000).

18516.name: default_icon_thresholds
18516.docs:
Excel's default icon-set thresholds: one per icon, the first being the lower bound,
then even percent steps (`0, 33, 67` for three icons).

30069.name: next_record
30069.docs: The next record with its `Continue` records, or `None` at the end of the stream.

12122.name: content_kind
12122.docs:
The format `path`'s content was recognised as when its extension doesn't name one (an
XLSX called `budget.dat`): Save writes it back in that format.

9579.name: has_content
9579.docs: Python code is content, as a formula is, whatever the cell shows.

10887.name: values_here
10887.docs: Σ Values comes right here, at row field depth `depth` (`vi`: the value field already chosen above).

26291.name: chart_ref_from_file
26291.docs:
A chart reference (`<c:f>`) read from a file → model text: drops a leading `=` and the
`[0]!` in front of workbook-scoped names (`[0]!Sales` → `Sales`), which the formula parser
would take for a structured reference. External books (`[1]Sheet1!$A$1`), quoted sheet
names and string literals are kept as they are.

9652.name: is_newer
9652.docs: Whether `v` is a macro in a newer format than this build reads.

26364.name: ref_target
26364.docs: The sheet and range a same-workbook reference (`Sheet1!$B$2:$B$9`) names.

27672.name: radical
27672.docs: `m:rad`: a square root, or a root with a degree.

8490.name: Ask
8490.docs:
Allowed once the person approves the macro; the text says why it asks ("came with a
workbook you opened").

9798.name: LineIndex
9798.docs:
Prefix sums over the custom-sized lines of an axis: O(log n) position ↔ line lookups even
when every row has an explicit height (common in imported files).

21351.name: Contains
21351.docs: The cell's text contains `value`'s text, ignoring case.

29053.name: PicturesOut
29053.docs: One rich value per shared model payload; copied cells can reuse a metadata block.

12414.name: windows_of
12414.docs: A workbook's windows in opening order.

24040.name: CalcSettings
24040.docs: File › Options › Formulas › Calculation options, stored per workbook (`<calcPr>`).

7401.name: line_styles_differ
7401.docs: Whether any row or column style in `lo..=hi` differs between two sheets' line maps.

29199.name: dynamic_cells
29199.docs: Cells inside the ranges above, for a cap before a pathological sheet proves it itself.

8709.name: formula_tokens
8709.docs:
Replaces references in a formula that are exactly the example input, one of its columns or
rows, or a column without its first row, with `{{token}}`.

29272.name: read_ext
29272.docs: Worksheet extensions: x14 data validations and sparklines.

6239.name: cells_with_formulas
6239.docs:
The formulas of a model range, in order. Every cell up to the last formula must hold one: a
cell without a formula there (a constraint overwritten by a constant, say) would shift the
rows below it and drop a constraint or the options. Empty cells after the last formula are
allowed.

28037.name: is_relative_path
28037.docs: Not empty, no root, no scheme or drive (`file:`, `http:`, `C:`).

30653.name: resolve_pending
30653.docs:
Attaches every pending formula to its anchor's template, returning how many shared
templates were expanded. An anchor whose template can't be imported is refused once:
its followers re-decode the same template for nothing, so they are skipped instead (they
keep their cached values).

14014.name: find_column
14014.docs: Column index of a label in the header row.

5077.name: draw_cell_picture
5077.docs: Cell pictures fit the current cell (or merged-cell) rectangle without changing aspect ratio.

3842.name: LineInfo
3842.docs: Outline grouping info for a row or column.

1299.name: Ctx
1299.docs: Services a function may need from the host.

9001.name: step
9001.docs: The step's path: `3`, `2.1` inside a Repeat, `4.then.1` inside an If.

24405.name: macros_unread
24405.docs:
Macros in a newer format than this build reads, as the file held them. They are never read,
listed or run; a save writes them back unchanged, so the newer build gets them back whole.
Shared between snapshots, as nothing changes them.

28256.name: CHART_SHEET_GRAPH
28256.docs:
Relationship kinds a chart sheet reaches that are otherwise rewritten: its drawing, chart and
their style, colour and shape parts are kept byte for byte (the chart sheet is not modelled).

3915.name: formula_at
3915.docs: A formula written for `first`, as seen from `at` (relative references shifted).

5223.name: shift_table_columns
5223.docs:
Columns inserted inside a table become new table columns (with names no other column has);
deleted ones leave it.

16776.name: opt
16776.docs: Base64 for optional shared byte blobs (VBA projects): `null`/missing stays `None`.

25786.name: pdf_string
25786.docs: A PDF literal string `( … )` for `text` in WinAnsiEncoding.

22008.name: span
22008.docs: Byte range of the literal's contents (between the quotes) in the code.

9220.name: at
9220.docs: The current item (0-based) and how many there are.

18230.name: table_type
18230.docs: `tableType` when it isn't a plain worksheet table: `xml` for a table bound to an XML map.

27240.name: body_marker
27240.docs:
A marker for the equation a text body holds: 16 hex digits of an FNV-1a 64-bit hash over what
carries the equation's meaning, the OMML element names in document order, the text of the
runs, and the properties the converter reads ([`PROPERTIES`]: a run's `sty`, a delimiter's
characters, an operator's limits and so on). The writer puts it in the shape's description
beside the LaTeX source; the reader takes the source only while the marker still matches the
body, so an equation whose Office Math another application edited (Excel leaves the
description alone) is converted from that Office Math instead of coming back as the old
source. What a re-serialisation may change without changing the equation is left out: every
other property (`ctrlPr`, DrawingML run properties such as size and colour), extension lists,
the DrawingML containers (`txBody`, `p`, `r`, `fld`, `lstStyle`), attributes, namespace
prefixes and whitespace between elements; adjacent runs without read properties are joined,
so splitting or merging them changes nothing, while a run with one is a unit of its own, as
the converter converts it (it recognises function names per run). A text change, an added
run, a structural change, a change to a property the converter reads or a styled run split in
two does.

9293.name: iteration
9293.docs: The innermost Repeat's pass (1-based) and count.

15760.name: MAX_REGRESSORS
15760.docs:
Most predictor columns LINEST, LOGEST, TREND and GROWTH accept. The normal equations are a
