19336.name: trendlines
19336.docs: Trendlines fitted to this series (Excel allows several per series).

6548.name: sensitivity
6548.docs:
The Sensitivity report. Simplex LP: each variable's reduced cost and the range of its
objective coefficient over which the basis stays optimal, and each constraint's shadow price
and the range of its right side over which the shadow price holds, from the final tableau of
the LP linearised at the solution. GRG Nonlinear: the reduced gradients and the Lagrange
multipliers of the binding constraints at the solution, from difference gradients.

29727.name: XlsxKind
29727.docs:
Which member of the SpreadsheetML family a package is saved as. Only the content type of the
workbook part differs (ECMA-376 Part 1 Workbook part; MS-OI29500 adds the macro-enabled types).

11853.name: start
11853.docs: Undo depth when the group began; the group's own steps are cut back to it.

6840.name: set
6840.docs: Stores `text` under `key`, replacing what was there (in either format). Empty text removes it.

14615.name: ets
14615.docs:
The FORECAST.ETS family: additive-error, additive-trend, additive-seasonality (AAA)
exponential smoothing over an evenly spaced timeline.

Model (Hyndman, Koehler, Ord & Snyder, "Forecasting with Exponential Smoothing: The State
Space Approach", 2008, ETS(A,A,A), component form):

```text
ŷ_t = l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + s_{t-m}        e_t = y_t − ŷ_t
l_t = l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + α·e_t
b_t = b_{t-1} + α·β·e_t
s_t = s_{t-m} + γ·e_t
```

Initial states follow the book's heuristic (§2.6.1): seasonal indices from a classical
decomposition (centred moving average) of the first seasons, level and trend from a straight
line fitted to the first ten seasonally adjusted values. α, β and γ (each in [0, 1]) minimise
the sum of squared one-step errors: a coarse grid, then a Nelder–Mead simplex clamped to the
box. Excel does not document its optimiser, so fitted parameters (and the last digits of
forecasts on noisy data) can differ from Excel's; exact data (straight lines, exactly
repeating seasons) forecast exactly either way.

Seasonality detection: the autocorrelation of the linearly detrended series; the highest local
peak above the 95% white-noise bound (2/√n) at a lag of at most n/2 (and at most 8,760).

Prediction intervals use the model's h-step forecast variance (the book's Table 6.1, class 1):
`σ²·(1 + Σ_{j=1}^{h−1} (α + αβ·j + γ·[j mod m = 0])²)`, σ² = SSE / n, with the normal quantile.

5751.name: branch_and_bound
5751.docs: Depth-first branch and bound over a relaxation solver; returns the best integer point.

27695.name: read_limited
27695.docs: Reads a small metadata part without allowing it to expand to the general part limit.

9821.name: pages_in
9821.docs: Page rows and columns overlapping the layout rectangle `[x0, x1] × [y0, y1]`.

13672.name: parse_closing_parens
13672.docs:
Parses formula text as typed into a cell with `parse`, closing up to eight missing `)` at the
end as Excel does (`SUM(1,2` enters `SUM(1,2)`). When no number of `)` makes it parse, the
error describes the text as typed: `1+` is "unexpected end of formula", not "unexpected `)`".

12437.name: set_active
12437.docs:
Makes the workbook at `i` active, in its most recently active window (unless the active
window already shows it).

13745.name: range_a1
13745.docs: A1 text with `sep` between the two ends of a range (`:` or a trim operator).

11202.name: formulas_newest_first
11202.docs: The formula texts a command's params enter, the last first, at most `budget` of them.

7424.name: value_text_as
7424.docs:
[`value_text`] for a value and a format code given apart from a cell (print takes the code
from the cell's effective look, which a conditional format can override).

16434.name: Large
16434.docs:
A large operator or delimiter (TeX's Size1 to Size4 fonts): drawn stretched to the glyph's
box rather than at the run's font size.

2338.name: reserve
2338.docs:
Reserve at most half the available height. A table that cannot fit is explicitly labelled
instead of dropping rows or allocating a series × point-sized matrix.

27987.name: controls_insert_at
27987.docs:
Where GridCraft's control entries go in a kept `<controls>` fragment: just before the close
tag of the `<controls>` element the reader reads (`controls::controls_of`), whatever its
namespace prefix. In an `mc:AlternateContent` with separate `<controls>` elements in its
Choice and Fallback branches that is the Choice's, the one an application that knows the
x14 extensions reads; the Fallback's is left as the file had it. With no Choice, or a Choice
without a `<controls>` element, it is the first `<controls>` element (a plain fragment, or a
Fallback alone).

21593.name: legacy_hash
21593.docs:
The legacy 16-bit password hash: each UTF-16 unit contributes its low byte (its high byte
when the low one is zero), folded in from the last character with a 15-bit rotation, then
the length and the constant `0xCE4B`.

29295.name: x14_cfvo
29295.docs: An x14 `cfvo`: unlike the 2006 one it has no `val` attribute, the value is an `xm:f` child.

1176.name: lambda_arg
1176.docs:
The function argument of a LAMBDA helper; a function given by name takes `arity`
arguments.

8878.name: REF_KEYS
8878.docs:
Parameter keys that hold references, where a whole-string token is resolved. Elsewhere a
string is text (a cell may hold "Row", a chart's type is "column"), and a token needs
`{"$ref": …}` or `{{…}}`.

3792.name: link_param
3792.docs:
A link parameter in its stored form: `$B$2` on the host sheet, `'My Sheet'!$B$2` elsewhere.
An empty text removes the link.

5173.name: comment_cells
5173.docs: Threaded comments in navigation order: visible sheets in tab order, then row by row.

21885.name: output
21885.docs: The last result, when the code ran without an error.

3938.name: PY_FORMULA
3938.docs: Typing `=PY(` doesn't make a Python cell; this says what does.

const.expr: "Python cells are made with the python.set command (the code as `code`), not by typing =PY(…)."

6554.name: solve_dense
6554.docs:
Solves the square system `a·x = b` by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting; unknowns
of a singular system that have no pivot are 0.

30968.name: phonetic_data
30968.docs:
The phonetic (furigana) data of a string item: its `<rPh>` runs in document order, and its
`<phoneticPr>` when present.

`base` is the item's base text ([`rich_text`]); the offsets are validated against it and never
used to index anything. Behaviour reference: ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.4.6 `rPh` (`sb` and `eb` are
zero-based offsets into the base text with `sb < eb`, both within its length; child `<t>` holds
the reading) and §18.4.7 `phoneticPr` — the `PhoneticRun` and `PhoneticProperties` classes on
Microsoft Learn:
<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/office/developer/office-2010/cc820083(v=office.14)>,
<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/office/developer/office-2010/cc797016(v=office.14)>.
Damaged runs are dropped rather than repaired: one without both offsets, with `sb >= eb`, wholly
past the end of the base text, or without a reading; the caller reports how many.

29733.name: MAX_RGCE
29733.docs: Formula token bytes decoded at most (Excel's limit is 1,800 per formula).

6846.name: item_key
6846.docs: The item a hidden name belongs to, lower-cased: `_gc_<key>_<k>` and `_sc_<key>` give `<key>`.

22250.name: file_id
22250.docs:
The `sheetId` the file gave the sheet, written back on save so that what refers to the
sheet by its id keeps finding it; 0 for a sheet the file did not have. Not in JSON.

8154.name: SCRIPT_SANDBOX
8154.docs: How many [`ScriptSandbox`]es are alive on this thread.

9462.name: cells
9462.docs: The written cells as ranges (at most 500 listed), and how many cells.

19780.name: Ink
19780.docs:
A freehand ink stroke; `Shape::text` holds the points as `x,y;x,y;…` relative to the
anchor (sheet points), `Shape::line` the ink colour and `fill` unused.

4449.name: default_source
4449.docs: The default source: the table at the selection, else the selected block / current region.

26247.name: read_mini_chain
26247.docs:
Follows a mini FAT chain inside the mini stream container. Like `read_chain`, the
container may end inside the chain's last mini sector.

4522.name: remove_from_area
4522.docs: Removes `field` from an area; returns the source field it referred to.

28936.name: shared_formula_bytes
28936.docs:
Bytes charged so far for shared formulas expanded into dependent cells (see
[`crate::xlsx::sheet_read::MAX_SHARED_FORMULA_BYTES`]).

16148.name: MAX_WALK
16148.docs: Deepest tree walked (RaTeX already refuses input nested deeper than 32).

17456.name: grand_totals_rows
17456.docs: Grand total for each row (the "Grand Total" column), like Excel's "On for Rows".

25158.name: shown_width
25158.docs: Display width of a token in a fraction section, for blanking a hidden part with spaces.

7211.name: seek
7211.docs:
Finds `x` with `|f(x)| <= tol`: secant steps (with growing steps while nothing is
bracketed), switching to secant-or-bisection inside a sign-change bracket. Returns the best
point seen. `f` returns NaN where the model errors.

30317.name: line
30317.docs: One border side: its style and colour; a side without a style has no colour.

12370.name: TextWidth
12370.docs:
Width in points of one line of text drawn in a cell font, measured by a front end that has
the font the grid draws with. With `exact` false the front end may answer with a cheaper
measure that is never narrower (AutoFit asks for it on columns with many distinct values).
Commands call it while they run, so a front end must not run commands while holding a lock
the measure takes (egui's: see `theme::cell_text_width` in the UI crate).

13678.name: significant_spaces
13678.docs:
Keeps a space token only where it is the intersection operator: between the end of an
operand and the start of another.

3433.name: normalized
3433.docs: Same-looking text: non-breaking spaces as spaces, whitespace runs collapsed, trimmed.

12443.name: locked_cell_message
12443.docs:
The warning an edit of `at` on `sheet` gets from sheet protection, or `None` when the edit
is allowed. Front ends ask before opening an editor, so typing into a locked cell never
leaves a draft that can't be entered (and so blocks saving).

20145.name: page
20145.docs: Page change (sliders): a click on the track, or Page Up / Page Down.

3506.name: ss
3506.docs: Sum of squared deviations from the mean.

11208.name: RECORD_LIMIT
11208.docs: The most steps one recording keeps; later ones are counted in [`Recorder::dropped`].

8665.name: Converted
8665.docs: A recording turned into a macro, with what was left out.

4887.name: hf_date_time
4887.docs: Today's date and the current time as headers and footers show them (`&D`, `&T`).

2344.name: max_forward_slots
2344.docs:
Most empty category slots a forward forecast may add after `ncat` categories: four times the
data (at least 32), and never past `MAX_CATS` in total. A larger forecast would shrink every
column to nothing.

27993.name: root
27993.docs: Drive or share and root separator (`/`, `C:\`, `\\server\share\`).

21599.name: target
21599.docs:
The original part name of the target (no leading `/`), or the raw target of an external
relationship. External targets are never opened.

15205.name: coup_args
15205.docs: settlement, maturity, frequency, basis at positions 0..=3 for the COUP* functions.

22907.name: minor
22907.docs:
The font follows the theme's body font (`<scheme val="minor"/>`) while its face is the
theme's minor font. Fonts derived from it (bold, a colour, a size) keep the link.

25523.name: WIDTHS
25523.docs: Advance widths in 1/1000 em for codes 0x20..=0xFF (0 where Symbol has no glyph).

8884.name: is_token
8884.docs:
Whether `text` starts like a token (its base is one this environment knows). A reference on a
sheet with such a name (`Output!A1`) is not a token.

3798.name: numbers
3798.docs: Applies `min`, `max`, `step`, `page` and `value` from `p` to `c` and checks the result.

1255.name: lambda
1255.docs: The LAMBDA given as the function argument of GROUPBY/PIVOTBY.

29520.name: FUTURE_FUNCTIONS
29520.docs:
Functions introduced after Excel 2007 that files store with the `_xlfn.` prefix. Entries with
`_xlws.` get `_xlfn._xlws.`.

15424.name: SCANS
15424.docs:
Lookups whose every call searches a lookup vector from its start, so a call lifted over `n`
needles does `n` x (vector length) work. Their search arguments don't lift.

21891.name: from_formula
21891.docs:
Reads a `PY(…)` formula (with or without `=`, and with or without the `_xlfn.` and
`_xlws.` prefixes): string literals joined by `&`, optionally followed by `,0` or `,1`.
`None` for anything else.

27050.name: NoDates
27050.docs: No `d/m/y` or `d-m-y` value in the sample: read as typed input does.

30974.name: to_utf8
30974.docs: Converts input bytes to UTF-8 XML text (handles BOMs and UTF-16).

1620.name: Entries
1620.docs: A formula's precedents split by shape: single cells, column intervals and wide ranges.

9395.name: compare
9395.docs: If's comparison of a cell's value with a step's `value`, the way Excel's `=`, `<`… compare.

6852.name: chunk_formulas
6852.docs:
`text` as name formulas: string literals of at most 255 characters joined with `&`, each formula
at most 8,192 characters, with the characters XML can't carry escaped (see [`ESCAPE`]).
Concatenating [`string_literals`] of each and turning the escapes back gives `text` back.

15862.name: value
15862.docs:
VALUE: a blank cell reads as 0, but empty or blank text is not a number (observed:
`VALUE("")` is `#VALUE!`).

1766.name: pop_component
1766.docs:
Pops one finished component off Tarjan's stack, labelling its nodes with `comp_index`. The
component is everything up to and including `root`.

4382.name: object_param
4382.docs:
The floating object a `{kind, id}` command names on the active sheet. Unknown kinds and
objects are errors, so a stale id never succeeds silently.

21094.name: noun
21094.docs: The plural noun used in messages ("must hold numbers").

28869.name: MAX_ENCODED_CHARS
28869.docs:
Encoded characters of a script that are decoded: enough for its first [`MAX_SCRIPT_CHARS`]
characters of code, whatever its escapes. One character takes at most 14 encoded characters
(a UTF-16 pair of `_xHHHH_` escapes) and a `\r\n` line break becomes one character, so
`2 × (MAX_SCRIPT_CHARS + 1)` decoded characters cover the code kept, and two more escapes'
worth keep the last of them, and the line break after it, from being cut.

5836.name: simplex_program
5836.docs:
Builds the [`SimplexProgram`] at `x0`. The solve and the Sensitivity report both build it
here from the start values, so the report's solve repeats the solve's pivots and returns the
same vertex: linearising at another point changes the coefficients in their last bits, and
that can break a tie between pivots the other way.

17462.name: last_range
17462.docs: Area written by the last refresh.

27780.name: oversized_part
27780.docs: The first part whose declared unpacked size is over [`MAX_PART`], with that size.

3439.name: MAX_MATRIX_VARS
3439.docs: Most variables in a correlation or covariance matrix (work grows with its square).

20151.name: check_numbers
20151.docs:
Checks the numbers of a slider or spin button: 0 ≤ min < max ≤ 30000, 1 ≤ step ≤ max − min,
and (sliders) page ≥ step. Each rule has its own message.

13757.name: print_r1c1
13757.docs: Prints an expression in R1C1 notation relative to `at`.

11214.name: selection
11214.docs: That document's selection just before the command ran.

2277.name: plot_kind
2277.docs:
The kind series `i` is drawn as (per-series kinds only apply to combo charts); the same rule
as `series_plot_kind`, applied to the already resolved series kind.

27926.name: first_start
27926.docs:
The first element named `local_name` (namespace prefix dropped) in `xml`, read from its start tag alone: no children, and nothing after the tag is read, so unbalanced markup around it (a VML caption's unclosed `
`) neither hides nor moves it. `None` when there is none, or when the markup before it is malformed.

2350.name: draw_trendlines
2350.docs:
Draws `s`'s trendlines fitted to its plotted points `pts` (data x, y). `frac` maps data to
fractions of the plot box (0..1 inside, along the x and y axes), `px` fractions to pixels.
Equation and R² label lines are appended to `labels`. Degenerate fits draw nothing.

25456.name: date_shape
25456.docs:
For a date or time format, whether the section that formats `value` shows calendar parts (year, month,
day) and whether it shows time parts, as `(date, time)`. `None` for any other format and for
elapsed-time codes like `[h]:mm`, whose value is a duration, not a moment.

4966.name: heading_w
4966.docs: Heading sizes in sheet pixels (0 when headings are off).

30615.name: attach
30615.docs: Decodes a formula and attaches it to the cell at `pos`, or records why it can't be.

3731.name: whole
3731.docs: A whole-number parameter of at least `min`, `default` when absent.

8890.name: named
8890.docs: A defined name (by its formula) or a table (its data rows).

15430.name: lookup_order
15430.docs:
Order of two values for the approximate and binary searches: [`compare`], except that numbers
compare exactly. Excel's `=` treats numbers equal to 15 significant digits as equal, but its
lookups don't. Observed in Excel 365 with A1 holding
`=0.1+0.2` (0.30000000000000004): `A1=0.3` is TRUE, yet `MATCH(0.3,A1,1)` is #N/A because
A1 is larger, and in {0.1;0.2;0.3;A1;0.4} `MATCH(0.3,…,1)` is 3 and `MATCH(A1,…,1)` is 4.
The same holds for `=100+1E-14` against 100, and in every XLOOKUP / XMATCH mode.

5185.name: protect_workbook
5185.docs:
Review › Protect Workbook: lock the workbook structure (sheets can't be added, moved,
renamed, hidden or deleted), optionally with a password that unprotecting must match.

6493.name: NotOptimal
6493.docs:
Builds every report before the solution or saved model can change.
What happens to a Sensitivity report the model allows but the solution doesn't: `Refuse`
fails the call before anything changes; `Skip` leaves the report out, with its reason, and
writes the others. `optimum` is false when the solve stopped before an optimum, so the
report isn't attempted.

3950.name: clipped
3950.docs:
`text` cut to [`MAX_REPORTED_CHARS`] characters for the conversion report, with `…` when it was
cut. Counting characters keeps a multi-byte input whole.

1407.name: recalc
1407.docs:
Dependency graph and recalculation.

The graph maps every formula cell to its static precedents (resolved areas). A reverse index
answers "which formulas read this cell?": single-cell precedents in a hash map, ranges as row
intervals per column (wide ranges per sheet), each an interval index so a lookup costs
O(log n + matches) however many ranges share the column. After an edit, the dirty set is the
transitive closure of dependents; it is evaluated in topological order, with on-demand
evaluation as a safety net for dynamic references. Cycles produce `#CIRC!` unless iterative
calculation is on: then a formula read while it is being evaluated gives its previous value,
and the formulas that read one are evaluated again until the loop settles
(`PassHost::iterate_loops`).

14268.name: prepare
14268.docs:
field_headers: 0 none, 1 present but hidden, 2 generate, 3 present and shown; missing =
automatic (headers when the first value row is all text and the next is not).

5331.name: Converged
5331.docs: Almost all of the population is within Convergence of the best member.

4096.name: draw_pdf
4096.docs:
Draws an equation's layout into the box `(x, y, w, h)` (page points) of a PDF page, with
`pad` points of padding. Glyphs no standard font has are drawn as `[?]` boxes.

15649.name: aggregate_values
15649.docs:
Evaluates SUBTOTAL/AGGREGATE function `function_num` over already-filtered cell values.

Codes 1–11 (and 101–111) are AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTA, MAX, MIN, PRODUCT, STDEV.S, STDEV.P,
SUM, VAR.S, VAR.P; 12 = MEDIAN, 13 = MODE.SNGL. Codes 14–19 need `k`: use
[`aggregate_values_k`] (they give `#VALUE!` here). Values that are not numbers are ignored
(COUNTA counts non-empty values); the first error value present is returned.

27202.name: expand_year
27202.docs: Expands a one- or two-digit year the way typed input does (`26` is 2026, `30` is 1930).

8020.name: DECRYPTED_NOTICE
8020.docs: The first open warning of a workbook decrypted with its password.

const.expr: "This workbook was password-protected. GridCraft saves it without the password."

6785.name: more
6785.docs: Items past the cap, not listed. A caller says so rather than letting them vanish.

1699.name: spills_as_before
1699.docs:
Whether `arr`, anchored at `anchor`, would spill exactly what the sheet already holds over
`range`: the same area, nothing new in the way, and the same values.

13252.name: walk
13252.docs: Visits every node depth-first, parents before children, left to right.

6858.name: workbook_view_flag
6858.docs:
File › Options › Advanced › Display options for this workbook: the sheet tabs and the two
scroll bars, saved with the workbook (`<workbookView showSheetTabs … />`).

19719.name: data
19719.docs:
Encoded bytes (PNG/JPEG), base64 in JSON. Shared, so a copy of the sheet (an undo step)
doesn't copy the picture.

1845.name: Fmt
1845.docs: A number format prepared once and reused for many labels.

30110.name: Cursor
30110.docs: Reads a record's payload, crossing into its `Continue` records when needed.

28875.name: Missing
28875.docs:
A `PY(index, …)` call naming a script the part doesn't hold (or over the budget): the
cell keeps only its cached value, since no calculation can evaluate the formula.

14852.name: horizon
14852.docs: Position of a time stamp relative to the last point (0 = last point, 1 = next step).

25170.name: FractionLayout
25170.docs: Where a fraction section's parts are (see [`render_fraction`]).

30329.name: MAX_RECORDS
30329.docs:
Records read from the whole Workbook stream at most (a 65,536 × 256 sheet has fewer). One
allowance shared by every substream: many BoundSheet records pointing into one huge
substream must not each get their own.

12382.name: journal_sizes
12382.docs: Serialized size of each journal entry, measured once when it is pushed, and their sum.

3445.name: MAX_SEED
3445.docs: Largest seed: seeds are whole numbers that a JSON number holds exactly.

11147.name: compile
11147.docs:
Parses a calculated-field formula. `field` maps a written name to the canonical name of a
source or calculated field.

12455.name: depth
12455.docs:
How many commands are running: 0 between top-level commands, 1 inside one, 2 inside a
command run by a command, and so on.

2210.name: wedge
2210.docs: A wedge of `ring`, split at 12 o'clock when it crosses the end of the circle.

26624.name: SEGMENT
26624.docs: Agile packages are encrypted in segments of this many bytes, each with its own IV.

16379.name: Path
16379.docs: A vector outline (stretchy braces, arrows, radicals), relative to `(x, y)`.

2283.name: legend_entries
2283.docs: Legend entries (text, colour, swatch) `render` draws for this chart; empty when hidden.

27932.name: first_free_block
27932.docs:
The first shape block free in kept VML: GridCraft's own shapes (notes, then form controls) are
numbered from `block * 1024 + 1` when they join it ([`merge_vml`]).

18995.name: MoveAndSize
18995.docs: Move and size with cells (Excel's default; `<xdr:twoCellAnchor>`).

26697.name: decrypt
26697.docs: The plain OOXML package (a zip) inside an encrypted workbook.

25462.name: rounding_section
25462.docs:
The section whose digits "Set precision as displayed" rounds `n` by. Observed in Excel
(COM), this differs from the section that displays `n`:
- Conditions are ignored; the sign picks the section, the first for positives and the
  second for negatives. `[<1]0.00;0` shows 2.333 as `2` but stores 2.33, and stores -10/3
  as -3 although it shows `-3.00`. `[>1]0.0;0.000` stores 1/3 as 0.3.
- A format with a condition and a single number section keeps negatives at full value
  (`[<1]0.00`, `[>=-100]0.0`); with an `@` section added (`[<1]0.00;@`) negatives use the
  first section, as every format without a condition does.
- A completely empty section (no characters, not even a colour) passes to the next one:
  `0.0;;0.000` stores -2.333 as -2.333, `;0.0` stores 2.333 as 2.3, `;;0.0` too. A section
  with only a colour or a literal (`0.0;[Red];0.000`, `0.0;" "`) has no digits and keeps
  the full value.

`None` keeps the full value.

4972.name: hf_text_scale
4972.docs: Scale of header and footer text: the print scale with Scale with Document on, otherwise 1.

2429.name: CYCLE_TINTS
2429.docs: Tints used for series beyond the six theme accents: lighter, darker, lighter still…

15290.name: nq
15290.docs: Whole quasi-coupon periods between settlement and the first coupon.

1194.name: deref
1194.docs:
Dereferences: one cell → its value; a block → an array; several areas → `#VALUE!`.

A block keeps its full shape (blanks included) when it holds at most `FULL_SIZE_CELLS`
cells, or when it holds at most `FULL_SIZE_BOUNDED_CELLS` cells (one full column's worth)
and does not run to the sheet's last row or column. Every other block (larger, or a
bigger one that runs to the sheet's edge, such as `A:A` or `1:1`) is trimmed to the
sheet's used range before its values are read. An array over `MAX_CELLS` is `#NUM!`.

8896.name: span
8896.docs: `a..b` with open ends filled from 1 and `len`.

3810.name: Policy
3810.docs: Whether a command may run as a macro step.

11512.name: doc_uid
11512.docs: The [`DocState::uid`] of the workbook it shows.

28224.name: write_workbook
28224.docs:
Writes the workbook's kept parts and relationships. Chart sheets that can't be written back
(see [`chart_sheet_usable`]) are left out with the parts only they reach.

7734.name: flash_fill
7734.docs:
Flash Fill: learns a transformation from the examples typed in the column of `at` (rows
above it with values) from the column(s) to the left, and fills the remaining rows.
Supported transformations: a token (word) of the source by index, concatenations of tokens
with literal separators, upper/lower/proper case, and fixed-position substrings.

15436.name: bsearch_upto
15436.docs:
Binary search for the last entry not ordered after the needle (`<= x` ascending, `>= x`
descending).

26989.name: agile
26989.docs:
Decrypts an Agile package ([MS-OFFCRYPTO] 2.3.4.10): checks the password against the
verifier, unwraps the package key, verifies the dataIntegrity HMAC, then decrypts the segments.

9115.name: prepare
9115.docs:
Binds the macro's inputs on the active document (`given`: `{"Input": "B2:D9"}`, or a reference
for the first input) and checks them. Errors list every problem found.

14274.name: pivot_dims
14274.docs:
Height and width of a PIVOTBY grid: `header_rows` (one per column field, plus the value-name row) and
`body_rows` (row keys plus the total row), each `lead` row-field cells wide plus `value_cols` cells per column key.

30986.name: encode_xstring
30986.docs:
ST_Xstring encoding for cell text: characters XML can't carry and carriage returns become
`_xHHHH_`, and literal `_xHHHH_` sequences are protected with `_x005F_`. The result still needs
[`esc`].

24592.name: MAX_DECIMALS
24592.docs: Most decimals we ever compute; placeholders beyond this are padded with zeros.

10496.name: RowKind
10496.docs: What a report row is (for row-wide styling).

7953.name: reference_at
7953.docs:
The A1 text of the R1C1 reference starting at `i`, and the index after it, or `None` when the
word there isn't a reference (a function or a name).

11804.name: doc
11804.docs: The uid of the document the group belongs to.

27208.name: read_field
27208.docs: Reads one field with the column's date rule; other values go through typed input.

16963.name: cellmap
16963.docs:
Serde helpers for maps keyed by `CellRef`. JSON object keys must be strings, so the keys are
written as `A1`-style text.

20814.name: MAX_MACRO_TEXT
20814.docs: The longest macro description, step note, Stop message or If value (as JSON), in characters.

8026.name: DecryptError
8026.docs: Why an encrypted workbook couldn't be decrypted.

20887.name: check_text
20887.docs:
Refuses `text` longer than `max` characters, and, for a one-line field, one that holds line
breaks or other control characters.

11950.name: areas
11950.docs:
A multi-area copy: the areas as selected (for the marquee). `wb` then holds them slid
together into one block at `range`. Empty for a single-range copy.

22268.name: show_outline_symbols
22268.docs:
The outline's level buttons and brackets (Excel's Show Outline Symbols, Ctrl+8); the
outline itself stays.

4321.name: rename_name_in_formulas

3086.name: StatsNeed
3086.docs:
Which statistics a rule reads. Scanning the rule's whole range for them costs O(range), so
rules that read none (cell value, formula, text, blanks, errors, dates) never scan.

543.name: parse_input
543.docs:
Interprets typed cell input (not formulas). Text that isn't a number, date, boolean or error
stays text. A leading apostrophe forces text.

4394.name: open_link
4394.docs:
Follows a link: a reference selects it; anything else is refused ([`crate::engine::links::classify`]).
An `http`/`https`/`mailto` address is refused too unless the host set
[`crate::engine::links::LinkPolicy::Allow`]: every caller of a command may be a script or an agent, so
the user opens such links by clicking and confirming, and the UI then calls
[`Session::open_confirmed_link`] (#2181). Opens no dialog.

4467.name: shift_values
4467.docs:
Keeps Σ Values in place after a field left (`inserted` false) or arrived at index `i` of
Rows (`rows`) or Columns.

8318.name: links
8318.docs:
Which hyperlink targets may be opened. A cell's link comes from the document (often a file
somebody sent), so it is hostile input: only `http`, `https` and `mailto` ever leave the
workbook for the system; `file:`, `smb:`, UNC paths, custom URL handlers, `javascript:` and
the like are refused. Everything without a scheme stays an in-workbook reference.

Opening an allowed address also needs the user's say-so (#2181): `link.open` is reachable by
the control channel, the CLI, MCP and workbook scripts, so a prompt-injected agent could open
`https://attacker/?d=<cell data>`. Under the default [`LinkPolicy::Confirm`] the command refuses
external addresses; only the host, after showing the address and getting OK from the user,
opens one through [`crate::engine::Session::open_confirmed_link`], which no command reaches.

10934.name: Calc
10934.docs: A calculated field (index into the PivotTable's calculated fields).

27646.name: omml
27646.docs:
Equations in drawings: Office Math Markup (ECMA-376 Part 1 §22.1) read back into LaTeX for the
common subset, the inverse of `crate::math::to_omml`. A construct outside the subset makes
the whole equation unreadable as maths (`None`), and the caller keeps it as a text box.

835.name: eval
835.docs:
The formula evaluator.

Expressions evaluate to [`Ev`]: a value, a reference (one or more areas, kept unresolved so
`ROW`, `OFFSET`, `INDEX`, `:` and friends can work on references) or a lambda. Cell reads go
through [`Host`], which lets the recalculation engine evaluate dirty precedents on demand.

12388.name: hide_ruler
12388.docs: View › Show › Ruler is off (rulers in Page Layout view; an application option).

8610.name: Recorded
8610.docs: Run while recording: plain parameters, which may become relative.

9918.name: parse_chart_link
9918.docs: (sheet, PivotTable name) of a PivotChart link; a leading `[Book.xlsx]` is ignored.

2289.name: decimate_area
2289.docs:
Decimates the top and baseline of an area chart together at the same horizontal indices so
`area_mesh`'s paired vertical-strip topology (`pts[i]` ↔ `pts[2n - 1 - i]`) is preserved.

29246.name: MAX_HYPERLINK_BYTES
29246.docs:
Target and tooltip bytes kept for hyperlinks of one sheet, over all cells: the same URL is
copied for every cell of its range, so length × cells must stay bounded whatever the file.

15223.name: disc_args
15223.docs: settlement, maturity, value, value, [basis] for discount securities.

8829.name: inputs
8829.docs: Declared inputs, with whether each has a header row.

2435.name: parse_ref
2435.docs: Splits `Sheet!A1:B2` / `'My Sheet'!$A$1` / `A1:B2` into a sheet index and range.

17839.name: legacy_password_hash
17839.docs:
The internal hash older GridCraft JSON workbooks stored ([`password_hash`]); still
verified when unprotecting, never written for new passwords.

21763.name: rel_id
21763.docs: The id of the workbook relationship to the chart sheet part, in the source file.

14134.name: opt_count
14134.docs: An optional integer argument where a missing or blank argument means `None`.

7740.name: Tok
7740.docs: Token index (negative from the end) with a case transform.

26995.name: differing
26995.docs:
High bytes that decode to different characters in the two code pages, apart from invisible
marks and ordinals after a digit.

11664.name: formula
11664.docs:
The Excel formula language: tokenizer, parser, syntax tree, printer (A1 and R1C1) and
reference adjustment for copy/fill and structural edits.

30919.name: path
30919.docs: Follows a path of child names.

14280.name: hankel
14280.docs: Hankel asymptotic expansion: (J_n(x), Y_n(x)) for large x.

4035.name: GO_TO_RECENT
4035.docs: How many references the Go To dialog keeps for going back to.

29684.name: image_part
29684.docs:
The `xl/media` file name (`imageN.ext`) holding `data`. A picture used on several sheets,
or twice on one, is written once and every drawing points to that part, as in Excel.

15588.name: reg_gamma_p
15588.docs: Regularised lower incomplete gamma P(a, x).

30992.name: si_body
30992.docs:
The contents of a shared string item (`<si>`): the base text, then — when the string has
phonetic (furigana) data — its `<rPh sb="…" eb="…"><t>…</t></rPh>` runs in document order and
its `<phoneticPr …/>`. Behaviour reference: ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.4.8 `si` with §18.4.6 `rPh` and
§18.4.7 `phoneticPr`. A string without phonetic data gives exactly [`t_el`]'s output.

The runs and the properties are independent: `<phoneticPr>` is a valid child of `<si>` on its
own (§18.4.8's `CT_SharedStringItem` allows it without any `rPh`), so a string whose runs were
all dropped still keeps its settings.

16896.name: value
16896.docs: Constant value, or the cached result of the formula or Python code.

24598.name: fixed
24598.docs: Rounds a non-negative number to `decimals` places (see [`fixed_from_digits`]).

4108.name: recent_functions
4108.docs:
Formulas › Recently Used: the functions most recently entered in a formula, newest first
(at most [`recent::MAX`]; see [`recent`]). An application list, as in Excel.

1565.name: unsettled_cols
1565.docs: Range indexes changed since the last [`Graph::settle`].

27214.name: write_csv
27214.docs:
Writes the sheet as CSV from A1 to the end of its used range, so leading empty columns and rows
stay as empty fields and every cell keeps its position (CRLF line ends, UTF-8 without BOM). `cell_text` gives
each cell's field text: the caller decides how values look (Save As CSV writes them as
displayed, number formats applied); quoting is done here.

The output is capped at [`MAX_CSV_BYTES`]: a cell far from A1 makes the file as big as the whole
rectangle between them (`A1` and `XFD1048576` are 16 GiB of commas).
An export that would pass the cap is refused before anything is allocated, or at the first
field or line end that takes it past the cap (a field is measured before it is written), with
[`IoError::TooLarge`]; accepted exports keep every field in its place.

2873.name: secondary
2873.docs: Plotted against the secondary (right) value axis.

8032.name: sane_python_output
8032.docs:
A Python result a file may hold: a scalar, or an array whose size matches its data and has at
most [`crate::model::python::MAX_RESULT_CELLS`] cells.

29830.name: SupBook
29830.docs:
A supporting link ([MS-XLS] 2.4.271): only links to this workbook (and add-in function
names) are resolved; external workbooks are never followed.

1638.name: waiting
1638.docs:
Formulas whose evaluation was abandoned for another one, to be calculated again after it.
They all need it, so reading one of them while it is calculated is a circular reference,
as reading a formula in progress is.

20893.name: estimated_bytes
20893.docs:
A rough size of the list in memory, for the undo budget: each macro's JSON, which holds
every name, text and step parameter, plus its structs. An undo step that keeps a copy of
the list (after a save, rename or delete) is charged for all of it. The JSON is counted as
it is written, without building it.

28595.name: PivotWriter
28595.docs:
PivotTables being written; the tables themselves are finished after the styles part (their
value number formats need style number-format ids).

9413.name: describe_conflicts
9413.docs: "C2:C9 on Sheet1, the sheet Old, 2 objects".

6870.name: MAX_HEADER_FOOTER
6870.docs: Excel keeps at most 255 characters per header or footer.

28741.name: MAX_RECORD_CELLS
28741.docs: Largest records snapshot written (cells); bigger caches are written without records.

15953.name: opt_num
15953.docs: Optional number: `default` when missing, otherwise coerced (an explicit empty is 0).

24963.name: split_sections
24963.docs:
Splits a code into sections at unquoted, unescaped, unbracketed semicolons.

A `[` opens a bracket only when a `]` follows it; the bracket then runs to the next `]` (quotes
inside it are not special), exactly as `tokenize` reads it. An unclosed `[` is a literal in both
passes, so a later `;` still separates sections. Linear: each `[` either jumps over its bracket
or, with no `]` left in the code, is a literal at once.

4473.name: calc_field
4473.docs: The calculated field named `field`, if any.

9632.name: time_limit
9632.docs: The run's `timeLimit` (seconds) in milliseconds, or the default.

3238.name: MAX_SIDE
3238.docs: Widest or tallest chart written; larger anchors are clamped.

27652.name: count_math
27652.docs:
How many `m:oMath`/`m:oMathPara` elements are under `e` (not counting those inside one), to
the same bounded depth as [`find_math`], stopping at two.

9705.name: parse_shortcut
9705.docs:
The letter of a macro shortcut: `"Ctrl+Shift+M"`, `"Cmd+Shift+M"`, `"⌘⇧M"` and `"m"` all give
`'M'`. `None` when it is not one letter from A to Z, alone or after Ctrl+Shift (Cmd+Shift):
other modifiers (`"Ctrl+Alt+M"`) are refused rather than read as Ctrl+Shift.

8470.name: debug
8470.docs:
`macro.debug {name?, inputs?, action: start|step|continue|runTo|stop|state, step?, keep?,
breakpoints?, breakpointsOnly?}`.

30268.name: font
30268.docs: A Font record. The colour is resolved later, once the palette is known.

9778.name: summary_below
9778.docs:
Outline summary rows sit below their detail, and summary columns right of it (Data ▸
Outline ▸ Settings; off puts them above / left). Saved as `outlinePr summaryBelow` and
`summaryRight`.

3384.name: covered_until
3384.docs: Per column: the row index (exclusive) down to which a `rowspan` from above covers it.

29033.name: TitleSpan
29033.docs: A print-titles span: the first and last row (or column) repeated on each page.

8543.name: DENIED_PREFIXES
8543.docs: Prefixes of commands that never run in a macro, with the reason.

12394.name: macro_approvals
12394.docs:
Macros the person allowed to run in this session: (document uid, the macro's content as
canonical JSON, from [`macros::fingerprint`]).

16245.name: symbol
16245.docs: The character a symbol name (`\alpha`, `(`, `\langle`) stands for.

22712.name: major_font_cs
22712.docs: The heading font's complex-script typeface (`<a:cs>`); empty when the file did not set one.

9924.name: Output
9924.docs: A computed report: a dense grid relative to its top-left, with row kinds.

29252.name: MAX_DYNAMIC_RANGES
29252.docs: Most dynamic-array and legacy-array ranges of one sheet.

2368.name: MAX_MARKERS
2368.docs: Most markers per series (after de-duplicating by pixel).

6219.name: model_formulas
6219.docs: The cells Save Model writes, top to bottom, as formula text.

3676.name: input_rows
3676.docs: The cells of a two-factor input range, row by row.

1133.name: range_values
1133.docs: Values of a block, row-major. Hosts can override with a sparse fast path.

2441.name: ref_format
2441.docs: Number format code of the first cell of a reference ("General" when not a reference).

28090.name: part_rels_xml
28090.docs: A kept part's relationships, ids unchanged, targets renamed.

2514.name: fit_trendline
2514.docs:
Fits `t` to the points `(x, y)`. `None` for moving averages and degenerate data (too few
usable points, all x equal, a singular system, non-finite results).

3822.name: with_action_names
3822.docs:
A copy of `wb` for xlsx with the button actions xlsx can't express (commands, fixed inputs,
output cells) in a hidden name, keyed by sheet name and the control's place on the sheet, with
the button's name and anchor cell to check it is still the same button when the file comes
back. `None` when there is nothing to store.

15375.name: EURO_RATES
15375.docs:
The currencies EUROCONVERT documents: ISO code, the irrevocable conversion rate in units per
euro (Council Regulation (EC) No 2866/98 as amended) and the calculation precision in decimals.

28236.name: MAX_KEPT_TOTAL
28236.docs: Most bytes kept for one workbook.

14140.name: cmp_keys
14140.docs: Compares two key vectors with per-key orders (1 ascending, -1 descending).

29544.name: with_agile_header
29544.docs: `EncryptionInfo` for an Agile descriptor: version 4.4, reserved 0x40, then the XML.

1352.name: calc
1352.docs:
GridCraft's calculation engine: the evaluator (references, names, tables, LET/LAMBDA,
dynamic arrays) and dependency-driven recalculation with spills and cycle detection.

5203.name: anchor_corner
5203.docs:
Bottom-right line of an anchor (the `to` marker of a two-cell anchor) and the offset of that
corner inside it, in points. Measured against `sh`'s current geometry.

27001.name: is_arabic
27001.docs:
Thresholds chosen against month, day and language names from 95 glibc locales (Western in
Windows-1252, Arabic, Persian and Urdu in 1256, Hebrew and Yiddish in 1255) plus CSV samples.

11670.name: numfmt
11670.docs:
GridCraft number formats: Excel format codes (`#,##0.00;[Red](#,##0.00)`, dates, fractions,
scientific…), the General display format and the `TEXT()` worksheet function. en-US only.

14286.name: bessel_k
14286.docs:
K_n(x) for x > 0: K_0 and K_1 from ∫₀^∞ e^{−x cosh t} cosh(νt) dt (trapezoid rule), then
upward recurrence.

4041.name: go_to_target
4041.docs:
Where one part of a Go To reference points, seen from sheet `sheet`: the sheet, its areas,
and whether a defined name or a table gave them. `Sheet2!Name` is the name scoped to Sheet2.
A name counts when what it refers to is a reference; a constant or a formula is not one.

7892.name: read
7892.docs: Reads a SYLK file into a one-sheet workbook. Returns the workbook and its warnings.

16902.name: styled
16902.docs: A value cell with this style.

22061.name: unescape
22061.docs:
The text of a plain literal's contents: `\'`, `\"` and `\\` stand for the character after the
backslash. `None` for any other escape or a line break, which make the literal not plain.

6730.name: LITERAL_UNITS
6730.docs: Characters (UTF-16 units, as Excel counts them) in one string literal.

8038.name: rename_first_sheet
8038.docs: A CSV opens as a sheet named after the file (like Excel).

1644.name: stack
1644.docs: Formulas being evaluated, innermost last (kept only when iterating).

9346.name: partial
9346.docs: Where the footprint stopped, if it did: "step 2 (file.exportCsv writes a file)".

1717.name: recalc_all
1717.docs: Recalculates every formula (F9 / Ctrl+Alt+F9, and after loading).

20972.name: rows
20972.docs: Allowed data rows (header excluded), `[min, max]`; a max of 0 means no limit.

6876.name: Compare
6876.docs: Column offset in the list, comparison operator and operand text.

482.name: civil_from_days
482.docs:
Proleptic Gregorian `(year, month, day)` for a day count `z` since 1970-01-01 (the inverse of
[`days_from_civil`]).

The calendar repeats every 400 years (146_097 days): chrono converts the day within its cycle
and whole cycles go back into the year (an i128 so no `z` overflows), which matches the
proleptic Gregorian answer the old hand-rolled code gave past `NaiveDate`'s ±262143 range.
1970-01-01 is `num_days_from_ce` 719_163.

4333.name: trace_error
4333.docs:
Trace Error: from the cell, the first reference in its formula that shows the same error
(in a range, the range's first cell showing it, row by row), then that cell's, and so on to the
cell the error starts in: one none of whose references shows it, or one without references.
Arrows link the cells on the way, and lead from the source's own references into it.

555.name: parse_time
555.docs: Time part: `h:mm`, `h:mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss.000`, `h AM`, with optional AM/PM.

28820.name: PART
28820.docs: Part name we write (the format names none; the relationship finds it).

8330.name: breakpoints
8330.docs: Breakpoints set for this run (step paths), on top of the steps' own.

12181.name: JOURNAL_MAX_BYTES
12181.docs:
Past this many bytes (entries serialized as JSON) the journal drops its oldest entries until
it is under half. Entries keep their full params so they replay (recorded scripts,
`engine.journal`), and a `file.open` holds the whole file as base64: without a size cap a
few opens of a large workbook keep tens of MB alive.

9638.name: check_limits
9638.docs:
Checks every field a file can set: the format version ([`check_version`]); the lengths of
the name, description, shortcut, notes, messages, references and command ids; the counts of
steps ([`MAX_MACRO_STEPS`]), inputs, permissions and column types; the nesting depth
([`MAX_MACRO_DEPTH`]); and each input's declaration. Command parameters are bounded only by
the size of the whole macro, which [`MAX_MACRO_STEPS`] and the workbook's item limit cap.
Every struct is taken apart field by field, so a field added later doesn't compile here
until someone decides its limit.

14797.name: Months
14797.docs:
Whole-day dates a constant number of calendar months apart, all on the same day of the
month (`day = Some(d)`) or all on the last day of their month (`day = None`).

4552.name: PivotDateGroup
4552.docs: Grouping of a date field (values are date serials).

2009.name: ChartData
2009.docs: Resolved data: series names, categories and values pulled from the workbook.

27658.name: group
27658.docs: `{…}` around a child's contents (empty group when the child is missing).

9711.name: MAX_LEVEL
9711.docs: The deepest outline level XLSX allows.

9784.name: margins
9784.docs: Left, right, top, bottom, header and footer margins in layout units.

3390.name: finish
3390.docs:
Closes the open cell (if any) into the current row, decoding its text: first past the
columns a `rowspan` above still covers, then the cell, then a placeholder per extra column.

8549.name: writes_file
8549.docs: Whether command `id` with `params` writes a file (an export or print given a `path`).

12400.name: comments_pane
12400.docs: Review › Show Comments: the Comments pane is open.

29112.name: read_cf
29112.docs:
One `conditionalFormatting` block. Every rule keeps its own copy of the block's ranges, so
`kept_cells` counts the range cells the sheet's retained rules hold so far, across blocks; a
rule that would take it past [`MAX_COND_CELLS`] is dropped. Unsupported rules cost nothing.

26569.name: shape_number
26569.docs: The shape number of a VML shape id (`_x0000_s1025` → 1025) or a `shapeId` attribute.

16324.name: total_height
16324.docs: Total height (height plus depth), in em.

9930.name: detail_cells
9930.docs:
The cells of the report grid (relative to its top-left) where [`detail_records`] finds
records: its value, subtotal and grand total cells, from one computation of the report. The
same errors as [`detail_records`].

13781.name: same_name
13781.docs:
Whether two LET/LAMBDA names are the same: case-insensitive in any script, as in Excel
(`dług` = `DŁUG`, `ß` = `ẞ`). Close to Unicode's default case folding: lower case, plus the
folds lower-casing misses for letters a name may hold (`ß`/`ẞ` -> `ss`, `ſ` -> `s`, `ς` -> `σ`).
Dotless `ı` stays distinct from `i`, as outside Turkic languages.

27950.name: elements
27950.docs:
The kept sheet elements, in schema order, with GridCraft's own form control entries
(`controls`, see `controls::write`) in the sheet's one `<controls>` element.

3609.name: matrix_vars
3609.docs: Variables of a range whose columns (rows) must all be numbers, for the matrix tools.

25407.name: num_sections
25407.docs: Sections that apply to numbers (a trailing text section is excluded).

29258.name: read_password
29258.docs:
A protection password hash: the iterated attributes (`algorithmName`, `hashValue`,
`saltValue`, `spinCount`) or the legacy 16-bit `password`, each name preceded by `prefix`
(`workbook` gives `workbookHashValue`…). One that can't be read keeps a hash that never
matches, so what it protects stays locked rather than open.

6225.name: read_constraint_row
6225.docs: One constraint row of Save Model (`AND(relation)`) as a `data.solver` constraint.

3682.name: z_test
3682.docs: z-Test: Two Sample for Means, for two samples whose population variances are known.

2447.name: plot_kind
2447.docs:
The kind series `i` is drawn as: its own kind in a combo chart (first series a column, the
rest lines when it has none), else the chart's. The one rule shared by resolving and drawing.

7606.name: holds_source_in_corner
7606.docs:
Whether `target` is a shape Excel's AutoFill accepts for `src`: it contains the source and the
source sits in one of its corners. Excel refuses a target that doesn't contain the source
(`2:3` into `A:A`, `H4:H9` into `D:F`) or holds it away from every corner (`H4:H9` into `H:H`).

11457.name: sheet_name
11457.docs:
The active sheet's name, so a sheet inserted, deleted or moved meanwhile in another
window still finds it.

1212.name: TrimMode
1212.docs: Which blank edges a trim reference drops.

20467.name: anchor
20467.docs: `None`: the shape's default (top for text boxes, middle for other shapes).

2520.name: num_text
2520.docs: A coefficient as trendline labels show it: up to four decimals, scientific when tiny or huge.

28242.name: MAX_FRAGMENT
28242.docs: Largest kept XML fragment of a sheet.

15454.name: quote_sheet
15454.docs:
Sheet text for ADDRESS, quoted when Excel quotes it. A `[Book]Sheet` prefix is judged by its
parts (Microsoft's ADDRESS examples: `"[Book1]Sheet1"` stays bare, `"EXCEL SHEET"` becomes
`'EXCEL SHEET'`). Unlike in a formula, `TRUE` and `FALSE` stay bare.

9060.name: gate
9060.docs:
Checks every enabled step against the policy: denied commands and undeclared file access are
errors; otherwise returns what the person must approve (empty when nothing).

4047.name: MAX_PASTE_LINK_CELLS
4047.docs:
Most cells one Paste Link writes (it writes a formula into every cell of the copied area,
blank ones included).

14365.name: parse_complex
14365.docs: Parses "a+bi" forms. Returns the number and its suffix ('i', 'j' or none).

9279.name: stopped
9279.docs: A Stop step ended the run: its message, and whether it asked for a rollback.

6736.name: items
6736.docs:
The items whose key starts with `prefix` (`"macro_"`), by lower-cased key, read in one pass
over the names: the first [`MAX_ITEMS`] items that can be read, and the count of the readable
ones past them. An item over the size limit is neither listed nor counted, so it takes no
place another item could have. ([`keys`] lists keys without reading the items.)

4193.name: max_periods
4193.docs: Most forecast rows for `history` rows of history.

1650.name: out_of_stack
1650.docs: Whether an evaluation ran past the stack budget since the innermost formula started.

27299.name: NS
27299.docs: Namespace of the part and of the `xfComplement` element.

29915.name: skipped
29915.docs: Per defined name: whether the import skips it (its formula can't be decoded).

488.name: days_in_month_in
488.docs:
Days in a month of a date system's calendar: like [`days_in_month`], except that February
1900 has 29 days in the 1900 system (serial 60 is the fictitious 1900-02-29).

4339.name: number_stored_as_text
4339.docs:
The number a cell's text stands for when Excel's background check flags it as a number stored
as text: a constant (not a formula's result) that would be a number if typed.

8263.name: Internal
8263.docs: A cell, range, name or table of the workbook (`Sheet2!A1`, `Total`).

15965.name: numbers_a

Numbers for the "A" aggregates (AVERAGEA, MAXA, STDEVA…): inside references and arrays text
counts as 0 and booleans as 1/0, blanks are skipped; direct arguments coerce as in
[`numbers`].

28826.name: budget

4485.name: AreaPlacement

8336.name: shifted

12187.name: push_entry

Adds a step without applying the limits: inside a command they wait for the outermost
command to collapse its steps (see [`Session::trim_history`]).

5793.name: solve_lp
5793.docs: Minimises `c·x` subject to `rows` (coefficients, sense, rhs) and `lo ≤ x ≤ hi`.

9644.name: MAX_MACROS
9644.docs: The most macros a workbook keeps.

7101.name: string_literals
7101.docs: Concatenates the string literals of a `"a"&"b""c"` formula.

22505.name: retained_bytes_against
22505.docs:
Approximate heap storage kept alive by this snapshot's bands that `newer` no longer
shares. This is for bounding Undo history, not for reporting process memory: BTreeMap
nodes and allocator overhead vary by platform. Shared formulas and values are counted
only when the newer band no longer holds the same Arc.

27664.name: escape_text
27664.docs:
Appends `s` escaped for `\text{…}`; `None` once the LaTeX exceeds [`MAX_OUT_BYTES`], checked
after every character so that a long run never expands in full.

9717.name: OutlineGroup
9717.docs:
One group: lines `start..=end` at outline level `level` or deeper, with its summary line
just after `end`, or just before `start` when `summary_before` is set.

8482.name: StepError

14949.name: line

26502.name: write

control `i`'s VML shape id.

12406.name: group_step
12406.docs: Where the last group ended, so `execute` can tell a command's own changes from its group's.

16257.name: span

27883.name: legacy_drawing_hf
27883.docs: The relationship id on `<legacyDrawingHF>` (header and footer pictures).

8701.name: ran
8701.docs:
What a step ran, by its index in `steps`, for a command that runs steps stored in the
workbook (`automate.runScript`, `macro.run`): the commands as they ran, so a recording
keeps them even when the script or macro is edited or deleted before the recording stops.
A run without an entry is left out when the recording is used.

6158.name: max_evals
6158.docs: The evaluation limit (in place of Excel's iterations and time limits).

3615.name: coef

20400.name: ShapeTextAnchor
20400.docs: Vertical anchor of a shape's text in its box (`a:bodyPr anchor`).

6304.name: eval
6304.docs: Evaluates the model at `x`; `None` once the budget is spent.

14006.name: lower_char
14006.docs:
Lowercase one char to exactly one char, so positions in the lowered text match the original
(U+0130 `İ` folds to `i`, like `fold` in text.rs).

21708.name: xml
21708.docs: The element, namespace declarations it needs included.

7612.name: Linear

`serial` moved by `n` weekdays (back when `n` is negative), keeping its time of day. A start on
a Saturday or Sunday moves to the next (or previous) weekday for the first step.

8993.name: interpolate

Replaces each `{{token}}` in `s`. `{{{{` is a literal `{{`, for text that needs the braces
themselves (`"Dear {{{{name}}"` writes `Dear {{name}}`).

24397.name: custom_lists

6450.name: ReportInput

28248.name: WORKBOOK_ROOTS
28248.docs: Relationship kinds kept from the workbook without a workbook element.

3907.name: remove_validation_cells
3907.docs:
Removes the cells of `cuts` from every validation, keeping the rest of each rule's ranges.
When the rule's top-left cell goes, its relative formulas are rewritten for the new top-left
cell, so the cells left keep checking the same cells.

14225.name: agg_arg

The function argument of GROUPBY/PIVOTBY: a built-in aggregation, or `None` for a LAMBDA (called
through the context).

25778.name: text_width

5288.name: better

22000.name: py_body

`text` without a leading `=`, spaces and the `_xlfn.` and `_xlws.` prefixes files put before
newer functions (in any letter case).

4053.name: Edit

15606.name: sorted_if_monotone
15606.docs:
Sorts `v` if it is already monotone in `total_cmp` order (a descending slice is reversed) and
says whether it did. At most two passes, each stopping at the first out-of-order pair, so
unordered data costs next to nothing. Needed because the std sort recognises ascending and
descending runs in O(n) with a small constant; selection is O(n) too but measured 1.2-1.8x
slower on such input.

28467.name: items
28467.docs: Group item captions, including the `<start` and `>end` items.

9285.name: guard
9285.docs:
Set unless the macro may overwrite: each step is checked for writes over data as it runs,
since the footprint can miss a write (it stopped early, or the run took another path).

4199.name: number
4199.docs: A number parameter given as a number or as text.

1656.name: MAX_RESULT_CELLS
1656.docs: The most cells a Python result may have (a crafted file can claim any size).

27305.name: checkbox_xf_ext
27305.docs: The `extLst` that marks an `xf` as a checkbox (complement index 0 of [`checkbox_part`]).

9577.name: diff
9577.docs:
Compares the workbook before and after a dry run. `touched` adds the cells commands wrote
without changing them (a formula written again), so a shift moves everything the macro writes.

26289.name: chart
26289.docs:
DrawingML charts (`xl/charts/chartN.xml`): reading the common 2-D/3-D chart groups into the
model, and writing model charts (with cached series values) from scratch.

8342.name: executed
8342.docs: The run's own steps so far.

9650.name: fingerprint
9650.docs:
A macro's content as canonical JSON text (object keys sorted): approval to run a macro holds
until the macro changes. It is the text itself rather than a hash, so no two different macros
share it.

9796.name: page_order
9796.docs: The sheet's page order, which numbers the printed pages.

21349.name: Empty
21349.docs: The cell is empty (`value` is ignored).

11104.name: refs
11104.docs: Canonical names of the fields used.

8561.name: NamedInput
8561.docs: A range the macro works on, with the shape and content it expects.

12412.name: active_window
12412.docs: The active window's id (`None` with no workbook open).

2167.name: largest_slices
2167.docs:
At most `cap` of the largest values, in category order. When a ring has more categories than
its share of the wedge budget allows, the big slices survive rather than the first ones.

17571.name: features
17571.docs:
Sheet features beyond cells: tables, conditional formatting, data validation, comments,
hyperlinks, charts, images, autofilter, print settings.

932.name: try_zip2
932.docs:
[`zip2`] that stops at the first cell `f` refuses (`None`), before the rest is built: the
result grows as cells are made rather than being reserved for the whole broadcast up front.

8707.name: ref_token
8707.docs:
The token for an A1 reference on the example's sheet near the example input. `here` says whether
an unqualified reference is on that sheet.

17717.name: OverThenDown
17717.docs: Across the first row of pages, then across the next one.

12631.name: map_span
12631.docs: Adjusts a span `[lo, hi]` (inclusive) on one axis.

6237.name: check_column_empty
6237.docs:
Refused, unless `overwrite`, when a cell of the model's column holds a value, a formula or
Python code (a model saved there before included): Save Model then asks before it replaces
data, as Excel does. The message carries [`OVERWRITE_ERROR`], which the dialog turns into its
question.

14012.name: wildcard_find
14012.docs:
SEARCH-style find: the char index (0-based) of the first position at or after `start` where
the wildcard pattern matches, case-insensitively.

5075.name: segments
5075.docs: Segments of a page along one axis: repeated titles (before the band) then the band.

28181.name: sheet_entries
28181.docs:
The `<sheet>` entries of the chart sheets that go right before the model's sheet `i`
(`i` = the number of sheets for those that come last), with their ids from `ids`.

3840.name: detail
3840.docs:
Hide Detail / Show Detail: the innermost group (or the one at `level`) that holds the lines, or
failing that the one they are the summary of. Hiding marks the summary line collapsed (the
+ button, saved to XLSX); showing keeps inner groups that were collapsed on their own collapsed.

1297.name: call_lambda
1297.docs: A LAMBDA must give one value per group; an array result is #CALC!.

5148.name: PicCache
5148.docs: Decoded pictures (bytes, width, height) keyed by (sheet, picture); `None` = undecodable.

8999.name: run
8999.docs:
Running a macro.

1. **Gate**: every step's command goes through [`macro_policy`]. Denied commands stop the macro
   before anything runs; commands that touch files must be listed in the macro's permissions;
   a macro from a file someone else made, or one that touches files, runs only once the person
   approves it (once per macro content, for the session).
2. **Inputs**: each declared input is bound to a range (given, its default, or the selection)
   and checked against its shape and column types, with messages that name the cells.
3. **Footprint**: unless the macro may overwrite, it first runs on the real workbook in dry-run
   mode, the changes are compared with `CellStore::diff`, and everything is put back. Cells it
   would write outside its inputs that already hold data are conflicts, handled by the output
   rule: ask, fail, overwrite, or shift the data down or right (and check again). The
   footprint can miss a write (a dry run stops early at a file step or Solver, and RAND or NOW
   can send the run another way than the dry run), so the run also checks each step as it goes.
4. **Run**: one undo step (`Session::grouped`); an error at any step rolls everything back and
   names the step.

The steps run on a small machine with an explicit frame stack, so the debugger can stop
between any two steps and pick up again on a later frame.

24403.name: macros
24403.docs:
GridCraft macros (typed command lists, not VBA), in the order the macro list shows them.
The JSON format keeps them as this field; xlsx keeps them in hidden defined names.

28254.name: SHEET_SLOTS
28254.docs: Kept sheet elements, in schema order (all after `<legacyDrawing>`, before `<tableParts>`).

3913.name: list_items
3913.docs:
List entries of a list validation (literal or from a range) for the cell `at`. A relative
source is written for the rule's top-left cell and read from `at`, as in Excel (`=$B1:$B3` on
A1:A9 lists B5:B7 at A5).

15466.name: ifs_numbers
15466.docs: The values of the `*IFS` target range with the mask from its pairs.

5221.name: map_range
5221.docs: Where a range of the edited sheet goes after a structural edit (`None` = deleted).

14231.name: rows
14231.docs: Indices of data rows that pass the filter.

25784.name: needs_cid
25784.docs: True when `c` has no WinAnsiEncoding byte and is drawn with the CID font.

6602.name: simplex_body
6602.docs: Simplex LP: reduced costs, shadow prices and their ranges from the final tableau.

22006.name: is_py_formula
22006.docs:
Whether `text` (a formula, with or without `=`) is a `PY(` call: such formulas are Python cells,
set with `python.set`.

4059.name: cell_selectable
4059.docs: Whether the cell may be selected: a protected sheet can forbid selecting locked and/or unlocked cells.

18228.name: filter
18228.docs:
Criteria of the table's AutoFilter (column offset within the table → criterion). With
criteria present, hidden data rows are filtered out rather than hidden by hand, which
SUBTOTAL distinguishes.

25930.name: link_page
25930.docs: Adds a link to a location on another page of this document (zero-based page index).

9291.name: current_json
9291.docs:
The current step for the debugger: its path, kind, command, parameters as they would run
now, and the Repeat pass.

354.name: color
354.docs: Shared legacy indexed colours used by XLSX and number-format rendering.

27311.name: needs_file_spelling
27311.docs:
Whether [`expr_to_file`] would change anything in `e`: a LET or LAMBDA (parameter prefixes),
a function with a file prefix, a spill, `@` or trim operator, or a structured reference.

5586.name: Map
5586.docs: A column of the simplex tableau standing for a variable: `x_var = offset + Σ sign·y`.

573.name: Timeout
573.docs: A Python cell ran longer than the time limit.

4424.name: macros
4424.docs:
Macros: typed command lists that run as one undo step. See [`crate::engine::macros`] for the model,
tokens, runner, debugger, recorder and policy. Automate scripts (`automate.*`) are a separate,
older feature with their own storage; these commands neither read nor change it. A recording
keeps the steps a script run ran while it recorded, as the run reported them.

12126.name: edits
12126.docs:
While a macro step runs: the structural edits its command made (the sheet's name, the
edit), so the macro's inputs, output and Repeat ranges follow their cells as formulas do.

15977.name: reference
15977.docs: An argument that came from a cell or range reference.

9583.name: make_room
9583.docs:
Inserts blank cells where the footprint lands (moving what is there down or right), so the
macro writes into empty cells. The block is every written cell's, so a row the macro writes
stays together. A shift that would move one of the macro's inputs is refused: the inputs were
checked and bound where they are, and only the block's columns (or rows) would move.

10891.name: flatten_tabular_values
10891.docs: Tabular form of [`Self::flatten_values`]: the first line also carries the parents' labels.

12199.name: StatusBarStats
12199.docs:
The selection statistics shown on the status bar, set with `view.statusBar`. Excel turns on
Average, Count and Sum by default.

9656.name: MAX_MACRO_NAME
9656.docs: The longest macro or input name, in characters.

7113.name: parse_range
7113.docs:
A range text (`"A1:C9"`, `"Sheet2!A:C"`) resolved against the workbook. Whole rows/columns
are trimmed to the used range.

26368.name: chart_ref_to_file
26368.docs:
A chart reference for `<c:f>`. Excel needs a name qualified there: with a bare `Name` it
draws the whole chart blank, with no repair prompt (observed in Excel for Windows,
Microsoft 365). A workbook-scoped name is written `[0]!Name`, as Excel writes it, a
sheet-scoped one `Sheet!Name`; an undefined name gets `[0]!`, as the file it came from had.

8421.name: versions
8421.docs: Each open workbook's uid and its current version, to see which ones a step changes.

30219.name: NamedStyle
30219.docs: A Style record: the XF it names and its name.

28984.name: workbook_xml
28984.docs: Read the workbook XML selected by the package's root relationships.

11037.name: MAX_AXIS_FIELDS
11037.docs: Most fields in the Rows plus Columns areas.

26441.name: f_xml
26441.docs:
`<cx:f>` for a reference: a new hidden workbook name for it (collected in `names`, written
with the workbook's defined names). A reference along a row says so; otherwise each column
is one level.

8494.name: Deny
8494.docs: Never runs in a macro; the text says why.

9802.name: build
9802.docs:
Paginates sheet `si` far enough to cover row `need_row` and column `need_col` (and at
least the printed area). `None` when the sheet doesn't exist.

24044.name: set_max_change
24044.docs: Sets Maximum Change (its magnitude); a value that isn't finite is ignored.

17650.name: different_odd_even
17650.docs: Different Odd & Even Pages: even-numbered pages use `even_header`/`even_footer`.

25352.name: fill
25352.docs:
Repeat-fill char from `*x` and its byte position in `text`, for the renderer to expand to
the cell width.

7405.name: PROTECTED
7405.docs: Excel's message for an edit of a locked cell on a protected sheet.

const.expr: "The cell or chart you're trying to change is on a protected sheet."

6243.name: reset_model
6243.docs:
`data.solverReset`: Reset All removes the active sheet's model. A model the sheet reads from
workbook-level names (which other sheets may read too) is left in place and masked by an
empty sheet-level `solver_opt`, so no other sheet's model changes.

11402.name: jump
11402.docs: Ctrl+arrow: jump to the edge of the current data region (Excel's End mode).

1157.name: fuel
1157.docs:
Lambda invocations this cell still has left. Every call spends one charge, so a
compact hostile formula (a LAMBDA that calls itself, nested `MAP`s over big arrays)
runs out of work after the same number of calls that a legitimately wide one could
make, instead of an amount of work that squares with array nesting (#2382).

26806.name: iterated_hash
26806.docs: H0 = H(salt ‖ UTF-16LE(password)), then Hn = H(LE32(n - 1) ‖ Hn-1) for `spin` rounds.

14018.name: cell_criterion
14018.docs: One criteria cell as a matcher. Plain text becomes a "begins with" pattern.

7697.name: SeriesOptions
7697.docs: Options for filling a numeric or date series.

15399.name: logicals
15399.docs:
Collects booleans for AND/OR/XOR: references and arrays contribute numbers and booleans
(text and blanks skipped); direct scalars coerce (empty literal = FALSE).

26952.name: AgileDescriptor
26952.docs:
What an Agile descriptor holds: the package's cipher, the password key encryptor with its
three encrypted values (verifier input, verifier hash, package key), and the package's
integrity pair, which Excel always writes and the reader requires.

9005.name: confirm
9005.docs: The step would write over data and the conflict rule is ask: overwriting answers it.

15472.name: if_numbers

5227.name: column_values
5227.docs:
Distinct, non-blank display values of a table column, in first-seen order. Used to populate a
slicer's tiles and to detect "everything selected".

25790.name: finite
25790.docs: True when every value is finite (NaN and infinities are rejected).

6608.name: multiplier_noise
6608.docs:
The rounding noise in the Lagrange multiplier of row `i`, one of the `active` rows whose
multipliers `lambda` solve the normal equations of ∇f = Σ λₖ ∇gₖ over the `free` variables.
Row i's equation gives λᵢ = (Σⱼ gᵢⱼ·dfⱼ − Σ_{k≠i} λₖ·Σⱼ gᵢⱼ·gₖⱼ) / Σⱼ gᵢⱼ²; the difference
gradients are good to about 1E-6 of each component, and the rounding error of a sum scales
with the sum of its terms' sizes, so the noise is 1E-6 of the terms' sizes over the row's
own squared norm. The bound is local to the row: another row enters only through its
coupling term with this one, so a row whose gradient is orthogonal to the others has a bound
from its own gradient alone, and a large component of ∇f that the row's gradient doesn't
touch hides nothing. Nearly parallel active gradients make the normal equations
ill-conditioned and amplify every multiplier's error beyond any bound local to a row; such
multipliers are ill-determined whatever the bound, and they print as computed.

28406.name: items_of
28406.docs: A pivot field's data items (not subtotal or grand-total items).

27244.name: write_equation
27244.docs:
An equation shape (inside the anchor): Office Math with a plain-text fallback when the source
is in the subset OMML covers, else the plain-text box alone. Both carry the source.

28552.name: axis_map
28552.docs: Pivot field → cache field, by the pivot field's position in rows, then columns.

27317.name: from_file
27317.docs: Formula text read from a file → model text (strips prefixes when it parses).

22304.name: last_contiguous_nonempty
22304.docs:
Last row (inclusive) of the maximal contiguous run of non-empty values in `col`, starting
at `from_row` and capped at `cap` (inclusive). `from_row - 1` when `from_row` itself is
empty (or `from_row > cap`), same as a cell-by-cell `value_ref` scan would find, but
without calling `value_ref` once per row: `CellStore::contiguous_value_run` walks each
band's row map directly for the common case (a run of stored cells), only falling back to
a per-row `value_ref` check where the stored run stops short of `cap`. Used by the fill-handle
double-click, where `col` can be densely populated for very long stretches.

9516.name: revision
9516.docs:
The document's revision: the rollback counts as a change, and front ends key their caches
on it, so a check that changed nothing leaves it as it was.

19907.name: store
19907.docs:
Makes this the entry for `src`, with `layout`. A source over the cap is neither copied nor
hashed.

28917.name: cell_code
28917.docs:
What a file formula makes: a Python cell from the Python part when it names a script, or from
string literals ([`PyCode::from_formula`]). `formula` is the parsed formula, `raw` the
formula's own text, which keeps line breaks in literal code.

8427.name: end_stopped
8427.docs:
After Stop Action rolled back the undo groups of the workbook with uid `doc`: ends the
debugger if its run was there. Returns the macro's name and the files the run wrote, which stay.

27682.name: MAX_TOTAL
27682.docs: Largest total decompressed size read from one package.

28990.name: SheetNames
28990.docs: The sheet names an import has assigned so far, for repairing repeated ones.

26447.name: GREY
26447.docs: Light grey for gridlines and the chart border: the text colour at a quarter strength.

9808.name: content_rect
9808.docs: Where the cells of page `(i, j)` go: inside the margins.

25212.name: parse_cache
25212.docs:
A small per-thread cache of parsed format codes for callers that format many values with the
same code (`TEXT` over a range, chart labels). A parsed format depends on the code text only
(the date system and values are applied when formatting), so the code is the whole key.

26520.name: Props
26520.docs: What a control's properties say, from `formControlPr` or VML `x:ClientData`.

12424.name: close_window
12424.docs:
Closes one window. The workbook stays open while it has another window; closing its last
window closes the workbook (unsaved changes are the caller's to ask about).

27828.name: chart_sheet_entries
27828.docs:
The `<sheet>` entries of the workbook that are chart sheets, each with the number of worksheets
(model sheets) before it.

7411.name: same_content
7411.docs:
Two cells hold the same value, formula or Python code (formats aside; a Python cell's result
is not something the person edits).

7484.name: Alternate
7484.docs:
The Ctrl+drag fill: the opposite of a plain drag. A lone number fills a
series stepping by 1; anything a plain drag would extend is copied.

29282.name: iso_datetime
29282.docs:
`2024-05-01T09:30:00` with optional fraction and zone: what `dT` (xsd:dateTime) accepts.
Anything else is left out rather than written into the file.

28047.name: reserve_vml_blocks
28047.docs:
Reserves the VML shape blocks the kept header and footer drawings of `wb` use, so that the
notes drawings GridCraft writes don't reuse their shape ids.

13951.name: split_op
13951.docs: Splits a leading comparison operator (`=` when there is none) off a text criterion.

24269.name: PhoneticProps
24269.docs:
The `<phoneticPr>` of a string item: how its phonetic runs are displayed. `kind` (`type`) and
`alignment` only ever hold values ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.18.57 `ST_PhoneticType` / §18.18.56
`ST_PhoneticAlignment` define, so damaged files cannot be written back invalid.

1309.name: DisplayedPrecision
1309.docs:
Rounds values to their cell's displayed precision, remembering each style's parsed format.
Styles don't change while it is used (one recalculation pass, one sweep of a workbook).

16713.name: check
16713.docs: Whether `latex` parses, without laying it out (cheap enough to run on every keystroke).

24415.name: name
24415.docs: Finds a defined name visible from `sheet`: sheet scope first, then workbook scope.

28266.name: group
28266.docs: (base field, grouping, group item captions); grouping `None` = unsupported grouping.

10319.name: make_item
10319.docs: (identity key, item) for a source value under a field's date grouping.

3925.name: data_range
3925.docs:
The range a data command works on: the selection when it's a block, else the current
region (trimmed to the used range for whole columns).

29574.name: add
29574.docs: Adds a relationship of type `kind` (last segment, e.g. `worksheet`); returns its id.

5233.name: find_slicer
5233.docs: The target slicer: by `slicer` id, else the last one on the active sheet.

16786.name: dynamic
16786.docs:
Read from a file that marks this formula as a dynamic-array formula (cell metadata `cm`).
The writer keeps the mark, so a formula Excel evaluates as an array is never saved as a
legacy formula (which Excel evaluates with implicit intersection). Formulas entered or
rewritten in GridCraft start without it, and the writer decides from their shape.

2690.name: Wedge
2690.docs: Pie/doughnut sector: centre, radii, angles in radians (0 = 12 o'clock, clockwise).

6541.name: Skipped
6541.docs: The reports left out under [`NotOptimal::Skip`], as `{report, reason}`.

21945.name: value
21945.docs: The result as cells (an array spills), or its preview as text when it has no cell form.

220.name: top_left
220.docs:
The top-left cell of a list of areas: the lowest row and the lowest column across all of
them, whatever order they are listed in. Excel writes the relative formulas of a
multi-area validation or conditional format for this cell. `None` for no areas.

4071.name: coalesce
4071.docs: Merges cells into vertical runs per column (a compact multi-area selection).

15624.name: moments
15624.docs: (sum of cross deviations, devsq x, devsq y, mean x, mean y).

293.name: unquote_sheet
293.docs:
The inverse of [`quote_sheet`]: takes the quotes off a sheet name and reads `''` as `'`.
Text that isn't quoted is returned as it is.

4144.name: denied_script_step
4144.docs:
Why a script step is refused, whatever the workbook's trust: scripts stay inside the
workbook. Anything that reads or writes files (`file.*`, or any `path` parameter: Get Data,
From Text/CSV, Insert Picture) or leaves the app (`link.*` opens URLs) is the caller's to run
directly, not a stored script's. (Nested `automate.*` steps are skipped.) This check goes by
command id and parameter name, so it is only the up-front refusal: the steps also run inside
an [`crate::engine::io::ScriptSandbox`] (file access refused whatever the parameter is called) and
[`run_script`] drops any `OpenUrl` request a step raises.

25942.name: text
25942.docs: Text with its baseline starting at `(x, y)`.

27323.name: dummy_function_inner
27323.docs:
The original formula inside Google Sheets' export wrapper
`IFERROR(__xludf.DUMMYFUNCTION("<formula, quotes doubled>"),<cached value>)`, if `e` is that
wrapper, the text parses and every function it calls is `known`. The parser has already undone
the doubled quotes. The cached value is also the cell's `<v>`, which the reader keeps.

31174.name: write_xlsx_as
31174.docs: Writes a workbook as the given member of the `.xlsx` family.

22310.name: set_picture
22310.docs: Pictures retain a scalar fallback for calculation and unsupported consumers.

30012.name: MAX_DEPTH
30012.docs:
Expression nesting at most, as in the formula parser: deeper trees would overflow the stack
when printed, evaluated or dropped (a hostile file can chain thousands of PtgParen tokens).

22383.name: lines
22383.docs: (line, start position of that line, its size), sorted by line.

4436.name: start_recording
4436.docs:
